title: Vox-Style Editorial Collage Design System
text: For serious explainer topics, use a textured cream grid canvas (`#D8D6D0`, 40px grid) paired with monochrome photo cutouts offset by solid terracotta silhouette shadows (`#CA4D2D`, offset X:-18px, Y:-14px). Emphasize key evidence using animated golden-yellow highlighter sweeps (`#EFBC22` with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` scaling X:0 to 1) and numeric odometer counters rolling via GSAP `onUpdate`.
how: Incorporate these CSS styles and helper animations into `compose_lab.py` for Kaise Tech AI/tech investigations and historical explainers on Aage Suno.

title: Shot-Scale Jump Contrast Rule
text: Avoid imperceptible 2-3% continuous camera drifts that feel like static presentation slides. Motivated zooming must execute true shot-scale transitions: switch between establishing wide shots (subject occupying ~35% of frame height) and medium close-ups or close-ups (subject occupying 55-65% frame height, zoom factor >= 1.08), followed by a 0.5s hold per voiceover beat.
how: Update visual instructions in `plan.py` and camera tween presets in `compose_lab.py` to use discrete focal scale steps rather than faint background drift.

title: Timeline-Mined SFX Cue Generation
text: Instead of manually scripting audio cues, inspect the GSAP master timeline (`window.__timelines['main']`) in headless Chrome, classify tweens into sound families based on property changes (camera moves to whoosh, entrance to impact, text reveal to paper/click), and output frame-snapped cue timestamps. Then mix stem layers and mux onto the final MP4 using `ffmpeg -c:v copy` without re-rendering video frames.
how: Upgrade `mix.py`: replace manual SFX cue estimation by running a headless timeline query on the HyperFrames composition to extract exact animation hits, generating stem audio prior to ffmpeg muxing.

title: Mechanical Anti-Slide Preflight Audit
text: Enforce automated layout linting before rendering: reject compositions if >= 3 sequential scenes simply toggle opacity/autoAlpha on static sections, enforce a maximum 2-tier text hierarchy per scene (headline + diegetic label), and flag camera scale changes under 5% as imperceptible Ken Burns drift. Ensure an anchor subject persists across >= 60% of runtime.
how: Add AST/DOM regex checks into `preflight.py` to inspect generated HyperFrames HTML before passing it to Puppeteer, automatically rejecting slide-like scene hierarchies.

title: SVG Joint Proxy Transform Wrapper
text: GSAP `transformOrigin` on SVG elements dynamically recalculates based on dynamic bounding boxes, causing rotating joints (limbs, needles, dials) to tear apart during motion. Resolve this using a lightweight transform proxy object `J(el, tx, ty)` that writes explicit `translate() rotate() scale()` attribute strings during GSAP `onUpdate` without directly tweening SVG container coordinates.
how: Add the `J()` transform proxy helper to our base HyperFrames script template for animated props, dials, and future character rigging in Puraan Ki Katha.

title: Subtler Asymmetric Exit Rule
text: Exit animations must never mirror enter amplitude. Because viewer attention moves ahead to the next scene, exit tweens should use 40-60% smaller travel distance and faster duration than enters (e.g., enter: translateY 20px -> 0 over 400ms; exit: translateY 0 -> -8px over 250ms with 4px blur). Symmetrical exits distract from incoming focal subjects.
how: In `compose_lab.py` and `compose.py`, adjust all GSAP exit tweens for stat counters, clue cards, and HUD overlays to cut travel distance in half.

title: Text Reading Hold Duration Formula
text: Calculate required static hold durations for kinetic titles, cards, and text overlays using `duration = (word_count * 0.3s) + 0.5s` settle time. At 30 fps, a 3-word title needs at least 1.4s (42 frames) hold before transition or exit. Prevents visual cards and sentence highlights from disappearing before viewers can read them.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, enforce this formula when generating GSAP timeline hold durations for sentence captions and kinetic titles against TTS voice timings.

title: Materializing Blur-Translate Enter Preset
text: Replace harsh fade-ins or slide-ins with Jakub's materializing entrance: simultaneously animate `opacity: 0 -> 1`, `translateY: 8px -> 0px`, and `filter: blur(4px) -> blur(0px)` using a crisp ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) or zero-bounce spring over 300-450ms. Blur simulates depth and optical focus, giving UI props physical arrival on dark canvas.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, upgrade entrance tweens for UI panels, chat bubbles, stat counters, and comparison cards to include the `blur(4px)` to `blur(0px)` transition.

title: Ease-In Cut-On-Beat Scene Transition
text: When transitioning into a cut or musical downbeat, never let the outgoing motion settle with ease-out. If a card or camera push transitions across a cut, use ease-in (`cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)`) so the cut lands at maximum velocity on or 1 frame before the downbeat, sustaining scene energy.
how: In `compose.py` and `compose_lab.py`, set outgoing push/pan tweens to ease-in (`power2.in`), aligning cut frame timestamps with downbeats detected in `mix.py`.

title: Non-Zero Scale Inception Guard
text: Never animate element scales starting from `scale(0)`. Starting an entrance from zero volume distorts visual aspect ratios and reads like an unnatural balloon inflating. Initialize entering badges, UI cards, and icon pops at `scale: 0.9` with `opacity: 0` before tweening to `scale: 1.0`.
how: In `compose_lab.py` and `preflight.py`, update and audit all GSAP pop-in tweens to clamp initial scale values to minimum `0.90`.

title: Windowed Latin Prompting for Hinglish Word Alignment
text: Whisper frequently hallucinates Devanagari or corrupts Romanized Hinglish phonetic spellings. Segment the planned Hinglish voice script into short time windows and pass the exact expected Romanized text as Whisper's initial_prompt (`--prompts`). This forces Whisper to preserve the intended Latin alphabet spelling (e.g., 'bhai', 'accha', 'jugaad') while producing precise millisecond-level word timestamps for kinetic light-up captions.
how: In `pace.py`, supply the generated Roman Hinglish script chunks into Whisper alignment as windowed prompts, ensuring 100% spelling fidelity for caption highlights in `compose_lab.py`.

title: India Shorts Trend Audio Scraper & Dual Master Export
text: Query YouTube Top Shorts India, Spotify India, and JioSaavn charts weekly to surface trending sounds. Never bake commercial trending music into exports due to Content ID copyright penalties. Instead, render two deliverables: a licensed-bed master, and an identical '_clean' video with music muted, providing metadata with the trending song title, artist, and start offset for in-app audio attachment.
how: Add a chart scraper script called by `scout.py`. In `compose.py` and `mix.py`, generate both standard and music-stripped `_clean` MP4s ready for platform trend tagging.

title: Multi-Check Pre-Delivery QA Matrix
text: Automate pre-delivery verification through programmatic ffmpeg checks: detect frozen video stretches (>1.5s identical frames via freezedetect), black frames at scene boundaries, WCAG flash safety violations (>3 flashes/sec or saturated red strobes), audio mono-fold phase cancellation, and empty or black frame 0. Block automated posting if any hard error is detected.
how: Expand `review.py` after rendering to run `freezedetect`, `blackdetect`, and first-frame validation before triggering Telegram approval in `publish.py`.

title: CSS 3D Perspective Rig for Prop and Panel Staging
text: Wrap composition scenes in container styling with perspective: 1000px and transform-style: preserve-3d, then animate elements along Z, rotateY, and rotateX (e.g., from z: -500, rotateY: 30, opacity: 0 with power3.out). This produces genuine 3D camera depth for floating cards and UI props without WebGL or Three.js dependencies.
how: In compose_lab.py, wrap UI panels and prop scene containers in .camera-container. Update GSAP scene timelines to animate rotateX/rotateY and z translations during entry transitions.

title: Scramble-Decode Headline Text Generator
text: Animate tech keyword reveals by iterating over string characters and cycling random glyphs (A-Z, 0-9, @#$%&*) at 30ms intervals across unresolved positions over 1.0 to 1.5 seconds until settling on the target text. Creates an authentic AI/decryption aesthetic for hook titles that outperforms standard terminal typing.
how: Embed the scrambleText helper in compose_lab.py HTML templates and invoke it for the primary hook keyword during the first 2 seconds of Kaise Tech explainers.

title: Dual-Layer CSS Chromatic Glitch Impact
text: Generate chromatic aberration without image filters by applying ::before and ::after pseudo-elements referencing content: attr(data-text). Shift the red channel -2px to -5px and cyan channel +2px to +5px while animating horizontal clip-path slices (e.g., inset(20% 0 80% 0)) during 0.3s impact hits.
how: Add .chromatic and .glitch-text CSS classes into compose_lab.py; tag high-energy hook titles or transition cards to receive the data-text attribute.

title: Subzone Graphic Intrusion Gate
text: To guarantee caption legibility in 9:16 vertical shorts (1080x1920), layout containers enforce a bottom safe margin of 490–570px (caption zone at y=1400–1520). Post-render audit extracts frames and measures high-contrast edge gradients (>24 pixel delta) inside the caption strip. Any non-caption visual card, chart, or prop entering the zone during speech triggers a layout collision reject.
how: Enforce a bottom safe container in compose_lab.py CSS, and add a numpy pixel-variance check over y=1400:1520 in review.py during voiced segments.

title: Bar-Spliced Pre-Drop Silent Stops
text: When arranging music for explainer drops, slice music tracks exclusively on 4-beat bar boundaries with 25 ms crossfades. Leave an empty gap of exactly 2 to 4 beats (half to full bar) immediately preceding high-energy drop sections. Place a standalone vocal shout line ('Look at this', 'Let's go') inside this silent window to maximize acoustic contrast.
how: Apply in `plan.py` and `mix.py`: insert a 2-beat silent stop right before major feature reveals and position the scene's kicker vocal inside that window.

title: Bake Complex CSS Gradients and Noise into PNG Tiles
text: Exceeding ~40 active DOM elements with live `radial-gradient`, CSS `filter: blur()`, or SVG `clip-path` causes headless Chromium/HyperFrames renderers to drop frames or render solid black rectangles. Replace procedural Ben-Day dots, noise grain, vignettes, and paper distress layers with static repeating PNG tiles using `background-image` or CSS `mask-image`.
how: Audit `compose_lab.py` and HTML templates; replace inline SVG noise filters and multiple layered CSS radial gradients with cached local PNG textures.

title: GSAP On-Twos Stepped Easing Quantizer
text: Emulate comic and hand-drawn stop-motion animation within GSAP timelines by quantizing continuous easing curves into 12 discrete steps per second: `on2(duration, baseEase) => gsap.parseEase(`steps(${Math.round(duration * 12)})`)`. Apply `on2` to character, UI card, and prop reveals while keeping camera pans, background drifts, and gradient fades continuous and smooth.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, add the `on2` helper to the template JavaScript header and wrap pop/slam animations during comic or lab tech callouts.

title: Dual-Band Beat-Grid and Kick Energy Fitter
text: Extract audio tempo and phase without Librosa using ffmpeg dual-stream decoding (full-band + 150 Hz low-pass) into numpy arrays. Compute RMS onset envelopes across 128-hop frames at 11 kHz and search candidate BPMs (100–130 at 0.02 step) and phase offsets (4 ms steps). Classify downbeats exceeding the 70th percentile low-band threshold as kick beats ('K') for visual triggering.
how: Build `beat_grid.py` using scipy/numpy; run on background music before `compose_lab.py` to populate beat timestamps (`B(n)`) and kick arrays for automated cut synchronization.

title: Speech-to-Music Stem Mix Balance Verification
text: Measure sidechain ducking levels by comparing isolated voice and music stems decoded at 8 kHz mono. Compute RMS dB separately for speech-active frames (`speech & body`) and silent pauses (`body & ~speech`). Enforce target balance: music must sit 4–6 dB below voice during speech and rise to voice level during pauses. Flag any ducking deeper than 8 dB as silent music defect.
how: Add `measure_mix_balance()` to `mix.py` or `review.py`. Generate temp stem WAVs before final loudnorm and abort render if ducking delta exceeds 7 dB.

title: Non-Semantic Audio-Reactive Mapping
text: When mapping audio features (RMS, Centroid, Onsets) to visual properties, avoid 'semantic overclaims' (e.g., assuming high frequency equals 'happiness'). Instead, use bounded, normalized, and smoothed mappings: RMS to scale, Onsets to opacity/flash, and Spectral Centroid to color-shift. Always provide a neutral fallback for silent segments to prevent visual 'jitter'.
how: Update 'mix.py' to export a normalized feature JSON. Update 'compose_lab.py' to use these values for property multipliers in GSAP animations.

title: Volatile Fact Verification Dating
text: API pricing, model IDs, and duration limits are 'volatile facts'. Every entry in our knowledge base must include a 'verified_on' date. If a fact is older than 30 days, the system must trigger a 'scout.py' check or warn the editor. This prevents using EOL models (like Nova Reel v1.0) or hitting stale pricing assumptions.
how: Update 'brain.jsonl' schema to require a 'verified_at' timestamp. Add a pre-flight check in 'doctor.py' to flag expired facts.

title: 2D Rig Viseme Inventory Rule
text: For future avatar work, do not use a fixed viseme count. Inventory must depend on the target language (Hinglish vs English). Ensure critical closures (M, B, P) are preserved. Use 'replacement' for hands/mouth poses to avoid 'volume collapse' seen in simple deformation/warping.
how: Add these rules to 'playbook.md' under a new 'Avatar' section to guide future development of 'compose_avatar.py'.

title: Precise Video Description (5-Aspect Rule)
text: When 'scout.py' or 'research.py' analyzes videos, it must use five distinct aspects: Subject, Scene, Motion, Spatial, and Camera. This prevents mixing 'creative intent' with 'literal observation'. For example, distinguish between 'subject-left' and 'frame-left' to ensure the AI-generated visuals match the script's spatial logic.
how: Update the system prompt in 'research.py' to enforce this 5-aspect structure for all visual analysis tasks.

title: Instruction-Guided TTS Performance
text: When using models like GPT-4o-audio, use 'instructions' for exact pronunciation of brand names (e.g., 'QuantaForge, pronounced KWON-tuh forge') and acting cues (e.g., 'conspiratorial and quieter'). Do not rely on phonetic spelling alone; use the 'instruction' field to set the 'warmth' or 'hype' level.

title: LLM Reasoning Evaluation (EVAL.md Pattern)
text: Implement a 'Reasoning Gate' using the repo's EVAL.md structure. Before any generation, the LLM must pass a 5-question quiz about the target model's constraints (e.g., 'What is the max duration for Kling lip-sync?', 'Does this model support SSML?'). If it fails, the job is blocked. This prevents 'hallucinated' parameters that lead to failed API calls or poor quality.
how: Add a 'reasoning_gate.py' step after 'plan.py'. It will generate a quiz based on the selected provider's constraints and verify the LLM's answers against our shared brain before allowing 'compose.py' to run.

title: D3.js Animated Data Visualization
text: Move beyond simple stat counters to full D3.js charts rendered to MP4. Use deterministic frame-based rendering (frame/fps) instead of wall-clock transitions to ensure every frame is identical across distributed renders. Requires frozen scales, fonts, and data joins to prevent 'morphing' errors where unrelated categories blend during sorts.
how: Create 'compose_data.py' using a headless browser to render D3.js templates. Integrate with 'HyperFrames' by passing a 'frame' variable to the D3 interpolators for perfect sync.

title: Lottie Vector Animation Integration
text: Use dotLottie/Lottie for high-quality, scalable vector overlays (icons, UI elements) instead of pre-rendered video clips. Use 'goToAndStop' frame-seeking for deterministic capture at 30fps. This reduces asset size and allows for dynamic color/text changes in 'Kaise Tech' explainers without re-rendering the base asset.
how: Add a Lottie handler to 'HyperFrames'. The renderer will use puppeteer to seek to specific frames of a .lottie file for each video frame, ensuring perfect sync with the voiceover.

title: Three.js Deterministic 3D Props
text: Upgrade 'lab look' props from 2D images to 3D glTF models. Use Three.js with a fixed camera orbit and absolute-time animation (frame/fps). Ensure non-color data (normal, roughness) is not marked as sRGB to prevent 'washed out' textures. Dispose of GPU resources (geometries, textures) after every render to prevent memory leaks in long runs.
how: Create 'compose_3d.py'. It will load a .glb asset, set up a standard 'lab' lighting rig, and render a sequence of PNGs based on the 'plan.py' camera directions.

title: Automated Screen Demo Capture
text: For 'Kaise Tech' tutorials, use Playwright to capture authentic UI interactions. Avoid 'fixed sleeps'; instead, use 'assert observable state' (wait for element). Distinguish between 'authentic' (real UI) and 'illustrative' (mocked UI) and disclose accordingly. Capture at 2x scale for 'Kaise Tech' zoom-ins to maintain text readability.

title: 120 BPM Structural Grid
text: Standardize all video pacing on a 120 BPM grid (0.5s per beat). Structural events like slams, landings, and cuts must land on beats or 16ths (0.125s). Repeated units (like story 'asks' or scenes) should use a whole number of beats (e.g., 11 beats/5.5s) to prevent the visual rhythm from drifting away from the music over time.
how: Update plan.py to snap scene durations and key events to 0.125s increments. Instruct Gemini in the style prompt to think in 'beats' for pacing.

title: FLIP Object Continuity
text: Use the FLIP (First, Last, Invert, Play) principle for transitions. An element (like an avatar or card) should fly to the exact rect of its counterpart in the next scene. The receiving scene takes over on the landing frame. This 'continuity over cuts' approach makes automated edits feel like high-end custom motion graphics.
how: Apply this in plan.py by identifying 'carrier' objects that persist across scenes and ensuring their end-rect in Scene 1 matches the start-rect in Scene 2.

title: Shared Timing Spine (layout.js)
text: Centralize all timestamps, shared geometry (rects), and content strings into a single 'spine' file (assets/lib/layout.js). Every composition and the audio engine import this file. This ensures that when a UI card moves, the sound effect and the next scene's handoff rect are perfectly aligned without hard-coding values in multiple places.
how: Modify plan.py to output a layout.js file instead of just a text plan. Update compose.py and mix.py to import this JS file as the single source of truth for timing.

title: Spine-Driven Procedural Scoring
text: Replace static music beds with a procedural audio engine (using seeded noise/oscillators) that synthesizes a score based on the layout spine. This allows for 'signature motifs' for characters and 'marks' (whooshes, clicks, hits) to be generated exactly on the frame where the visual event occurs, normalized to -16 LUFS.

title: CSS 3D Head-on Stage
text: Implement a CSS-3D world using perspective (e.g., 1100px) where UI cards always face the camera (no rotation). Depth is achieved via camera dolly (z-axis), parallax, and focus pulls. This 'head-on' rule ensures text remains readable while providing a premium 3D feel. Use a 'follow cam' with Hann-smoothed look-ahead for tracking moving elements.

title: Mathematical Character Rigging
text: Convert static mascot rasters into rigged SVG modules. Use marching squares for tracing, Douglas-Peucker for simplification, and Catmull-Rom splines for smoothing. Create 'rigs' as pure functions of time for nodding, blinking, and 'thinking' (flickering points via sine waves). This allows faceless characters to react to the script without manual animation.

title: Dual-Side Transition Snapshots
text: Improve the visual audit by capturing snapshots exactly one frame before and one frame after every transition/handoff. Compare these frames to ensure 'pixel-identical' handoffs where an object in Scene A perfectly matches its position in Scene B. This eliminates 'jumps' or 'stray frames' during complex transitions.

title: LLMS.txt Verbatim Extraction
text: Prioritize 'llms.txt' or 'llms-full.txt' files when researching tech products. These files provide clean, verbatim technical truths (API endpoints, feature names) without DOM clutter. Ensure every on-screen claim is traced to a specific URL in RESEARCH.md to prevent AI hallucinations in explainers.

title: Reference Energy Mapping
text: Analyze reference videos for a 'stillness ratio' (target >25% dead-still) and 'bursts' (>=3 changes in 1.5s). Use a character-based energy map ( .:-=+*#%@) to visualize motion density and ensure the edit 'breathes'.

title: Rhythm Variance Rule
text: Ensure shot lengths vary by at least 4x (e.g., 0.25s words next to 2.5s holds). The Coefficient of Variation (CV) for shot lengths should be >= 0.25 to avoid a 'metronome' or 'slideshow' feel.
how: Add a validation step in plan.py to calculate the CV of the generated scene durations. If CV < 0.25, re-prompt Gemini to vary the pacing.

title: Camera Air & Depth SFX
text: Generate 'air' noise (band-passed 150Hz-9kHz) scaled by camera velocity (|d log zoom / dt|^1.3). Closer zoom = brighter noise. Adds physical presence to digital camera moves.
how: In mix.py, generate a procedural noise track based on the camera's zoom velocity exported from the animation metadata.

title: Continuity Carry Oracle
text: Measure 'carry score' at scene boundaries. A boundary is 'carried' if an element survives and moves >2% diagonal or scales >10%. Reject videos with score <0.5. Prevents 'slideshow' feel where scenes just replace each other.
how: Add a 'carry check' to preflight.py. Use the GSAP timeline to verify at least one object ID persists across scene transitions with significant transform changes.

title: UI Replica System
text: Instead of screen recordings, rebuild UI in HTML/CSS. This allows infinite zoom without pixelation, instant language swapping via string tables, and programmatic control of every state (hover, click, active).
how: Upgrade compose_lab.py to generate HTML components for 'tech explainers' rather than using static images. Use a 'stage' helper to manage scaling and crispness at high zooms.

title: Shutter-Based Motion Blur
text: Render moving frames by averaging multiple sub-frame captures (4-48 samples) across a 180-degree shutter. Essential for moves >80px/frame to prevent strobing. Only apply to 'moving' frames to save render time.
how: Modify the rendering loop in compose.py to take multiple screenshots per frame during high-velocity GSAP segments and blend them using ffmpeg or canvas globalAlpha.

title: Event-Driven SFX Scoring
text: Export an __events() JSON from the animation containing exact timestamps, pans (screen X), and impact strengths. Use this to drive score.py to place foley (clicks, whooshes, thuds) with sub-millisecond precision.
how: Update compose.py to emit a JSON of GSAP 'onStart' events. Feed this to mix.py to automate SFX placement instead of relying on manual timeline mining.

title: Screen-Space Camera Rig
text: A camera rig that chases the subject's screen position and log-zoom, not world position. This ensures that a 'landing' or 'zoom' feels identical whether the subject is at 1x or 300x scale.
how: Implement a 'rig' function in layout.js that calculates CSS transforms based on a target element's desired screen-center coordinates rather than absolute offsets.

title: Language Time-Warping
text: Map animation beats to specific words in different languages using 'knots' [filmT, authorT]. Allows the same visual composition to sync perfectly with English and Hinglish VO even when sentence lengths differ.
how: In plan.py, anchor visual 'hits' to specific words in the script. Use a time-warping function in compose.py to adjust the GSAP timeline speed based on TTS word timings.

title: Three-Tier Style Variation Constraint Hierarchy
text: When generating new visual variations or channel sub-themes, split aesthetic parameters into three strict tiers: 1. Safe to tweak (palette hexes, fonts, speech pace, SFX accents); 2. Character-altering (shading/materials, contrast logic, camera grammar); 3. Invariant essence (core visual medium, e.g. mono terminal HUD vs isometric cutaway). Never allow prompt variations to alter Tier 3, and cap Tier 2 modifications to maximum 2 changes per iteration to prevent visual degradation.
how: Add the constraint tiers to plan.py and compose_lab.py theme configurations, ensuring AI prompt overrides only modify Tier 1 variables unless explicitly defining a new channel sub-brand.

title: Narrative Arc Echo Rule (Setup-Turn-Echo)
text: Every 30–60 s explainer script must follow a strict three-phase spine: one subject with one goal, exactly one pivotal turn, and an echo ending. The ending must bookend the opening hook (revisiting the initial hook image with transformed perspective, scale reveal, or flipped outcome). Secondary subplots and multi-pivot twists must be cut.
how: Update plan.py prompt schema to require an `echo_hook` field linking the final scene's visual and thematic payoff directly back to scene 1.

title: Cross-Scene J-Cut and L-Cut Sound Transitions
text: Implement at least two audio-led transitions per video using sound overlap. A J-cut brings the upcoming scene's foley or ambient sound in 0.3–0.5 s prior to the visual cut; an L-cut sustains outgoing foley or reverb tails 0.3–0.5 s past the cut over the incoming scene.
how: In mix.py and plan.py timeline cues, add audio offset timing allowing incoming scene SFX or ambience beds to trigger before visual scene cut points.

title: Small-Speaker Harmonic Bass Mastering
text: Mobile phone speakers cannot reproduce sub-bass (20–120 Hz), causing synth bass to disappear or distort. Balance low-end energy by keeping 20–120 Hz at −3 dB relative to mids, omit chord and pad notes below MIDI note 48 (C3), and enrich basslines with 2nd and 3rd harmonics so mobile speakers clearly project perceived pitch.
how: In `mix.py`, add a harmonic saturation pass to the music bed pipeline and high-pass or tame sub-48 Hz synths before final LUFS normalization.

title: Spelled-Out TTS with Digitized Captions
text: TTS engines frequently misread or inconsistently vocalize raw numbers, acronyms, and dates, whereas viewers process digits 3x faster than written words. Always generate two parallel streams: spell numbers phonetically in the spoken script for TTS (e.g., 'ten thousand dollars', 'nineteen eighty four'), but encode them as digits ('$10,000', '1984') in the on-screen captions.
how: In `plan.py`, split output scenes into `spoken_text` (spelled-out phonetic words for Gemini TTS) and `display_text` (formatted numerals for HyperFrames captions).

title: FFmpeg Post-Render Grain Injection
text: Rendering film grain dynamically in HTML/Canvas causes every browser screenshot to be noisy and incompressible, drastically slowing headless capture. Instead, render clean frames in headless Chrome and inject procedural grain during the FFmpeg muxing pass (`-vf noise=alls=...:allf=t`). When encoding grain, pass `-tune grain` with an adjusted CRF to preserve texture without macroblocking.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, remove in-browser CSS/SVG noise overlays. In the final mux script, inject procedural grain via FFmpeg video filters right before LUFS mastering.

title: Google Fonts Query-Text Dynamic Subsetting
text: Non-Latin fonts (such as Devanagari for Hindi explainers) are large (10–30 MB), causing headless browser latency and layout shifts. Query Google Fonts CSS API using `&text=<URL_ENCODED_CHARACTERS>` containing only the unique glyphs appearing in the script. Download the resulting ultra-compact WOFF2/TTF (<50 KB) locally and load via `@font-face`.
how: In the new Devanagari caption pipeline, extract distinct script characters, curl the tailored font subset via Google Fonts API, and link locally in HyperFrames HTML.

title: AAC Inter-Sample Peak Stepback Loop
text: Lossy AAC encoding frequently creates inter-sample true-peak overshoots even when the source WAV is limited to -1.2 dBTP. After muxing, measure the audio stream with ebur128. If true peak exceeds -1.0 dBTP, re-encode only the audio track (-c:v copy) with a progressively lower limiter ceiling (stepping down 0.4 dB) up to 3 times until true peak <= -1.0 dBTP.
how: In mix.py or mux stage: add post-mux ebur128 true-peak check; if peak > -1 dBTP, re-transcode audio with lower ceiling while copying video.

title: Headless SwiftShader ANGLE Fallback
text: Virtualized cloud VMs often drop headless WebGL contexts silently after initialization, producing blank or corrupt frames. Launch Chromium with the ANGLE backend set explicitly to SwiftShader (--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader or LEMO_ANGLE=swiftshader) in server/CI environments to guarantee deterministic software rasterization without requiring physical GPU pass-through.
how: In the headless browser launcher for HyperFrames rendering, inject '--use-gl=angle', '--use-angle=swiftshader' when running in server/Docker mode.

title: Style-Specific Instrument Palettes
text: Use the source's 'Picking instruments by style' matrix to define channel-specific audio identities. For 'Puraan Ki Katha', use the 'Chinese/Folk' palette (guqin, pipa, erhu) as substitutes for Indian strings. For 'Kaise Tech', use the 'Cold/Sci-fi' palette (bowed vibraphone, glass, suspended cymbal rolls).
how: Update `knowledge/brain.jsonl` with specific instrument combinations for each channel to guide the music generation step in `plan.py`.

title: Authentic String Slide Modeling (Yin-Nao)
text: Use the physical modeling parameters `bend` (piecewise-linear pitch) and `vib` (frequency/depth) to simulate realistic finger slides and vibrato. This is essential for the 'folk' feel in mythology videos where static notes sound robotic.
how: When generating scores for 'Puraan Ki Katha', the planner should include `bend` arrays in the event dicts passed to the pluck engine.

title: Velocity-Based Timbre Darkening
text: For single-layer instruments, apply a low-pass filter that scales with velocity (`fc = 18000 * (vel / 0.8) ** 2.2`). Real instruments are naturally darker/warmer when played softly; this prevents 'toy-like' audio when lowering volume.
how: Apply this mathematical filter in `mix.py` whenever an audio asset's gain is reduced below 0.8.

title: Procedural Instrument Scoring Engine
text: Integrate the `sampler.py` and `pluck.py` logic to generate original, royalty-free background scores. It uses a 'score' format: `(time, instrument, pitch, duration, velocity, pan)`. This allows the script planner to request specific melodies or motifs rather than just looping static music beds.
how: Add `sampler.py` and `pluck.py` to `core/audio/`. Modify `mix.py` to accept a 'score' list from `plan.py` and render it into the final mixdown before mastering.

title: Cross-Faded Long-Note Extension
text: Implement the `_extend` function logic which uses cross-correlation at the fundamental period to splice grains of audio. This prevents the 'hum' or periodicity of simple loops when extending short instrument samples into long background pads.
how: In `mix.py`, replace simple audio looping with this grain-splicing logic for background textures and atmospheric pads.

title: Just-In-Time Audio Asset Fetcher
text: Implement the `ensure()` and `fetch.sh` logic to download only the required sample libraries (VSCO, VCSL, etc.) when a specific instrument is called. This keeps the main repo small while allowing access to GBs of high-quality audio samples.
how: Create a `tools/fetch.sh` and integrate the `ensure()` check into the audio render start. This allows the studio to scale to 100+ instruments without bloating the server disk.

title: Automated Music Credit Attribution
text: Use a registry-based credit generator like `S.credits()`. It tracks which instruments were actually used in a render and outputs the exact CC-BY license strings required for the description or end-card.
how: Add a `credits` method to the audio pipeline that appends the required text to the `results.md` or the video's description metadata during `publish.py`.

title: NumPy Procedural Foley & UI SFX Synthesis
text: Generate crisp, license-free UI SFX procedurally using NumPy/SciPy without external audio asset libraries. Implements math-modeled sounds: plastic clicks (2.5 kHz high-pass noise burst + dual sines at 2.9 kHz and 4.6 kHz), whooshes (swept bandpass 600 Hz–3.2 kHz noise with sin² amplitude envelope), thumps (70 Hz decaying sine + 300 Hz lowpass burst), and radio walkie-talkie distortion (380–2800 Hz bandpass + tanh saturation).
how: Add `sfx_synth.py` alongside `mix.py` to synthesize transition whooshes, UI clicks, and pop effects directly into the audio mix buffer based on animation cue timestamps.

title: Capture-Phase WebGL Context Loss Sentinel
text: Virtual GPUs and CI runners frequently drop WebGL contexts silently after initialization or when exceeding 16 active contexts, resulting in completely blank frames while Playwright exits with success code 0. Injecting an init script that traps `webglcontextlost` during the capture phase (`addEventListener('webglcontextlost', ..., true)`) records the lost canvas ID to `window.__glLost`.
how: Add the context-loss listener init script to Playwright browser launching in `preflight.py` and `compose_lab.py`, halting frame capture immediately if `window.__glLost` is detected.

title: Boundary-Padded Whisper ASR Verification
text: Short voice clips (<1.5 s) frequently trigger Whisper hallucinations or truncated transcriptions due to attention window edge effects. Prepending and appending exactly 0.6 s of silence before running Whisper, then subtracting 0.6 s from the generated word timestamps, stabilizes recognition. ASR comparisons then enforce a zero-tolerance policy on spoken numbers even if overall difflib similarity exceeds 0.92.
how: Implement in the voice gate right after Gemini TTS: pad audio with 0.6 s silence, run `faster-whisper` for word-level validation, and reject clips with number discrepancies.

title: NTSC Horizontal Chroma-Bleed Shader Pass
text: Achieve high-end tech/lab visual styling by emulating NTSC analog video transmission via WebGL2 shaders. The fragment shader converts RGB to YCbCr, maintains sharp luminance, horizontally averages Cb across 7 pixels, and shifts Cr rightward by 2 pixels. It then overlays a 3-pixel RGB vertical subpixel grille and luma-modulated scanlines.
how: Include this shader pass in `compose_lab.py` as an optional fullscreen post-processing canvas filter for technical, terminal, or retro explainer scenes.

title: Dynamic Silence Trimming Thresholds
text: Trim leading/trailing silence by finding samples > 2% of peak volume. Keep a 0.03s lead-in and a 0.08s to 0.10s tail to prevent cutting off the natural 'ring' or decay of the final word.
how: Update pace.py to use the 2% peak threshold and specific 30ms/100ms padding instead of simple zero-crossing or fixed duration cuts.

title: Audio Plausibility Gate
text: A generated audio clip is only valid if it is >= 0.15s long and has a max amplitude > 1e-3. This catches 'successful' API calls that return silent or empty files.
how: Add these checks to the existing voice gate logic immediately after TTS generation and before pace.py.

title: Themed Style Expansion
text: Expand 'lab look' and 'classic look' into specific sub-styles found in the manifest: Ukiyo-e, Satellite Briefing, Thermal Camera, Risograph, and Blueprint.
how: Use the style names as keywords in our image generation prompts (Muse/FLUX) to create more distinct visual identities for different series.

title: Hinglish Phoneme Guard
text: Explicitly check for CJK characters in English-tagged TTS lines. If found, the engine will produce noise. This logic can be adapted to ensure Devanagari doesn't leak into English TTS calls.
how: In plan.py or voice.py, add a regex check to ensure the script language matches the TTS engine's expected character set.

title: Kokoro Offline TTS Integration
text: Integrate Kokoro-82M (ONNX) for high-quality offline voice generation. It uses espeak-ng for phonemes and provides a faster, local alternative to Gemini TTS credits.
how: Add a new provider in voice.py using kokoro-onnx. Use the logic in tts.py to handle the 160-byte espeak-ng path limit by symlinking to ~/.cache.

title: SHA1 Param-Based Audio Caching
text: Cache TTS results using a 16-character SHA1 hash of the combined voice, rate, pitch, and text. Use a '.part' suffix during download/generation to prevent corrupted cache hits from interrupted jobs.
how: Modify Gemini TTS calls to check a local .cache/ folder first using this hashing strategy before hitting the API.

title: Dependency Checksum Sentinel
text: Track environment health by storing a checksum (cksum) of requirements.txt and package.json in a hidden marker file (.lemo-ok). Trigger reinstalls only when the marker doesn't match.
how: Integrate into doctor.py to detect when a git pull has changed dependencies, preventing 'module not found' errors during automated runs.

title: Fixed-Coordinate Parent Transform Prohibition
text: Never apply CSS transforms (translate, scale, matrix) or CSS filters to a parent container that houses position: fixed or viewport-anchored HUD elements. Under the CSS spec, any non-none transform establishes a new containing block, trapping fixed children and causing abrupt coordinate snapping when transition transforms end.
how: In compose.py and compose_lab.py GSAP timelines, animate individual child elements or use opacity/clip-path on parent wrappers instead of animating container transforms.

title: 95th-Percentile Scrim Stepper Gate
text: Before rendering text over generated backdrops, sample the 95th-percentile brightness in the text bounding box. If contrast falls below WCAG AA thresholds (3:1 for bold/display, 4.5:1 for body/captions), automatically step up background scrim density through 4 discrete tiers (.deep1 to .deep4) until compliant, using the minimum opacity that passes.
how: Add a bounding-box luminance check in preflight.py using Pillow/NumPy on background stills before HTML assembly; dynamically inject scrim-depth classes into compose_lab.py template.

title: Telestrator Freeze-Draw Breakdown Pattern
text: To explain complex tech interactions or fast-moving action clips, briefly pause playback into a freeze frame, apply a 30% background scrim, and animate high-contrast vector markup (target reticles, connecting paths, trajectory curves) directly onto the frozen screen. Resume full-speed playback or split-screen comparison immediately once the vector locks, breaking continuous visual fatigue in under 1.5 seconds.
how: Apply in `plan.py` for technical breakdowns on Kaise Tech. When analyzing UI flow or hardware, script a 1-second freeze-frame with GSAP stroke-dashoffset annotation lines.

title: Color-Coded Subsystem Flow Isolation
text: When presenting technical architecture (chips, algorithms, or mechanics), tint distinct subsystems with unique high-contrast colors sequentially along the energy/data path. At the script's tension point, isolate and disable one subsystem (e.g. cutting clock or cooling) to visually illustrate system failure before restoring operation in extreme slow-motion.
how: Use in `compose_lab.py` for Kaise Tech explainer scenes. Define multi-part SVGs with dedicated subsystem color classes, animating opacity to zero during the problem statement.

title: Unrendered Template Placeholder Sentinel
text: Automated HTML generation often leaves unpopulated template placeholders (e.g. {delta}, {stat_value}) when an LLM omits a key. Run a regex scan `re.findall(r'\{[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\}', html)` over the rendered DOM prior to browser capture, ignoring script/style blocks. Any match immediately fails preflight and triggers scene regeneration, preventing raw brace syntax from ever reaching rendered video frames.
how: Add to `preflight.py` right before launching Puppeteer/Playwright headless render. Scan `template.html` and raise `PreflightError` if unfilled `{placeholder}` tokens exist.

title: Clean Still Frame Heuristic Auditor
text: When picking stills or thumbnails from rendered video, candidate frames often hit cuts, black pauses, flashes, or blur. Sample 4 fps downscaled raw frames (160x90 gray), compute median luminance mean, standard deviation, inter-frame diff (near-cut), and spatial gradient. Reject frames where mean < 0.35*m_mean, mean > m_mean+0.25, std < 0.3*m_std, cut_diff > 3.5*m_cut, or gradient < 0.4*m_grad. Step up to ±10 frames (2.5s) to find the nearest clean frame.
how: Implement in `thumb.py` and `review.py`: when extracting hero frames or audit stills, evaluate candidate timestamps against this heuristic array to prevent selecting motion-blurred cuts or black transition frames.

title: Seamless Procedural Grain Tile Generator
text: Generate a lightweight, tileable film grain texture procedurally using NumPy and PIL without external assets. Create a 192x192 float32 normal noise grid, apply a 3-tap smooth wrap via `(g + np.roll(g, 1, 0)*0.5 + np.roll(g, 1, 1)*0.5) / 1.6`, inject quarter-strength 3-channel color noise, scale by `GRAIN_AMT (0.011) * OVERLAY_GAIN (1.35)`, center around 127.5, and clip to uint8.
how: Add to `compose_lab.py` asset initialization: procedurally generate `grain.png` on build rather than shipping static noise assets or running expensive FFmpeg grain passes on every render.

title: Reference DAG Chaining for Multi-Asset Generation
text: Maintain visual consistency across varied shots by organizing image generations into a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Generate root hero character/prop assets first without reference, then feed those outputs via `@ref` into all subsequent props, close-ups, and alternative angles.
how: In `plan.py` and `research.py`, structure image prompt requests so secondary scene visuals explicitly reference the file IDs of primary scene character/prop outputs.

title: Selective Fast-Motion Blur Sampling (mb brackets)
text: Instead of full-timeline post-process blur or heavy multi-sampling across every frame, declare selective motion blur windows `[{t0, t1, n}]` where `n` sub-frame samples are captured only during designated high-velocity asset transitions, leaving static holds lightweight.
how: In `compose.py` / `compose_lab.py`, add an `mb` pass flag in the render pipeline to dynamically oversample frames only during rapid slide or scale transforms.

title: Minimum Source-to-Screen Resolution Sentinel (RESCHECK)
text: Audit every rendered prop and cut-out image at time t to calculate source px per rendered screen px. If the ratio drops below 1.0 (source asset has fewer pixels than displayed screen pixels), fail the preflight build to eliminate visible upscaling blur.
how: Add an automated check in `preflight.py` comparing the native source dimensions of fetched FLUX/Muse assets against their peak rendered CSS dimensions.

title: Procedural Anchor-Linked Vector Markers
text: Define animated ink, lines, dimension callouts, and wake effects by binding their endpoints directly to asset anchor coordinates (e.g., `objectId.anchor` like bow, stern, waterline) rather than fixed pixel coordinates, ensuring connector lines track properly during scaling or repositioning.
how: Update `compose_lab.py` HUD connector and arrow lines to read live anchor bounding box coordinates from target DOM elements dynamically.

title: Ground-Plane Perspective Distance Ruler Formula
text: Project metric scales onto perspective photographs without 3D camera reconstruction using D = K / (row - horizon_row), where K = known_distance * (subject_row - horizon_row). Draw ticks crowding into perspective along the ground plane and animate a counting readout synchronized to narrator timing, providing accurate ground telemetry visualization on flat terrain.
how: Apply in plan.py and compose_lab.py when illustrating physical measurements, flight paths, or scale comparisons in explainer shorts.

title: Pincushion Loupe Shader with Explicit Gradient Sampling
text: Simulate an optical inspection loupe with 2.5x magnification, pincushion distortion (k ≈ 0.16 at the rim), and per-channel RGB dispersion. In WebGL or shader pipelines that branch inside the lens circle, texture samples must use explicit gradients (textureGrad) instead of standard texture lookups; hardware derivative calculations across conditional boundaries cause incorrect mip-map selection and dashed seam artifacts.
how: Update lens/zoom shader filters in compose_lab.py to use textureGrad for magnified quads and implement pincushion formula with channel-split chromatic aberration.

title: Silver-Gelatin Glass Negative Transmission Formula
text: Convert positive scans of documents or historical plates into backlit glass negatives using transmission curve T = 0.035 + 0.9 * (1 - pos)^1.25 with a warm silver-gelatin tint. Derive an emulsion mask by detecting outer scanner white borders touching boundaries, ensuring broken glass corners and border chips transmit pure 0.97 cool table backlight without emulsion.
how: Add a negative-inversion shader pass in compose.py / compose_lab.py for historical explainers on Puraan Ki Katha or Kaise Tech archive dives.

title: Tri-Layer Engraved Gold Keyline Stroke
text: Render metallic vector linework without cartoon outlines using three layers: a dark engraved background line 1.6 px wider than base, a banded metallic gradient line (dark #6F5220 -> base #C9A24B -> light #F3D98B -> specular #FFF4D2), and a sub-pixel highlight hairline on top. Animate the gradient sheen offset from -0.2 to 1.2 to create a light sweep on musical beats.
how: Add a deco_stroke helper in compose_lab.py to generate three-layer SVG/Canvas keylines for titles, UI containers, and badges.

title: Marquee Bulb Skeleton Crossing-Number & Ignition Model
text: Convert text into bulb marquees by sampling glyph skeletons using crossing numbers and welding endpoints within 14 px to prevent staircase bunching on curved letters (S, G, R). Trigger bulbs with a 1.6x brightness overshoot settling in 0.18 s accompanied by an ignition click, then cycle a 16th-note chase pattern once all bulbs ignite.
how: Implement in compose_lab.py for number counters, milestone reveals, and kinetic tech titles.

title: Acoustic Distance Progression for Narrator VO
text: Automate spatial narrative distance by feeding TTS voice through stepped DSP filters matching camera progression: bandpass 320–3800 Hz + slap-echo (exterior speaker), 1.2 kHz low-pass (through wall), RT60 1.8s convolution reverb (cavernous interior), and full dry (close mic). Keep saturation under 16% so Whisper ASR verification continues to pass at 100%.
how: Add scene-dependent DSP filter chain profiles in mix.py keyed by the location/staging tag emitted in plan.py scenes.

title: Constrained Glyph-Pool ASCII Dissolve Morph
text: Transition text into terminal imagery by dissolving sentence characters into image cells where the target ASCII density ramp strictly restricts glyphs to the characters in the source sentence. Target cells spawn particles from random matching source characters (scaling from 18 px down to 8 px while fading over 0.2 s), flashing 1.9x brightness upon arrival.
how: Add an ASCII particle morph effect in compose_lab.py for tech explainers when transforming prompt text or code snippets into hero icons.

title: Construction Grid to Typography Baseline Morph
text: When transitioning between visual diagramming and conclusion titles/formulas, do not cut or fade. Retract graphic shapes while leaving the thin construction grid lines (axes, tangents, rulers) intact. Animate these remaining grid lines directly into the text baselines, cap lines, and arithmetic glyphs (+, =, /) of the next typographic scene before folding them away.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, create a GSAP sequence where SVG grid lines transition their coordinates to target text baseline bounding boxes before headline text renders along them.

title: True-Area Geometric Quantity Scaling Rule
text: When representing data quantities with 2D geometric shapes (discs, squares), scaling radius or width linearly squares the visual quantity, deceptively exaggerating ratios (e.g., doubling radius yields 4x area). Discs must scale radius by sqrt(factor) to preserve true visual area equivalence. Use area-based scaling whenever comparing tech metrics, cost, or market sizes in lab explainers.
how: Apply in `plan.py` visual prompts and `compose_lab.py` data visualization presets, enforcing `Math.sqrt(value / base_value)` for circle radius transforms.

title: Camera-Scale Stroke and LOD Attenuation Formula
text: When executing wide pull-backs or zooms in vector/SVG scenes, static line weights degrade into dense black blobs or invisible hairlines. Dynamically scale stroke width by z^-0.6 relative to camera zoom z. Pair this with a hard level-of-detail scale cutoff ZL: elements below ZL (sub-labels, decor, micro-props) are culled completely from DOM/Canvas rendering, preserving silhouette clarity across multi-magnitude zooms.
how: Implement in `compose_lab.py` and HyperFrames SVG renderer: wrap vector groups in a camera transform listener adjusting `stroke-width` via `Math.pow(zoom, -0.6)` and auto-toggling opacity/display below threshold ZL.

title: Local-Light Modulated Volumetric Fog
text: Uniform scene fog lifts deep shadows into flat gray washed-out rectangles, destroying silhouette contrast in dark corridors. Multiply fog color by local surface illumination relative to average light: `fog_color * clamp(local_bounce / avg_bounce, 0.0, 1.0)`. Where scene lights are dead or off, fog density darkens to near-zero, rendering distant figures as true silhouette voids ('holes in the light').
how: Add to Three.js shader passes in future 3D scene rigs or CSS canvas lighting passes in `compose_lab.py` to prevent background washouts during dark tech explainer sequences.

title: Comparative Judgement Frame Protocol
text: When comparing items against a threshold, use staircase framing: meet the item on a detail close-up upon landing, then pull out to a wide 'judgement frame' showing the full item, the baseline threshold, and dimension arrow. Hold for >= 2.5 s. The verdict stamp/strike lands only after the camera settles. Judgement frames widen progressively across items (e.g. 28% to 50% width).
how: Apply in plan.py and compose_lab.py for benchmark comparisons (e.g., LLM context windows, GPU specs). Mandate fixed >= 2.5 s camera settles before showing pass/fail graphics.

title: Inanimate Prop Expressive Acting States
text: Give non-character props emotional readability through synchronized physics cues: failure/rejection unfolds over ~1.5 s with mechanisms decelerating, booms/vanes sagging, and gauges deflating to zero; joy/success snaps upright instantly with needles overshooting (back-ease) past 1.0. Snap actions settle in ~0.17 s (4 frames at 24 fps) with a 0.35-unit overshoot.
how: Add GSAP animation presets in compose_lab.py for UI cards, server icons, and metric gauges to visually convey positive vs negative tech benchmarks dynamically.

title: Thin-Geometry Vector Overlay for Matched Cutouts
text: AI matting models (like BiRefNet) degrade thin structures (cables, wires, antenna needles, masts, railings) into stair-stepped noise or erase them entirely. Detect or crop out thin structures during asset prep, then composite clean SVG/canvas vector strokes with identical color and weight over the cutout image at anchor coordinates.
how: Add a post-matting utility in preflight.py/compose.py that pairs cutouts with coordinate-anchored vector line overlays for device cords, antennas, and schematic pinouts.

title: Write-Wipe-Rewrite Misconception Correction
text: To debunk myths in tech explainers or mythology shorts, anchor the popular misconception at fixed screen coordinates. In one 0.2 s wipe, strike through or erase only the flawed keyword while leaving the frame intact, pause for a 0.3 s silent beat, and write the factual correction into the identical coordinate space before dropping a verdict checkmark.
how: In plan.py, format debunking beats into fixed-anchor claim/correction pairs; in compose_lab.py, implement an in-place text replacement animation on a single coordinate-locked container.

title: Proportion-by-Darkness Sweep
text: When presenting a statistic or ratio (e.g., 'nearly half lost', '16% affected'), animate an accent boundary line sweeping across the background footage to the exact percentage coordinate. The passed area desaturates and darkens (e.g., 40% saturation, -20% brightness), and the numerical figure renders prominently on the darkened side. This retains visual context while creating an immediate, high-contrast container for data.
how: In compose_lab.py, create a proportion_sweep widget using a CSS clip-path or SVG rect tweened with GSAP, applying backdrop-filter grayscale/brightness to the passed area and mounting the stat card.

title: Consonant-Band Spectral Music Ducking
text: Broadband volume ducking alone leaves voice consonants vulnerable to masking by music, degrading ASR transcriptions and mobile speaker clarity. Notch-cut or shelf-cut the 1.2 kHz to 5.0 kHz consonant intelligibility band by 4–6 dB on the music stem specifically during speech segments, combined with standard -8 dB overall ducking. This guarantees crisp consonant recognition without killing the rhythm track.
how: In mix.py, add dynamic parametric EQ attenuation (FFmpeg anequalizer or dynamic filter graph) targeting 1.2k–5k Hz on music stems whenever TTS speech activity is detected.

title: PDF Bounding-Box Swept Highlighter
text: When citing AI papers, government reports, or news articles, extract exact text line coordinates via pdftotext -bbox. Render the document page with slight perspective tilt and vignette, sweep an accent highlight box (mix-blend-mode: multiply) across the exact bounding box in 0.3–0.5 s, and pop out the highlighted figure into an enlarged, high-contrast stat badge beside the page.
how: In research.py and compose_lab.py, extract PDF bboxes using pypdf/fitz, pass the coordinates to an HTML overlay template, and animate the highlight sweep and callout card using GSAP.

title: Emissive Buffer Silhouette Occlusion
text: When rendering scenes with neon glows, backlit titles, or bloom post-processing, bright background emissive channels bleed color halos through foreground props and characters, turning white surfaces pink or destroying edge contrast. Stamp every foreground object or character silhouette as pure black (#000000) onto the offscreen emissive buffer before running the bloom pass to prevent glow bleed-through.
how: In our WebGL/Canvas post-processing pass for 2D/3D props and kinetic titles, draw foreground alpha silhouettes in solid black to the glow/bloom render target before blur calculation.

title: Diegetic Band-Pass Filter Snap
text: When cutting into an in-world screen recording, retro terminal, or phone interface demo, band-pass the master music bed to 380 Hz–2800 Hz with light saturation for 1–2 bars to establish a diegetic device texture. On the scene climax or transition back to narrator voice, snap or rapidly sweep the filter open to full spectrum on the downbeat.
how: In mix.py, parse scene flags (e.g. diegetic_bandpass: true) and apply FFmpeg highpass=f=380,lowpass=f=2800 to the audio stem for the flagged cue duration.

title: BPM-Locked Multi-Subdivision Cutting Ladder
text: Edit non-narrated or montage sequences strictly by mathematical subdivisions of a locked BPM (e.g., at 120 BPM / 30 fps: 1 bar = 60 frames, 1 beat = 15 frames, triplet = 5, sixteenth = 3.75 frames). Progressively step cut duration from 2 bars down through triplets and 2-frame sixteenth flicker cuts into a 15 ms abrupt dry stop with remaining reverb tail.
how: Apply in plan.py and compose.py when generating fast montage sequences or recap hooks, locking cuts directly to calculated frame multiples of the music bed tempo.

title: Handwriting Stroke Pacing Limits
text: To maintain human-like kinetic handwriting on screen, cap stroke rendering speed to approximately 0.1 s per stroke for large text/characters (0.04 s for small labels). Never accelerate beyond 0.07 s per stroke; if pacing tightens against speech duration, reduce the on-screen text volume rather than unnaturally accelerating the drawing animation.

title: Two-Octave FR-4 Clearance-Pour Board Engine

title: Differential AC/DC Current Motion Kinetics
text: Differentiate alternating vs direct current flows visually on traces without perspective: AC is represented as bidirectional rocking dashes oscillating at a scaled frequency (e.g., 0.55–1.1 Hz) over a faint baseline; DC is rendered as a continuous unidirectional head stream leaving an exponentially decaying afterglow tail; step-downs shrink stroke width and dash lengths synchronously.

title: Waveform-Correlated Functional State Audio Synthesis
text: Link electrical/system state changes directly to sound design: map alternating states to an amplitude-gated tremolo drone tuned to power mains frequency harmonics (50 Hz / G1 or 60 Hz / Bb1); smooth the gate into a pure sustained tone at the exact frame a rectifier/transformer conducts, accompanied by stepped pitch-down relay click transients for transformer stages.

title: Centroid-Linked Median Background Crowd Tracking

Isolate blobs with pixel luminance deltas > 22/255, extract centroids, and connect each centroid to its nearest predecessor within a distance threshold (< 70 px) with decaying 2 px stroke lines while dimming and desaturating the video plate.

title: Chalk Coverage Sprite Accumulator with World-Space Slate Tile

Incrementally uncover pixels up to current arc length with round leading edges, modulating alpha through a world-space periodic slate grain tile. Restrict loose powder particles (2–5 grains) to stroke lift-off points.

title: Anchor Coordinate Texture Projection
text: To prevent procedural shading, hatching, or paper-tooth textures from swimming over moving geometry ('through-glass' artifact), compute texture UVs in anchor coordinates by projecting vertex positions through a fixed reference camera. Within any continuous camera movement, restrict camera transforms strictly to translation (truck, crane, push). Never rotate the camera within an anchored shot group; execute rotations or re-scaling only across hard cuts or inside designated transition insets.

title: Elevation-Scaled Drop Shadow Rig
text: In 2.5D paper, card, and UI prop staging, communicate physical elevation and kinetic weight by coupling shadow properties to virtual Z-height. An object lifted or flying in casts a diffuse, large shadow (30–45 px offset, 25–40 px blur, 0.15 opacity). Upon slapping down, animate the shadow to snap with a 1-frame overshoot into a tight contact shadow (3–4 px offset, 2–4 px blur, 0.45 opacity).

title: Alternating-Pitch Biphonic Audio Ticks
text: Monotone metronomic timer ticks cause ear fatigue and masking during fast countdowns or multi-second builds. Alternate consecutive tick clicks between two distinct frequencies spaced a third apart (e.g., 1850 Hz and 1480 Hz) while ping-ponging subtle stereo pan (±15% L/R). During the final 3 seconds, narrow the interval and lift tick gain by +3 dB over the ambient bed.

title: Many-Into-One Climax Grid Collapse
text: To build tension toward a major reveal, statistical drop, or countdown zero, partition the canvas into a dense multi-cell grid (e.g., 3×3 or 4-panel split-screen) populated sequentially on rhythmic beats. Exactly at the climax beat (T=0), collapse all split-cell boundaries inward over 0.35–0.45 s into a single full-bleed hero video shot, accompanied by a 1-frame contrast flash or UI color inversion.

title: Dual-Mark Zero Timestamp Calibration
text: Never rely on container metadata or start-of-file offsets to sync archival event footage. Calibrate event time T0 by cross-checking two independent markers: a high-contrast visual transient (such as an ignition flash or digital bug rollover) and an audio speech transient (such as the first phonetic burst of a known callout). Measure source cut offsets directly on decoded frames.

title: First-Person Mystery POV Inversion

At the emotional climax, cut directly to the counterpart subject's eye-line looking back, revealing who or what the camera was all along, followed by minimal closing text on quiet visual space.

title: Pre-Ignition Quarter-Second Score Mute
text: To maximize impact during a countdown or high-stakes reveal, drop all background score stems 0.25 seconds prior to the zero/climax frame, leaving solely native Foley, diegetic room audio, and the final tick. Trigger an un-ducked orchestral impact or native transient exactly on frame zero.

title: NPR Screen-Space Ring Traced 3D Crayon Renderer
text: Render 3D low-poly primitives offscreen into an 8-bit region ID, light, and depth buffer at half resolution. Trace region boundaries into smoothed vector rings using marching squares, then draw crayon hatching and outlines into 2D layers. Keep paper tooth, emboss, and camera vignette completely static in screen space while 3D objects rotate and parallax behind it, stepping drawings at 12 fps.

title: Strip-Perspective Opaque Projection Rule
text: When applying pseudo-3D Y-axis rotation (rotY ≤ 24°) to 2D UI panels via sliced canvas strips, semi-transparent layers cause visible vertical seam artifacts where slice edges overlap and double the alpha. Always render UI panel surfaces at 100% opacity during the strip slicing and projection phase, and composite soft alpha transparency, glows, and sweeps in screen space afterwards.

title: Dual-Scan Plane State Rewrite Shader
text: To transition between two historical states or metrics in a single continuous shot without cutting, use two analytic moving scan planes: d = S - dot(p, D). Geometry ahead is unseen (d < 0). A bright front pulse exp(-d²/w²) reveals state A. A second trailing scan plane sweeps behind it, overwriting visual textures, lighting conditions, and HUD annotations from state A to state B in real time as the front passes.
how: Implement in custom Three.js shader uniforms inside compose_lab.py. Pass two time-dependent scan front positions to transition tech architecture diagrams or server loads without cuts.

title: Pentatonic Landmark Unit Sonification
text: When counting or stacking sequential data units, standard units emit brief inharmonic clicks (1-3 kHz wood or 3-8 kHz metal). Every 10th landmark unit triggers a pitched mallet note (vibraphone or glockenspiel) ascending through a pentatonic scale. Viewers aurally track scale magnitude through rising melodic intervals rather than reading digits alone.

title: Voxel Sticker-to-Toy Hinge Rig
text: Convert 2D sprite matrices into procedural 3D characters without skinned meshes. Each non-empty pixel instantiates a bevelled unit cube. The rig hierarchy links Root (pos, yaw) -> Hinge (rotation around feet axis from 0° flat sticker on surface to 90° upright toy) -> Squash (scale on Y/Z) -> Spin. Pure-black matrix pixels designate protruding eyes that blink by temporarily taking the color of the pixel directly above.

title: Camera-to-Subject Minimum Pixel Coverage Audit
text: Prevent hero props or character mascots from shrinking into illegible specks during wide camera pull-backs. Calculate on-screen pixel diameter at render time: screen_px = (world_width * frame_height) / (2 * distance * tan(fov / 2)). Preflight flags any keyframe where the subject drops below 35 px in wide recap shots, clamping camera distance or applying a temporary scale boost.

title: Outline Union Occlusion Dimming
text: When rendering 2D segmented bone rigs or multi-part illustrations out of points or strokes, interior overlapping segments look like confusing transparent wireframes. To maintain solid silhouette readability, cull or dim outline points that fall inside another part on the same or nearer z-layer down to <= 5% brightness. Ensure animal/character side profiles stagger legs so silhouettes never merge into single thick limbs.

title: Sinusoidal Engraving Hatch Swell Law
text: To give procedural or vector hatch lines natural intaglio burin weight without flat pen looks, calculate line width along normalized stroke parameter u (0 to 1) as: width * (0.2 + 0.8 * sin(pi * u)^0.7). Taper the line over its first and last 22% of length. Activate stroke families progressively by tone thresholds: primary hatching at tone >= 0.14, cross-hatch at >= 0.50, and tertiary cross at >= 0.75.

title: 5-Level Multi-Resolution Splatting Pyramid
text: Render depth-of-field bokeh particles across 5 discrete Gaussian blur tiers: sigma = [1.0, 2.1, 4.8, 10.5, 23.0] px at buffer scales [1, 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125]. Fractional particle blur smoothly interpolates energy between adjacent levels. Scale per-level energy gain by [1.0, 1.55, 2.7, 5.2, 10.0] / (res_scale^2), ensuring deep-bokeh out-of-focus discs automatically expand in area while diluting core luminance without blowing out exposure.

title: Jittered Grid Text Particle Sampling
text: When forming text titles from particles, never sample positions randomly—random distributions cause clumping and broken letter strokes. Render glyphs to an offscreen alpha mask and sample on a fixed jittered grid (one particle per sample point). Allocate ~3,400 points for a large headline (140–170 px) and ~800 points for secondary lines (30–40 px). Once landed, freeze positions with sub-pixel shimmer only.

title: Grazing-Angle Projection-to-Pin Text Switching
text: Text printed on perspective ground planes becomes illegible at oblique angles (>45° camera tilt from nadir). At tilt angles > 45°, transition from plane-projected text to 2D screen-pinned billboard labels attached to the ground coordinate by a 2.5 px leader line, preventing perspective compression distortion.

title: Hard-Edged Two-Step Screen-Print Glow
text: Avoid GPU-heavy, blurry drop-shadows that degrade flat vector clarity. Simulate luminous bodies by layering two concentric solid discs, stepped one and two tonal values lighter than the dark ground. Bright objects maintain crisp graphic silhouettes, replicating mid-century screen-printed posters while eliminating blur shader overhead.

title: Logarithmic Scale Ribbon with Dynamic FOV Readout

The camera's physical field-of-view width (from light-years to micrometers) updates continuously in log-space. At scale shifts, milestone icons pulse with spring overshoot while the readout rolls to the target order of magnitude.

title: Fixed-Step LOD Streamline Engine
text: Render vector flow fields (wind, traffic, currents) without flicker using world-space jittered seed grids across discrete LOD octaves. Spacing halves per level; octave weight is 1 - |log2(on_screen_spacing / target)|, with adjacent levels summing to 1. Integrate polylines using fixed-count RK2 steps and animate stroke phases using compressive time-of-flight (integral of ds / v^0.6) against a global flow clock.

title: Field-Velocity Modulated Wind Foley Synthesis
text: Synthesize procedural wind and flow audio directly from visual simulation metrics. Drive three filtered noise bands (body 90–420 Hz, mid 0.4–1.6 kHz, air 1.8–6.5 kHz) based on mean on-screen vector magnitude, and add a narrow-band whistle whose pitch scales linearly with peak velocity (pitch = 400 Hz + 24 Hz * m/s), automatically ducking 300 Hz–4 kHz under speech.

title: Lead-Consonant Beat Pre-Roll Offset
text: When synchronizing short spoken voice shouts or sound cues to a strict musical tempo grid, place the audio clips 20–30 ms before the beat marker. Spoken consonant attacks take 20–30 ms to peak; offsetting them ensures acoustic perceptual onset hits exactly on the visual downbeat. For crowd vocal hits, stack 4–6 distinct voices staggered 5–6 ms apart and panned between -0.6 and +0.6.

title: Channel-Cap Specular Highlight Guard
text: To prevent high-energy climaxes (gilded metal, neon HUD spikes, laser passes) from blowing out into flat, desaturated white blobs, clamp lit specular highlights to a maximum of 82% on every color channel toward the target tint. Clamping preserves underlying texture seams, leaf lines, and graphic outlines instead of blooming out into solid white.

title: Downbeat Exponential Squash Decay
text: For rhythm-locked kinetic props and characters, synthesize continuous beat bounce and hit reactions without keyframe bloat using: scaleY = 1 - 0.1 * exp(-frac(t) * 16), where frac(t) is beat progress (0 to 1). For heavy hits or judgements, trigger a damped oscillation: cos(30 * (t - t0)) * exp(-8 * (t - t0)) for 0.35 s duration.

title: Single-Entity Carrier Verb Guard
text: Isolated single-word proper nouns or product names (e.g., 'Aura.', 'Cursor.') at sentence boundaries suffer frequent Whisper ASR rejection and listener misinterpretation. Always prepend an active carrier verb or framing phrase (e.g., 'Meet Aura', 'Inside Cursor') to provide necessary phonemic context and prevent syllable clipping in automated voice gating.

text: Verdict and status stamps must animate from 2.6× to 1.0× scale in 0.09s using ease-in, followed by a 5% damped bounce. Fire an impact SFX, a 16–26px quadratic camera shake, and a screen flash on the hit frame. Flash overlay opacity must be clamped at 0.50 max; a 1.0 white flash is perceived as a dropped frame.

title: Diagrammatic Limb Peripheral Alpha Fade
text: Diagrammatic hands or tools interacting with technical props look like severed plastic toys if shaded realistically. Render limbs one tier lighter using flat near-white fill, thin grey outlines, and segmented knuckle strokes, applying a linear alpha gradient along the limb direction to softly fade the wrist out as it approaches the viewport edge.

title: Selective 10 FPS Line Boil with Text Masking

Never apply the boil filter to typography, HUD markers, or halftone dot grids to prevent illegible visual vibration.

title: Axial Explode with Stationary Luminescent Core
text: Translating outer casings and inner components together in parallel during teardowns does not visually register as an explosion. Anchor the internal core component stationary at its origin while translating outer shells outward strictly along their local assembly axes. Concurrently shift the stationary core's material to a near-white luminescent state and counter-rotate any rotational elements (rotors/stators) across 1–2 musical beats.

title: Accumulating Side-Rail Spec Chip Docking
text: Displaying technical specs sequentially causes earlier stats to be forgotten, while keeping all on screen causes clutter. Display each callout as a hero card for >= 2.5 s with animated rolling digits. Upon completion, fade the hero card over 0.35 s while sliding a compact summary chip horizontally into a persistent side rail (step = min(112, 410 / (n - 1)) px, capacity 2–5). Retain the rail until final lockup.

title: Held-Envelope Foley Ducking with Transient Bypass
text: Mechanical SFX and UI whines often sit in the 300 Hz–4 kHz vocal range; simple sidechain ducking pumps awkwardly during natural pauses between words. Duck both music (-16.5 dB) and foley/SFX (-15 dB) under speech using a 0.5 s max-filter hold envelope so attenuation remains clamped during inter-word gaps. Allow only the first 0.2 s of UI confirmation transients to bypass attenuation.

title: Target-Box Bounding Flag Filter
text: Procedural target reticles around technical models balloon wildly when bounding boxes include thin peripheral attachments (wires, hoses) or hidden internals. Tag peripheral connectors with box: false and hidden sub-assemblies with internal: true. Calculate focus target dimensions strictly from external structural meshes at rest pose. Snap the box from 1.9x scale with 30% alpha over 0.22 s cubic ease-out.

title: Coordinated Multi-Channel Flash Curve
text: Single-channel screen flashes or opacity fades appear synthetic and detached from the scene. Implement a dual-strike flash curve: 150 ms primary strike, rapid dip, 60 ms secondary re-strike, and exponential decay with a 0.22 s time constant. Synchronously modulate ambient light intensity, background sky brightness uniform, fog density, and camera exposure, followed by thunder or boom SFX delayed by exactly 0.25 s.

title: Micro Open Loop Interval Rule
text: Inject a micro open loop or pattern interrupt every 5 to 8 seconds (e.g., 'lekin twist yaha hai', 'par ek dikkat thi'). Pacing dips occur when narrative tension plateaus for more than 5 seconds without a new curiosity gap or visual shift.

title: Payoff-Snap Zero-Linger Outro

title: Dual-Metric Funnel Diagnostic Gate
text: Decouple Shorts evaluation into two separate signals: Hook Efficiency ('Stayed to watch' vs swiped away) and Pacing Efficiency (Average Percentage Viewed from Engaged Views). Low swipe-stop indicates first-frame visual failure; early APV collapse (3–8s) indicates delayed payoff or narrative fluff.

title: Share-Save Utility Payoff Structure
text: DM shares and saves heavily outrank likes and comments in recommendation weighting. To trigger saves, scripts must contain high-density reference utility (e.g., exact specs, command syntax, cheatsheets) in the final act. To trigger DM shares, the script must frame a relatable paradox, peer debate, or immediate 'send this to someone who uses X' value proposition rather than passive entertainment.

title: Strict 5-Hashtag Niche Clamping
text: Instagram strictly limits and penalizes Reels using broad hashtag dumps; the hard cap is exactly 5 tags. Algorithm distribution relies on these for topic clustering under user topic controls. Video publishing pipelines must extract exactly 3 to 5 hyper-specific niche tags directly tied to the primary named entity, dropping generic reach tags (#viral, #trending, #reels).

title: First-Three-Second Skip-Rate Gate
text: Early viewer swipe-away (>40% drop within 0–3 seconds) acts as a primary negative distribution signal. The first 3 seconds require non-zero visual velocity, an explicit kinetic on-screen value proposition, and zero silence. Any visual asset that remains static or delays voice onset beyond 0.2s degrades recommendation eligibility.

title: Small-Channel Outlier Validation Gate
text: Before greenlighting a topic or format, verify organic algorithmic pull rather than creator subscriber momentum. Score an idea as viable only if at least one channel with fewer than 100,000 subscribers achieved a 3x view outlier relative to that channel's median view count on the topic within the last 60 days.

title: Duration-Tiered Shorts Retention Benchmark Rule
text: Retention targets must scale inversely with runtime rather than using a uniform retention percentage. Shorts under 35 seconds require 80% to 90% average percentage viewed (with loops exceeding 100% for breakout reach). Shorts 60 seconds and longer succeed at 60% to 75% average view duration. Enforcing an 85%+ retention standard on 60s+ narrative explainers creates false-negative audits and over-pruned scripts.

title: Sound-Off First-Two-Second Visual Loop Verification
text: Autoplay Shorts viewers make stay-or-swipe decisions within 1 to 2 seconds before voice audio registers or when device volume is muted. The opening 2 seconds cannot rely solely on voiceover to hook the audience. Frames 0-60 must contain an active visual transformation, visible countdown, or immediate kinetic curiosity trigger that creates a reason to watch with audio completely muted.

title: Post-2025 Shorts Engaged-View Telemetry Decoupling
text: Since March 31, 2025, YouTube Shorts views register instantly at frame 0 playback with no minimum dwell time, measuring algorithmic exposure rather than content attention. Ingesting pipelines must decouple raw views from engaged views (found in YouTube Analytics Advanced Mode). Only engaged views and viewed-vs-swiped-away ratios should drive content scoring, RPM revenue projections, and hook iteration.

title: Yellow = New Part Rule
text: In technical or assembly sequences, the 'new' object added in the current step is colored safety yellow (#F7D35A). Once fitted or the step ends, it fades to white. This creates an immediate visual anchor for the viewer's eye.

title: Magnifier Match-Cut

title: Fixed-Seed Stroke Stability
