how: Add carve() to print.js. Replace all line() calls for key lines (mountain ridges, pine needles, rock facets, wave outlines) with carve(). Tune taper per element (e.g., mountain ridges [.35,.02] and [.02,.4]). Seed per layer for consistent jitter across frames.

title: Vertical Title Slip (Cartouche) with Series Label & Seal
text: cartouche(x, cx, y0, title, {series, w=84, size=50, fill='#f3e7c6', tab=beniL}) draws a vertical slip: series in small red tab at top, title below in sumi. Double border (3px + 1.2px inset). vtext() writes chars vertically (gap 1.06). Seal stamped beside slip with pop-in scale (1.35→1 via ss) and multiply blend. Animated reveal: slip p=clamp((t-t0)/.35), seal p=clamp((t-t1)/.3).
how: Add cartouche(), vtext(), vlen() to print.js. In main.js, define CART[i] positions per sheet. In drawSheet(), trigger at T.cart.vX[0] with stampFn for slip, drawSeal for seal. For subtitles, use horizontal slip (subtitle() in main.js) with same fill/border, seal '旅' at left. Replace thumb.py title cards with this style for ukiyo-e series.

title: Parametric Traveler with Gait, Mino, Hat-Off, Sit/Back Modes
text: traveler(x, px, py, s, o) draws a 100-unit character scaled by s. Modes: 'walk' (antiphase legs, bob, arm swing, staff sway), 'sit' (bench, tea cup lift, head tilt), 'back' (rear view, bundle, hat on/off). Details: kasa hat with brim ribs, cord blowing in wind; indigo kimono with igeta-gasuri cross stitches; leggings; straw sandals; bundle with knots; mino straw cape (18 strokes + hem); head side view with sakayaki + topknot. All geometry procedural, no assets.
how: Port traveler.js to Python (traveler.py) using Cairo or Skia via PyCairo/PySkia, or keep in JS for HyperFrames. Define limbPoly() for variable-width limbs. Expose modes: walk(ph), sit(cup), back(hatOff), mino(bool), wind, tilt. Use in compose_ukiyoe.py for character shots. Deterministic at 8fps (q8).

title: Whiteout Transition: Wave Claws Burst to Paper
text: At crash (29.7–30.4s), 16 claws + 26 droplets emit from wave tip in screen space (mulberry seeded). Claw len/wid scale with progress^1.7. After 72% progress, fade in full-screen TX.paper (multiply). Creates a diegetic transition: the wave becomes the paper. No cross-fade; the white claws *are* the paper texture.
how: In main.js whiteout(t, M), compute wave tip in world, project to screen via M. Loop 16 claws with fclaw() (claw variant with fill/stroke styles). Loop 26 droplets. If progress>.72, ctx.globalAlpha=ss((c-.72)/.26); drawImage(TX.paper). Call after drawSheet, before subtitle. Add to compose_ukiyoe.py as a transition primitive.

title: Print Texture Overlay (printTex)
text: printTex(ctx, grain, opacity, x, y) applies a subtle paper fiber texture via seeded noise. Called after wave body fill and before key lines. Gives final render a tactile paper feel without heavy post-processing.
how: Implement in print.js using existing vnoise. Add as final pass in compose_lab.py and compose.py before cover stamp. Control via style config: grain=0.14, opacity=0.2 for lab; grain=0.08 for classic.

title: Bloom Clip for Color Arrival Transitions
text: bloomClip() generates a noisy growing circle (24 segments, radius modulated by n2) centered on subject. Used as canvas clip region for color wash reveal. Simple, deterministic, and visually organic.
how: Add to thumb.py and compose_lab.py for transition wipes: color arrives from a point with noisy edge. Parameterize by arrival field progress (0-1).

title: Sound Cues Export: Stroke Times, Trajectories, Events
text: export_cues.mjs extracts: static layer stroke draw times (from time texture), hat trajectory (speed, screen pan per frame), and event list (hat lift, bounce, steps, bells, dive, catch). Outputs cues.json for sound design.
how: Add to publish.py: after render, export stroke timestamps (from preflight), object trajectories (from plan.py), and event markers (from script). Feed to mix.py for automated SFX placement and music sync.

title: Step-based animation (12fps) for paper elements
text: Paper pieces move on twos (stepT = floor(t/STEP)*STEP, STEP=1/12) while camera moves every frame. Adds stop-motion feel. Jitter per frame via deterministic hash(id, frame).
how: In HyperFrames render loop, add stepT(t) for designated layers. In compose_lab.py, add animate_on_twos prop. Use for paper-cut sequences in Puraan Ki Katha.

title: Reserve/mask for highlight preservation
text: Before washing color, draw mask polygons (clouds, building windows) with reserve(ctx, poly, feather, expand, seed) which writes to alpha channel. Subsequent washes skip masked pixels. Keeps paper-white highlights clean.
how: Add reserve() to compose_lab.js: ctx.globalCompositeOperation='destination-out'; draw feathered polygon. Use for keeping title areas clean during background animation. Call before wash() in pipeline.

title: Manifest-Driven Asset Geometry
text: Every sprite in manifest.json: w,h,crop[x,y], world x,y, scale, plus overprint offsets (off[x,y]) and source rect (src[x,y], srck). Enables pixel-perfect compositing at any camera push-in.
how: Adopt in compose.py/compose_lab.py: load manifest → place sprites by world coords → camera transform handles scale/pan.

title: Ransom Note Title Generator
text: Per-character variation: cycle through 8 (font, paper, ink) combos, size 86–114% of base, digits swap to lining figures. Each char baked as separate PNG with manifest entry.
how: Extend thumb.py hook-title path: input string → ransom() → composite sprites per manifest positions.

title: Stamp Color Separation Extractor
text: From scan: paper mask = min(R,G,B)<228; red plate = (R−(G+B)/2−18)/110; blue plate = (B−R−4)/90. Upscale 2×, Gaussian sharpen (σ=1.1/0.8), contrast stretch, tighten edges with (x−0.38)*5+0.5.
how: Add to asset prep script for any multi-color print source; output plates as separate sprites for overprint animation.

title: Timeline Generator from VO Durations
text: Input: VO start/dur per line + cue offsets within line. Output: cues.json (zh/en/t0/t1) + timeline.json (sections, VO, clips, subs). Handles intra-line splits (offset 2.3s → new slip) and overlap guard (next slip −0.08s).
how: Replace manual cue timing: timeline.py reads vo/dur.json + CUES list → writes cues.json for bake2.py and timeline.json for render.

title: Unified Archival Grade Presets
text: Three CSS filter presets for consistent look: footage (grayscale(1) contrast(1.22) brightness(0.94)), documents (grayscale(1) contrast(1.05) brightness(0.86)), maps (grayscale(1) brightness(0.62) contrast(1.1)). Applied at draw time, not baked.
how: Define gradePresets in compose_lab.py config. Apply via ctx.filter in plate() / cover() based on asset type tag. Keeps source files pristine; grade adjustable per project.

title: Ring Callout with Progress Leader
text: Thin circle draws clockwise with ease-out progress (0-1). At 60% progress, a leader line extends sideways and a label fades in. Used to highlight ignition point on freeze frame, mooring mast on approach footage, and gas cells on schematic.
how: Add ringCallout(cx, cy, radius, progress, label, side) to compose_lab.py primitives. Call from scene plan with progress tied to section timer. Use for data points, map locations, diagram highlights.

title: Corroboration Badge (Red Box + Hand-Drawn Check)
text: Animated red square with hand-drawn checkmark (three strokes) appears at source timestamp. No text — pure visual 'verified' signal. Used on each evidence column when its timing aligns.
how: Add corroborationBadge(x, y, triggerTime, duration) to compose_lab.py. Trigger from film.json evidence events. Style matches lab look (red accent, mono font).

title: Waveform Bar Synced to Playback
text: Precomputed 1/60s peaks (JSON) drawn as vertical bars; played portion bright, unplayed dim. Vertical playhead line moves with audio. Used for newsreel commentary clips.
how: Add wave.py step in prep.sh to generate peaks JSON for each audio asset. Add waveformBar(component) to compose_lab.py that reads peaks and current playhead from shared events.json.

title: Dot Grid for Count Visualization
text: Grid of circles (passengers/crew/ground) — live dots fill instantly, dead dots draw red stroke over time. Numbers revealed at end. 36 passengers (13 dead), 61 crew (22 dead), 1 ground (1 dead).
how: Add dotGrid(data[], cols, radius, revealStagger) to compose_lab.py. Data: [{label, total, dead, color}]. Use for casualty counts, server stats, model parameters, benchmark results.

title: Broken-Axis Timeline (Dual Scale)
text: Single horizontal axis with a break: left segment = 4 minutes (240s compressed to 320px), right segment = 32 seconds (stretched to 140px). Break marked with double-slash. Three event markers (ropes, ignition, impact) animate in.
how: Add brokenTimeline(segments[], events[]) to compose_lab.py. Segments = [{start, end, pxLength}]. Events = [{time, label, color}]. Use for stories with vastly different time scales (launch + orbit, bug + fix).

title: Data-driven schematic map with rainfall bands, coastlines, route, fire spots
text: main.js buildMap() projects 70+ lat/lon stations (STN) to equirectangular, interpolates log rainfall via inverse-distance weighting + 2-layer Perlin noise (scales 26,11). Classifies into 5 log-spaced bands (250-4000mm) with fixed colors. Renders coastlines as stroked paths (step 26px), 26 fire spots in 500-900mm band, quadratic Bezier route (centre→rainforest). All deterministic.
how: Use pattern for Animated Map with Albers Projection: swap projection, keep band logic. Feed real rainfall CSV to scout.py. Output band GeoJSON for compose_lab.py. Add fire/route as data-driven props.

title: Logarithmic rainfall gauge HUD with animated pointer & tick marks
text: drawHUD() right column: log-scale bar (100-4000mm) mapped to pixel width. Pointer is filled Bezier triangle at log(mm). Ticks at 250/500/1k/2k/4k with labels. Biome panels left: colored stroke + Cormorant title + italic subtitle + mono badge (01/05). All fade in/out per biome time window.
how: Add to HUD component library (Integrated HUD Overlay System). Use for data-driven shorts (climate, energy). Parameterize scale, ticks, colors. Drive from script measurements (Data-verified script numbers).

title: Data-driven visuals with primary-source measurements
text: White model uses 3DBAG LOD1.3 (building footprints, heights, construction years) and BGT (water, bridges). prep.py computes stats.json: pre-1940 area share, band counts, over-100m towers, tallest height, shadow reach (astronomical sun position). Every on-screen number comes from stats.json, not script.
how: For Kaise Tech/Puraan Ki Katha: fetch primary datasets (gov, papers), write prep.py to compute measured stats, inject into plan.py as verified numbers.

title: Handwritten annotation system with curved leaders
text: scene.js hand(txt, x, y, progress) draws Caveat font with paper-shadow, clips to reveal width (eo easing). leader(x0,y0,x1,y1,progress) draws quadratic curve with jitter, dot at target. note() combines both with timed fade-in/out. Used for species labels, scale markers, dimension lines.
how: Add hand() and leader() to compose_lab.py for diegetic labels on HUD panels, map callouts, schematic dimensions.

title: Procedural biome generation with rainfall-driven zones
text: scene.js defines ZONES by world-x (desert <250mm → mulga 250-500 → wood 500-900 → wet 900-1800 → rain >1800). Hero plants placed first; fill uses zoneJit (jittered zone boundary). Each zone has specific generators (spinifex, mulga, gum, ash, rainforest trees) with scale/sway params. Parallax layers (far/mid/main/fg) with different speeds.
how: For map/geography shorts: define data-driven zones (rainfall, elevation, pop density), assign procedural asset sets, use zoneJit for natural edges.

title: Handwriting ribbon fill with chisel angle + pressure taper
text: Stroke ribbon width varies by pen angle (chisel effect: 0.8+0.2×|sin(θ-2.35)|) and pressure (ramp up 0.72→1 over 2.2×stroke_width, ramp down near end). Overshoot hook at stroke end uses seeded noise. Deterministic via mulberry seed.
how: Upgrade compose_lab.py kinetic titles and lab-look UI panels: replace uniform-width stroke with ribbon(ctx, stroke, progress, k) that computes per-vertex normals and variable half-width. Use existing seeded noise for overshoot/jitter.

title: NOAA Meeus solar position for accurate shadow animation
text: solar(year, month, day, utc_hours, lat, lon) returns altitude/azimuth to ~0.01°. Used to cast winter-solstice noon shadows on 2 m grid: extrude building heights, march along sun azimuth, compare heightfield. Output shadow reach, shaded roof counts, per-building distance.
how: Integrate sun.py into map/data shorts (Puraan Ki Katha map sequences, Kaise Tech solar explainers). Precompute shadow masks in prep step, feed to compose_lab.py as animated mask layers. Use Albers projection for map coords.

title: Structure-Tensor Directed Hatching Filter
text: Convert photographic or AI-generated input frames into woodcut/engraving line art whose cut direction follows natural contours. Compute Sobel gradients to build the structure tensor (Jxx, Jxy, Jyy), box blur to regularize, and extract the isophote orientation angle theta = 0.5 * atan2(2*Jxy, Jxx - Jyy) + pi/2. Blend with a fallback angle weighted by coherence, then generate variable-width hatch strokes driven by smoothed luminance.
how: Add to compose_lab.py as a procedural NPR rendering filter for technical diagrams, historical explainers, or high-contrast stylized cutouts before compositing.

title: Single-Line Vector Glyphs for Real-Time Stroke Animation
text: Render authentic handwriting reveals letter-by-letter using 1-line vector skeleton fonts (EMS single-line format) stored as normalized coordinate arrays ([x, y, x, y...]). Unlike standard outlined TTF fonts that require artificial clipping or mask geometry, single-line polyline strokes animate natively with exact arc-length timing and variable stroke-width pressure profiles.
how: Store EMS single-line glyph JSONs in assets/fonts/ and use them in HyperFrames/compose_lab.py to animate whiteboard and diagram text write-ins cleanly.

title: Relief shading via inflated normals on distance field
text: Region.normal(x,y,R) computes a pseudo-3D normal from the distance field: height h(d)=R*sqrt(1-(1-d/R)^2) (round edges, flat top). Normal = (-gx*dh, -gy*dh, 1) normalized. Lambert tone = amb + k*max(0, N·L) + rim*(1-Nz). R≈60px sets relief scale. Gives convincing 3D form from 2D silhouette.
how: In woodcut style guide for planners: specify light direction (e.g., lower-right for 'forge' look) and relief_radius_px. In compose_woodcut.py, use reliefTone(reg, L, {R, amb, k, rim}) as tone function for hatch(). Works on any closed polygon (maps, icons, diagrams).

title: Deterministic seeded asset generation with memoization
text: Region constructor takes polygons + {res, pad, bbox} → rasterizes at fixed resolution, computes distance field once. shape(), bell(), gifts() use memo(key, factory) cache keyed by geometry params + seed. All randomness via mulberry(seed) (deterministic LCG). Assets baked once, reused across frames/shots. Region.res controls detail vs speed (2px default).
how: Adopt in asset bake pipeline: bake_asset(asset_type, params, seed) → manifest.json with content hash. In doctor.py, verify manifest matches. Use mulberry for all procedural jitter (hand shake, particle spawn, stroke chip). Ensures reproducible renders across machines and after code fixes.

title: Height-field sculpting for deterministic close-up assets
text: Sculpt class builds a height field from capsules, blobs, planks with bevels, creases, and noise. Shaded with directional lighting (ambient, diffuse, specular per material) to grayscale+alpha, then fed to woodcutFilter. Used for founder's hands (forearm, fingers, knuckles, veins, sleeve folds) and boy's compass palm (cupped hand, fingers, thumb, compass disc/lid/needle). All geometry parameterized, seeded, resolution-independent.
how: Add sculpt.py porting hands.js Sculpt class. Use for recurring 'close-up' inserts: hands manipulating objects, writing, turning dials. Define asset recipes (hand poses, tool grips) as data. Render to grayscale canvas → woodcut filter → HyperFrames layer. Cache baked assets per seed+params.

title: Procedural prop factory with parameterized geometry (bell, bellows, crucible, gifts)
text: fx.js defines bellPoly (half-profile + bottom), bellows (pleated leather with hinge angle), GIFT objects (pot, candle, keys, ring, spoon, bracelet) as local-space polygons, heap (randomized items in ellipse), crucibleTop (rim + body + heap), villager silhouettes, rings (expanding sound waves). All use WC.shape/cutAlong/hatch with seeded params. bell() supports crack progression, glow, clapper angle.
how: Create props/woodcut_props.py with classes Bell, Bellows, Crucible, GiftSet, Villager. Each has draw(mask_canvas, color_canvas, t, params) returning stroke lists. Parameterize by scale, seed, animation state (crack, open, tilt). Register in asset bake. Use in compose_woodcut.py for recurring props across episodes.

title: Carve/Print dual-mode rendering
text: A global CARVE flag toggles between 'print' (white areas hatched) and 'carve' (white areas cleared by wide U-cuts) modes. In carve mode, shapes use kind:'u' with wmax; in print mode, kind:'v' with normal hatching. Sky, mountains, snowfield, roofs, spire, pines all respect this flag.
how: Add a style config flag `carveMode` to compose_lab.py. In hatch/shape calls, branch on it: if carve, set kind='u', wmax=13, white=false; else kind='v'. Use for woodcut/engraving aesthetics in Kaise Tech lab look or Puraan Ki Katha myth scenes.

title: Spatial reveal timing (rv function)
text: rv(t0, t1, key, speed) returns {t0,t1,key,speed,jit:0.12}. `key` can be a function (x,y)→[0,1] for spatial progress (e.g., (HOR-y)/(HOR+200) for sky top-down, (y-HOR)/330 for field bottom-up, distance from center for tower). Reveal drives hatch `reveal` param and stroke `t0/dur`.
how: Add `revealTiming(scene, progressFn, t0, t1)` helper in compose_lab.py. Pass progressFn to GSAP timeline as `onUpdate` to drive per-element opacity/stroke-dashoffset. Use for progressive drawing hooks (first 2s) and section transitions.

title: Procedural pine trees with tiered snow caps
text: Pine built from 6 tier polygons (trapezoids with jagged edges). Each tier gets two snow-cap strokes (left/right) following upper edge with U-cuts (kind:'u', seeded). Trunk rect. Whole tree shaped with reveal rv(4.6,5.5, (base-y)/h). Caps drawn as separate strokes after tree reveal.
how: Create `pineFactory(seed, x, base, h)` returning {treeShape, capStrokes[]}. Use in background layers for cold-weather scenes. Snow caps use same `kind:'u'` carve logic. Parameterize tier count, width taper, jitter.

title: Footprint track generation
text: Two trudging tracks from foreground to village: 26 steps each. Position: x = 760 + 180*sin(u*2.2)*(1-u) ± 9*(1-u*0.7), y = 880 - u*260, radius = 7*(1-u*0.7). Each step a short stroke (kind:'u') with seeded jitter. Reveal staggered in carve mode.
how: Add `footprintTrack(start, end, steps, stagger)` to visual grammar library. Returns stroke array with per-step reveal timing. Use for narrative 'journey' shots in Puraan Ki Katha or 'user path' in Kaise Tech. Style as snow/mud/sand via tone function.

title: Sky hatching with horizon glow gradient
text: Sky region: horizontal cuts (dir≈0.012*sin(x*0.002)), tone = 0.08 + 0.78*pow(clamp((y+100)/(HOR+100)), 2.4). Denser toward horizon (sp:12, seg:[90,340], gap:[4,30]). Reveal top-down over 5.0-6.1s. Gamma 1.2 for print pop.
how: Add `skyHatch(horizonY, worldH)` to background module. Returns hatch config with tone/dir/reveal functions. Use as base layer for any outdoor scene. Parameterize horizon glow intensity and hatch density for mood (dawn/dusk/night).

title: Bell tower with animated belfry arch and bell
text: Tower: body (reveal 4.3-5.2 bottom-up), belfry box (4.9-5.3), spire (5.1-5.6 top-down, white, lit left/dark right), finial (appears after 5.5s). Arch polygon with carved rim (offset 4px, kind:'k'). Bell callback injected at render time (o.bell). Spire outline stroke separate.
how: Create `landmarkTower(config)` module returning {body,belfry,spire,arch,finial,drawBell}. Use for temple/church/clock tower establishing shots. Bell animation: scale+rotate on beat, with ring particles. Integrate with beat-synced cuts.

title: Catalog durability guard
text: Before publishing, compare current results.md/stats against the last committed version; abort if any video duration or view count drops to zero (indicates a build run without source media).
how: In publish.py, load git show HEAD:results.md and diff durations/counts; if any entry loses data, halt and alert. Mirrors their catalog.json dur check.

title: Process wording filter
text: Scan scripts, brain.jsonl, and lessons for internal process terms (PRODUCTION_LOG, 返修, 定稿版, 审片, reviewer note, vN 的意见) and strip or flag before any public-facing output.
how: Add a lint step in plan.py and research.py that runs a regex over generated text; replace matches with generic placeholders or raise a warning in the Telegram approval.

title: Required asset checklist per video
text: Enforce a publish gate: every video must have thumbnail.jpg, cover.jpg, <slug>.srt, metadata.json (title, description, tags, duration), and voice_alignment.json. Missing any blocks auto-approve.
how: Extend preflight.py with a checklist validator; integrate into publish.py approval flow. Mirrors their per-style poster, styleframe, CREDITS, catalog entry requirement.

title: Asset manifest with SHA256
text: Pack versioned asset bundles (TTS voices, background packs, music beds) into .tar archives and write a manifest (assets.json) with file name, size, and SHA256. Upload only changed bundles to object storage; verify on deploy.
how: Add pack() and verify() steps to doctor.py or a new release.py; define PACKS dict for our asset types (kokoro-onnx, muse-bg-pack, music-bed-v1); store manifest in repo; upload to Cloudflare R2 via API.

title: Web-optimized transcode pipeline
text: Generate 720p H.264/AAC cuts with -preset slow -crf 24 -maxrate 2M -bufsize 4M -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart; copy AAC audio if already AAC else encode 256k AAC. Only rebuild when source film is newer.
how: Add web_cuts() to render pipeline after mux.py; output to .release/web/<slug>.mp4; use in publish.py for YouTube uploads (when ready) and as fallback for slow connections.

title: Pre-commit hygiene gates
text: Automated checks on committed files: reject >5 MB, local paths (/Users/, /home/, /private/tmp/), secrets (API keys, tokens), orphan images not referenced by any code/doc, unreachable files, and process wording (PRODUCTION_LOG, review terms).
how: Extend doctor.py with hygiene() scanning git-staged files; integrate into preflight.py; fail render on errors, warn on orphans/process words. Reuse their regex patterns for secrets and local paths.

title: frame.md design inversion
text: frame.md translates a web design system (design.md) into video-ready tokens: same atoms, but rewritten for camera scale, frame-safe composition, and agent-composable numbers. Includes 10 ready templates (Biennale Yellow, BlockFrame, Cobalt Grid, etc.) with light/dark palettes, typography scales, and component patterns.
how: Adopt frame.md for each page (Kaise Tech, Puraan Ki Katha, Aage Suno) to version-control visual identity; feed the tokens into compose.py/compose_lab.py style configs so Gemini planner respects brand rules automatically.

title: HyperFrames agent skills for video patterns
text: Six core skills encode video-specific patterns generic LLMs miss: /hyperframes (render contract + work loop), /hyperframes-registry (450 blocks), /media-use (free/HeyGen media sourcing), /reverse-any-video (deconstruct existing videos), /style-sampling (5 proven styles), /hyperframes-cli (lint/check/render). Skills version-lock to CLI release.
how: Install core skills in our planner/editor agents (`npx hyperframes skills update`); reference skill patterns in plan.py prompts (e.g., caption timing rules from /hyperframes, block reuse from /hyperframes-registry); schedule weekly skill refresh in doctor.py.

title: Reverse-any-video workflow for reference analysis
text: Pro skill: upload any MP4 → agent reconstructs as editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI footage) with frame-by-frame verification. Outputs composition HTML + assets + timelines.
how: Use in scout.py to deconstruct viral Shorts in our niches; extract hook structure, pacing, visual grammar into playbook.md; feed findings into ideas.py scoring and plan.py scene templates.

title: Frame adapter pattern for multi-runtime animation
text: Animations plug in via seek-by-frame adapters: GSAP (primary), CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, custom. Root timeline must be paused on window.__timelines[compId]; child timelines must NOT be paused. Enables mixing runtimes in one composition.
how: Document adapter rules in our motion guide; allow compose_lab.py to embed Three.js 3D scenes or Lottie icons alongside GSAP; ensure all timelines follow pause contract for deterministic seek.

title: Catalog block installation via CLI
text: 450+ installable blocks/components (transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves) via `npx hyperframes add <name>`. Each block is editable source HTML+GSAP; components include demo.html for instant preview. Catalog drift check validates determinism.
how: Replace hand-built lab-look components (stat counters, UI panels, line charts, chat bubbles) with catalog equivalents; add `hyperframes add` step in compose_lab.py asset prep; run `bun run check:catalog-drift` in doctor.py for regression safety.

title: AWS Lambda distributed rendering SDK
text: @hyperframes/aws-lambda deploys a render stack (API Gateway + Lambda + S3) driven from local CLI or CI. Scales frame capture horizontally; same deterministic output. Free tier covers thousands of minutes.
how: Add `hyperframes render --cloud` fallback in publish.py when local queue > 10 videos; store Lambda URL in env; use for burst renders (festival specials, breaking news) without provisioning servers.

title: Media-use skill for systematic asset sourcing
text: Skill covers music, SFX, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar video, transcripts, cutouts, color grades — using HeyGen models or free local tools (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations). Includes mixing placed audio and fixing dark/flat footage.
how: Replace ad-hoc image/clip fetching in compose.py/compose_lab.py with skill-recommended prompts and free-tool parameters; add SFX cue library from skill to mix.py; use footage-fix recipes for low-quality generated clips.

title: Player component for instant preview embeds
text: @hyperframes/player is a `<hyperframes-player>` web component that plays rendered MP4s with frame-accurate seeking, keyboard shortcuts, and no external deps. Can embed in our dashboard (Today, Runs, Approvals) for instant QC.
how: Add player to stats.py dashboard for each rendered video; wire frame-accurate scrub to review.py alignment checks; use in Telegram approval flow via web preview link.

title: Visualization Registry (Show-Don't-Tell Routing)
text: Four-class routing table: ui-recreate (faithful mock of real UI), ui-analog (honest metaphor: panel, meter, pipeline), terminal (CLI command + result), checklist (last resort, ≤6 rows). Each surface has proven choreography (e.g., Studio editor: clips drop/stack, drag-snap with green flash). Never invent fake UI.
how: In research.py/scout.py, after topic selection, route each beat through a local visualization-registry.md (mirror structure). In compose_lab.py, add component library for each surface type (editor timeline, inspector panel, render panel, terminal strip). Enforce: if no registry entry exists, fall back to checklist scene.

title: Cut-the-Curve Seam Catalog (5 Techniques + 2 In-Scene)
text: Five seam techniques with exact parameters: (1) Zoom-Through (Z forward, 1→1.2→0.75→1, 10px blur, 0.2s/0.5s), (2) Inverse Zoom (Z back, 1→0.8→1.25→1, arrival beats only), (3) Cut-the-Curve (X/Y default LEFT, ±230px/12% frame, mirrored power4.in/out, early fade), (4) Waterfall Cut (word-level, stagger +0.022s, entry ignite 0.35 opacity, gaps ×0.84 decay), (5) Rack-Focus Blur-Cut (visible cut, peak 8-12px blur, power2.in/out, ≤1 per 8s). Plus Waterfall Entry (Y from below, binary 0→1 opacity, weight-varied travel/duration) and Nudge Curve (slow-fast-slow 10/65/25% distance, 20/18/62% time, tail ≥3× ramp-in).
how: In compose_lab.py, replace ad-hoc transitions with a transition selector that picks from this catalog per seam. Add ledger.json generation in plan.py (cut time, axis, dir, technique). Port seam-stamp.mjs to Python to auto-write GSAP wrapper tweens. Add seam-gate verification in review.py (check exit moving, entry mid-flight, speed match, zero overlap, Z-sign scan).

title: Oversized Cursor as Eye-Carrier
text: Full-frame cursor = 7cqw (~134px at 1920). Always enters from off-screen (top:115%) on one continuous vector (power3.out, 0.4-0.92s). Tip-targeting: land arrow tip (transformOrigin 21% 14%) on target center. Click = asymmetric compress/expand (scale 0.84, 0.1s in / 0.22s out). Click ignites next beat same-frame. During long beats, cursor drifts aside (0.5-0.9s power2.out). Exits physically (off-frame power2.in or cut-the-curve handoff to next scene).
how: Add cursor component to compose_lab.py (SVG, drop-shadow, z-index 20). In plan.py, for any UI/demo beat, insert cursor-led action: entry → travel → click → reaction → drift/exit. For cross-scene handoff, implement cut-the-curve cursor handoff (last 0.3s of scene A starts next scene's cursor path; scene B gsap.set at handoff pose, continues matched velocity).

title: Changelog Video Pipeline (Weekly Branded Shorts)
text: End-to-end: bootstrap from skill assets (fonts, bg-pattern.mp4, bgm.mp3, master-skeleton.html) → parse changelog (45-60s budget, ≤3 items/theme) → route via visualization registry → two-layer script tokens → Annie VO (pinned voice ID) → align captions → build on scaffold (brand tokens, glass cards, one green moment/scene) → ledger.json → seam-stamp → seam-gate verify → caption presence gate (sample 4 frames across VO) → render. Non-negotiable: always copy master-skeleton, never prior video's index.html.
how: Adapt for our scout.py weekly digest: create a changelog-video skill in skills/ with our brand assets. In scout.py, when playbook.md has ≥3 themes, trigger this pipeline. Use our Gemini TTS (Charon) with align-captions fallback to Whisper. Enforce caption presence gate in review.py. Output to projects/active/weekly-<range>/ for Telegram approval.

title: Skills Manifest with Content Hashes
text: skills-manifest.json tracks each skill directory with a content hash (e.g., hyperframes: e8373632c84a7187, 81 files) and file count. Regenerated on skill change via gen-skills-manifest.ts; re-staged in pre-commit. CI enforces manifest sync. Internal skills (metadata.internal: true) excluded from marketplace but auto-discovered by local agents.
how: Create skills/ directory for our reusable patterns (caption-overlay, motion-doctrine, lab-look-components, etc.). Add generate-skills-manifest.py that hashes each skill's content (excluding .git). Add pre-commit job to regenerate and git add manifest.json. In doctor.py, verify manifest matches disk before each run. Tag internal skills for studio-only use.

title: Two-layer script tokens (display vs spoken)
text: Script lines are arrays of tokens: bare strings = identical display/spoken; objects = {display: 'JSON', spoken: 'jay-sawn'}. One line = one caption phrase (≤40 chars). Build vo-spoken.txt by joining spoken forms; captions render display layer. Eliminates TTS mispronunciations (CLI→'C L I', JSON→'jay-sawn', OAuth→'oh-auth') while keeping captions clean.
how: In plan.py, change script output to this token format. Add a lexicon.json (see item 2) for standard mappings. Before TTS, expand tokens to spoken text; after TTS, use align-captions logic to map word timestamps back to display tokens for caption rail.

title: TTS lexicon with plain-text phonetics
text: A JSON file mapping display terms → spoken phonetics for HeyGen/Gemini TTS (no SSML). Rules: initialisms spaced (CLI→'C L I'), acronyms respelled (JSON→'jay-sawn', GSAP→'jee-sap'), compounds hyphenated lowercase (ffmpeg→'ff-mpeg', OAuth→'oh-auth'), URLs as 'dot' (hyperframes.heygen.com→'hyperframes dot hey-jen dot com'). Never guess — ask owner, add, listen to generated line.
how: Create knowledge/lexicon.json seeded from the source's lexicon.json. In plan.py/script generation, auto-apply lexicon to technical terms. Add a step in voice gate: if a term lacks lexicon entry, flag for owner review before TTS. Store approved entries back to lexicon.json.

title: Opaque stage ground to prevent white flashes at seams
text: During transitions (cut-the-curve, zoom-through, crossfade) there's a window where both wrapper opacities sum <1. If #root background is transparent, the renderer composites over white → white flash on dark films. Fix: #root { background: var(--canvas-deep, var(--canvas, #000)) }. Verified on Spotify runs. The assembler (our compose.py) must paint this.
how: In compose.py and compose_lab.py, ensure the root container (the main HTML element) has an explicit opaque background CSS rule (black for lab, dark for classic). Add a preflight.py check: parse generated HTML, verify #root or body has background-color set and not transparent.

title: Motion Doctrine: Vector Law & Current
text: Every film picks ONE dominant direction (house default: LEFT = 'next beat'). All ordinary seams use it. Other vectors are RESERVED: UP = elevation/reveal, Z forward = push deeper, Z backward = arrival (something bigger lands), scale-burst = leaving a world. Never run consecutive seams in opposing directions (ping-pong = error). Direction change needs visible cause (click/bounce/impact) or chapter boundary. Axis never trades across cut (x stays x). On Z, direction = sign of scale change: growing = push, shrinking = pull. A receding exit answered by grow-from-small entry is a mirrored vector — the most common violation.
how: In plan.py, add 'current_direction' field (default 'left'). When planner chooses transitions, enforce vector law: exit axis/dir must match entry axis/dir. For Z seams, ensure scale velocity sign matches (both shrinking or both growing). Document reserved vectors in playbook.md for intentional use only.

title: Seam Probe for Ledger Authoring
text: seam-gate.mjs probe --t <cut_time> --project <dir> scans ±0.1s around cut, lists movers with velocity (vx, vy, vscale), opacity, size. Output shows selectors + signs (x-: left, y-: up, scale+: push, scale-: pull). Use to discover true carrier selectors when authoring ledger.json. Run after comp edits (restart preview server first — stale bundle = wrong measurements).
how: Add probe_seam.py wrapper calling node seam-gate.mjs probe. In plan.py, after composing scenes but before finalizing ledger, run probe at each planned cut time to verify carriers and directions. Integrate into preflight.py as 'seam_discovery' step.

title: BeginFrame Deterministic Rendering
text: The 'chrome-headless-shell' is identified as the only Chrome build supporting BeginFrame, which allows the driver to dictate exactly when a frame is painted. This is essential for capturing <video> elements inside HTML compositions without dropped frames or sync drift.
how: We should update our Muse/Cloudflare rendering containers to use chrome-headless-shell instead of standard stable Chrome to ensure frame-perfect sync for video-in-video tech explainers.

title: Cross-Architecture Font Parity
text: Ensures font rendering is identical across ARM64 (Lambda) and x86 (Dev) by comparing JSON font-maps and screenshot hashes. Prevents 'text-overflow' bugs that only appear in the cloud.
how: Run a one-time 'font-audit' comparing our local Muse browser renders vs Cloudflare FLUX outputs to ensure Hinglish/Devanagari characters don't shift or clip in production.

title: Canary Sunset Governance
text: A scheduled task that checks for experimental 'canary' features that have passed their expiration date. Forces the team to either fully integrate or delete 'coming soon' code.
how: Add a 'sunset' field to our experimental visual features (like 3D scenes). If a feature stays in 'beta' for 30 days without a successful render, doctor.py should disable it.

title: Telemetry Suppression in CI
text: Uses HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 to prevent CI runs from polluting usage analytics. Ensures that 'test' renders don't skew our 'real' video production stats.
how: Set an environment variable in our local server and Cloudflare workers to ensure preflight/test renders aren't counted in our stats.py reports.

title: Performance Work-Count Ratcheting
text: Instead of measuring noisy execution time, the system counts 'work units' (number of DOM renders, page loads, and network requests) during a project open. If a code change increases these counts, the build fails.
how: Add a 'work-counter' to compose.py that logs the number of GSAP ticks and Image() loads per Short. If a script change causes a 20% spike in work for the same scene, doctor.py should flag it.

title: Incremental Quality Gate (Fallow)
text: Uses a 'new-only' gate for code complexity and dead-code analysis. Existing legacy issues are ignored, but any NEW issues introduced in a PR fail the build, preventing technical debt from growing.
how: Integrate a 'new-only' lint check in our git hooks. When we update ideas.py or research.py, the check should only fail if the NEW lines add complexity, ignoring old messy code.

title: Flake-Gate Test Sharding
text: Automatically detects changed test files and runs them 10+ times in a loop ('flake-gate') to catch intermittent rendering failures before they reach production.
how: In preflight.py, if a new visual component is detected, render it 5 times with different seeds. If it fails once, reject the asset before the full render starts.

title: Interaction p95 Performance Gate
text: Measures the p95 latency of UI interactions (like timeline scrubbing) in a headless browser. Ensures that the editor/studio remains responsive as the project grows in complexity.
how: In review.py, simulate a 'scrub' of the rendered HyperFrame. If the p95 frame-render time exceeds 16ms (60fps), mark the video for 'optimization' (e.g., flattening layers).

title: Stale draft auto-archive
text: Auto-archive video drafts (idea JSON, script MD, partial renders) older than 14 days with no activity. Move to archive/ folder, log in brain.jsonl, notify owner. Keep workspace clean and brain focused.
how: Add a daily cron (doctor.py extension) that scans workspace/drafts/, checks mtime and git activity, moves stale items to workspace/archive/<date>/, updates brain.jsonl with 'archived' tag, sends Telegram summary.

title: Sharded render performance benchmarks
text: Run 5 benchmark shards (load, fps, scrub, drift, parity) with 3-5 runs each on a standard heavy video; measure frame times, audio sync, render duration, and SSIM vs reference. Fail if any shard regresses >5% from baseline.
how: Add a nightly GitHub Action (or cron job) that renders a fixed complex test video (multiple lab-look scenes, charts, transitions) via compose_lab.py, captures metrics in JSON, compares to stored baselines, and posts a summary to Telegram.

title: Cross-browser render parity gate
text: Test render output in current Chrome and Firefox (or Chrome stable vs beta) using headless browsers; compare key frames with SSIM >0.995. Catch GSAP/CSS rendering differences before they hit production.
how: Extend preflight.py to launch a second headless browser (Playwright Firefox), render the same scene, compute SSIM on 3 key frames (start, middle, end) via Pillow, and block deploy if similarity drops.

title: Bin-packed render job scheduling
text: Maintain a JSON file of historical scene render times (scene_type -> median_seconds). At queue time, pack pending scenes onto workers to minimize makespan (greedy longest-processing-time first). Re-record timings nightly.
how: Modify doctor.py (or a new scheduler) to read/write packages/producer/tests/shard-schedule.json equivalent; when dispatching render units, sort by estimated duration and assign to least-loaded worker.

title: Automated failure artifact bundle
text: On any render failure, automatically zip: failed frame PNGs, browser console logs, TTS alignment JSON, asset manifest, and compose script. Upload to cloud storage (R2/S3) with TTL 7 days; link in Telegram alert.
how: Wrap compose.py and render steps in try/except; on exception, collect artifacts from /tmp/render-<video_id>/, tar.gz, upload via Cloudflare R2 API, post presigned URL to Studio360 Telegram.

title: Immutable render commit pinning
text: Tag every video render with the exact git commit SHA, asset manifest SHA256s, and dependency versions (bun.lock, package.json). Store in video metadata JSON for full reproducibility and audit.
how: In plan.py or render entrypoint, run `git rev-parse HEAD` and `sha256sum assets/manifest.json`; write to output metadata. Verify in review.py that metadata matches current HEAD for non-hotfix renders.

title: Variable system with types, defaults, descriptions, and portrays
text: Each variable declares: `id`, `type` (string|color|enum|image), `role` (content|style), `label`, `description`, `default`, `max` (for strings), `options` (for enum), and optional `portrays` (e.g., `subject_name`, `competitor_name`) for semantic tagging. Enables UI editors and validation.
how: Define a `VariableSpec` dataclass in `studio/schema.py`. Update `brain.jsonl` to store block metadata with these fields. In `plan.py`, validate user-provided variables against specs (type, enum, max length). Use `portrays` to auto-fill from video context (brand name, competitor list).

title: Documentation standards (AGENTS.md) for user-facing guides
text: Strict rules: write for smart general users; explain outcome before implementation; prefer plain words, short examples, screenshots; one component per job (Cards for navigation, Steps for instructions, Tabs for variants, Tables for comparison); no accordions for journeys; cards link to pages not anchors; max two columns; end pages with visible `## Related topics` or `*Next:*` pointer. Verified via `mint validate` and `mint broken-links`.
how: Adopt these rules for our `docs/` (if any) and internal runbooks. Add a `docs/lint.py` that checks Markdown against the component table (e.g., no accordions in troubleshooting). Enforce in PR template. Use for `playbook.md` and `lessons.md` updates from `scout.py` and owner feedback.

title: CLI command to install blocks with assets
text: `npx hyperframes add <block-id>` scaffolds the block's composition HTML and any supporting assets (images, fonts) into the project, ready to mount via data attributes. The command is non-interactive and scriptable.
how: Add `add-block` subcommand to our CLI (or a new `hf` wrapper). It should fetch from our local registry, copy files, and print the mount snippet with `data-variable-values` JSON. Integrate with `doctor.py` to verify installed blocks.

title: FFmpeg feature inventory verification in CI
text: Before rendering, the Windows CI runs `ffmpeg -encoders/-muxers/-demuxers` and asserts required features: libx264, libx265, libvpx-vp9, prores_ks, aac encoders; mp4, mov, webm muxers; image2pipe, rawvideo, mov/mp4 demuxers. Fails fast if a build lacks a codec.
how: Add a `verify_ffmpeg_features()` step in `preflight.py` (or a new `ci_preflight.py`) that shells out to ffmpeg and checks the same lists. Run it in GitHub Actions on every PR and in `doctor.py` before local renders. Log missing features as hard errors.

title: Windows headless render smoke test with canary composition
text: A minimal 8-second 1080p composition (`windows-canary.html`) is rendered on `windows-latest` via the CLI (`hyperframes render --fps 30 --quality draft --workers 2`). The output MP4 is probed with `ffprobe` for exact width, height, fps, and duration (~8s). Proves Chrome, FFmpeg, and the render pipeline work end-to-end on Windows.
how: Create `fixtures/windows-canary.html` (simple animated box). Add a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/windows-render.yml`) that checks out, installs FFmpeg (via shared action), Bun, Node, builds CLI, runs `hyperframes doctor`, scaffolds canary, renders, and verifies with ffprobe. Upload MP4 as artifact.

title: Regression test for reused video segments (issue #574 pattern)
text: A test composition reuses the same 12s source video three times sequentially with different `data-media-start` offsets (0, 4, 8) and `data-duration` 4s each. Rendered at standard quality, the output must be 12s with correct frame accuracy. Catches seek/keyframe bugs when reusing a clip.
how: Add `fixtures/reused-video-test.html` and a script `test_reused_video.py` that generates a 12s test clip with ffmpeg `testsrc2`, renders the composition, and verifies duration + frame count. Run in CI on Windows and Linux. Integrate into `review.py` as an optional gate.

title: Multi-Phone Product Showcase Layout
text: Three floating phone mockups (320×650px) with bezel/notch, staggered entrance: center scales up first (back.out 0.7s), sides fade in then fan out to x=±340px with rotation ±12° (expo.out 1.2s). Each screen shows distinct UI: left motivational (SVG shapes + tagline), center dashboard (avatar, progress ring 2/3, 3 activity bars), right calories graph (area+line+dots). Ambient slow stage scale (1.02 over 3.5s) adds depth.
how: Adapt for Kaise Tech app/feature demos: create a 'trioShowcase' template in compose_lab.py. Use our existing phone bezel SVG, swap screen content via data-driven UI components (progress ring, bar charts, line graphs). Stagger timing matches our 5.5s Short format.

title: Deterministic Rank Interpolation for Bar Races
text: Precompute integer ranks at 10 keyframes/period (K=10). At render time, continuous rank = smoothstep(a + (b-a)*e) where a,b are adjacent keyframe ranks. This guarantees bars never cross without a visible swap, and the swap duration equals one keyframe interval (periodDuration/10). Paint order follows current value so the overtaking bar draws on top.
how: Apply this algorithm in our existing chart components (bar, line) when animating ranked data. Replace any ad-hoc position tweens with rankPosAt(t) for consistent, glitch-free overtakes. No new code needed if we adopt the math in planner prompts.

title: Kinetic Number Counter with Particle Burst
text: Counts $0→$10,000 in 3.16s (linear ease), then snaps to green (#30d158) with text-shadow glow, scale punch (1.06→1.0), full-screen green flash (0.34 opacity), and 62 money icons (bills/coins) bursting from center on deterministic polar layout (angle = i*2.4, 5 rings, clamped to ±865/±465). Icons pop with back.out(2), float, then fall out with power2.in. SFX on separate audio track.
how: Extend our lab look stat counters (compose_lab.py) with a 'countUpBurst' variant. Use the deterministic polar layout for icon bursts (reuse moneySpecs logic). Hook into existing SFX cue system (mix.py) for the flash/burst sync. Keep tabular-nums font-variant for clean counting.

title: Mathematically exact dolly-zoom with depth layers
text: Dolly zoom constraint: d * tan(FOV/2) = constant. In CSS 3D, perspective = focal length (px), tan(FOV/2) = (width/2)/perspective, so perspective/distance = SUBJECT_SCALE (1). Subject at translateZ(0); background arches at -560, -1120, -1720, -2360, -3200px. Camera Z = perspective - distance. Requires preserve-3d and no overflow:hidden on ancestors.
how: In plan.py for 'cinematic depth' shots, specify dolly-zoom with direction/strength. compose_lab.py builds #dz-rig with subject at z=0 and 3+ background layers at negative Z. Use for Kaise Tech 'zooming into chip die' and mythology 'god perspective' shots.

title: Deterministic frame rendering via property setter
text: Drive per-frame camera/transform updates with a setter on the tweened object (camera.u = value) instead of timeline onUpdate; the setter fires on every render including seeks, guaranteeing frame-accurate output for effects like dolly-zoom where perspective must match distance exactly.
how: In compose_lab.py and any 3D camera rigs, replace tl.eventCallback('onUpdate', ...) with a driver object { _u:0, set u(v){ this._u=v; applyCamera(v); } } and tl.to(driver, { u:1, duration, ease }). Ensures preflight.py stills and final render match at any seek.

title: Responsive HUD overlay with CSS custom properties
text: Camcorder HUD uses --hf-camcorder-color, --hf-camcorder-accent, --hf-camcorder-inset (5vmin), --hf-camcorder-font-size (3.7vmin) and vmin units so the REC dot, battery, date, and counter scale cleanly from 1080p to 4K. Battery drawn with ::before/::after pseudo-elements; counter formats seconds to HH:MM:SS on each tick; REC dot blinks at 0.55s interval via opacity toggle.
how: Add a camcorder-hud block to our catalog (compositions/camcorder-hud.html). In compose_lab.py, allow variable injection for color/inset/font-size per video. Use for 'Kaise Tech' lab intros and 'Puraan Ki Katha' vintage camera treatments.

title: Text fragmentation/reassembly for hook reveal
text: Intro title 'Introducing' shatters into 4 remnants (Intro, ducin, g, tro) that scatter with blur, then 5 fragments (blu, e, x, swea, ter) fly in from custom offsets with per-piece carry/settle/lock vectors, finally locking into final wordmark 'blue x sweater' with scaleX corrections. All timed to 0.004s stagger.
how: Add fragmentReveal() helper in compose_lab.py: takes target word, splits into N spans, assigns random-from-center from/to vectors, runs GSAP stagger. Use for Kaise Tech hook titles ('AI', 'GPU', 'LLM') and mythology name reveals.

title: Burst particle system with per-particle custom paths
text: Six orange burst-blocks each follow a 7-keyframe path (source→scatter→drift→select→squeeze→release→fade) with unique coordinate arrays and per-block rotation direction. Star-center scales 0.08→0.16→1 then drifts out. All blocks fade at individual times (2.17/2.33s).
how: Add burstEmitter() in compose_lab.py: takes count, color, pathArray[][{source,scatter,drift,select,squeeze,release,fade}]. Generates divs with clip-path polygons. Use for section transitions in lab look and mythology 'divine intervention' moments.

title: Social card CTA with animated follow button
text: Card (800×430) enters at 9.86s with expo.out scale/blur. Follow button (174×54) at 10.88s scales 0.9→1 with elastic.out(1,0.45), background shifts to #2f2f2f, 'Follow' label cross-fades to 'Following' + checkmark SVG in 0.08s. Cursor taps button at 10.5s.
how: Add socialCardCTA() in thumb.py and compose_lab.py: accepts handle, avatar, name, bio, followAction. Renders card with gradient top bar, avatar ring shadow, bio text. Use for end cards on all three pages; auto-insert channel handle from config.

title: Variable system with validation and defaults for reusable blocks
text: Camera-dolly-zoom declares variables in data-composition-variables JSON (direction enum, strength 1.1-4, subjectDistance 600-3000, easing enum). Script reads via window.__hyperframes.getVariables(), merges with DEFAULTS, clamps/validates with clamp() and oneOf().
how: Extend our block registry (registry/blocks/) to include variable schemas. In compose.py, parse data-variable-values on mount, validate, inject into composition as CSS custom properties or JS constants. Enables one block file to serve multiple videos with different params.

title: Quintic Hermite handoff interpolation
text: Use quintic Hermite (position, velocity, acceleration continuity) to blend between animation phases without jumps. The canopy block computes correction coefficients from finite differences at the handoff time, then applies p(t)=1-10t³+15t⁴-6t⁵ for smooth settling.
how: In compose_lab.py transitions, replace simple ease with quintic Hermite when switching from scripted motion to idle breeze; compute correction at handoff via three samples (t-dt, t, t+dt).

title: Progress LUT for complex speed curves
text: Precompute a Float64Array lookup table (600+ entries) mapping time → accumulated progress for non-linear speed profiles (fast-slow-fast). Evaluate via linear interpolation for O(1) per-frame cost. Used in carousel for cruise/arrive/exit phases.
how: In pace.py or edit timing, build LUT for any variable-speed segment (e.g., beat-synced cuts); store in brain.jsonl for reuse; sample via lerp during render.

title: AE-style cubic Bezier from keyframe data
text: Parse After Effects keyframe JSON (time, value, easeIn/Out speed+influence) into cubic Bezier segments. Solve for parameter s via Newton-Raphson (8 iterations) to get exact value at any time. Supports cumulative (accumulate) and ping-pong modes.
how: Extend motion.py to accept AE keyframe export; use for title animations, camera moves; replace hand-tuned GSAP eases with data-driven curves.

title: Depth-based scaling with perspective boost
text: Project 2D path position onto a depth angle vector; normalize to 0-1; lerp between scaleMin and 100% by scaleDepth factor; apply globalScale and perspectiveBoost. Creates convincing 3D carousel size gradient without 3D engine.
how: Add depthAngle, scaleDepth, scaleMin variables to lab look panels/cards; compute in compose_lab.py per element; use for fake 3D carousels, data walls.

title: Headline reveal via wipe uniform synced to sweep
text: Text reveal driven by two uniforms (uIn, uOut) tracking the sweep's leading/trailing edge. Visible edge stays inside dense leaf band: uIn = clamp((sw1-0.3)/0.52,0,1)*1.1-0.05. Second headline uses uLift for vertical wipe.
how: In lab look title cards, bind text opacity/clip to sweep progress uniforms; compute in renderAt() from master timeline; ensures text never appears in empty space.

title: Alpha-aware depth prepass for post-process DOF
text: Before BokehPass, swap all materials to MeshDepthMaterial with alphaTest matching source material; render depth texture; restore materials. Preserves alpha cutouts (leaf edges) in depth buffer so blurred background doesn't bleed into foreground text.
how: If adopting Three.js blocks, add depth prepass in render loop; for 2D lab look, simulate via CSS filter on duplicated layer with clip-path; document in visual QA checklist.

title: Seeded per-element breeze with independent periods
text: Each retained leaf gets unique mulberry32 seed (0x62726565 ^ batchPrime + indexPrime). Breeze params: phase/phase2/phase3, rate, driftX/Y/Z, depth, tiltX/Y, roll, turn, arrival. Avoids synchronized rocking; scales with retainedBreeze variable.
how: Apply to any idle animation (HUD panels, floating props, particle systems): generate per-element seed from global seed + index; store breeze params in brain.jsonl; drive via single time uniform.

title: GPU warm-up before readiness gate
text: Render the composition at 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 of duration during initialization to force shader compilation, texture uploads, and geometry processing before the first visible frame. Call renderer.getContext().finish() to flush GPU commands.
how: Add warmGpu() in HyperFrames render pipeline after compile(); await renders at fractional times; integrate into doctor.py preflight to catch GPU stalls early.

title: Semantic Variable Portrays for Asset Selection
text: Each variable declares portrays: ["subject_image"] (or other tags). Enables automated asset pickers to match semantics (e.g., "person", "diagram", "map") instead of generic "image". Defaults point to CDN assets with SHA-stable URLs.
how: Extend ideas.py/research.py asset fetch to use portrays tags. Add portrays field to our style config JSON variables. Tag brain.jsonl assets with portrays for smarter reuse.

title: Staggered Entry with Lead Time
text: Entry animation: each of n cards starts at ringStart + i*(entryStaggerTotal/n) - entryLead, with entryDuration and power3.out ease. Negative starts get partial progress (tail ease). Cards fade from autoAlpha 0, scale 0.72 → 1. Converge-from-center variant scales position toward center.
how: Integrate into compose_lab.py scene-intro system. Add entryStaggerTotal, entryLead, entryDuration to scene spec. Use for multi-element reveals (bullet points, character entrances, data rows).

title: Orbit Rig for Spherical Distributions
text: orbitRig() places n items on sphere (golden-angle spiral) with radius, spinTurns (x/y/z), rotationX/Y/Z, perspectiveBoost. Scale varies with distance to camera (scaleMax→scaleMin). Items behind camera (z<=camZ*0.92) hidden. Jitter (1% per odd index) breaks symmetry.
how: Add orbitRig to compose_lab.py for 3D spherical layouts (globe data points, concept clusters). Expose radius, spinTurns, perspectiveBoost. Use for Puraan Ki Katha cosmology visuals or Kaise Tech architecture diagrams.

title: Chained Drive for Cumulative/PingPong Loops
text: chainedDrive() wraps aeCurve; if cumulative (net delta > 1e-6) it accumulates cycle offset each period, else pingpongs. Drives Move Carousel, Rotation X/Y/Z seamlessly across 6s composition.
how: Add to motion/drives.py. Use for any looping parameter: background drift, HUD sweeps, ambient particle flow. Configure via keyframe JSON in block data.

title: End Fade by Path Percentile
text: For open paths, cards near start/end (pct < endFade or > 1-endFade) fade linearly over endFade (0.06 = 6% of path). Prevents pop-in/out at path seams.
how: Add to motion/path_rig.py as end_fade_alpha(pct, endFade). Apply in any path-based layout (map routes, timeline) where cards enter/exit frame.

title: Text drift easing: linear-power blend
text: Drift x(t) = (1−k)×(1−(1−t)^p) + k×t where k=linear (default 0.35), p=power (default 3). Gives subtle curved drift that feels organic but never overshoots. Applied to word-container x-offset after word-reveal stagger.
how: Add `drift_ease(linear=0.35, power=3)` to caption.py GSAP easing map; use in kinetic title and sentence-caption animations for Hinglish/English shorts.

title: Billboarded Card Camera-Facing Rotation
text: For each card at (x,y,z), compute yaw = atan2(cx−x, −(camZ−z)) and pitch = −atan2(cy−y, hypot(cx−x, camZ−z)) in degrees. Apply as rotateY(yaw) rotateX(pitch) so cards always face camera. Includes behind-camera culling: visible = false when z ≤ camZ×0.92.
how: Use in compose_lab.py for any 3D label/card system (HUD panels, mythological info cards, tech spec callouts). Add culling to avoid rendering back-facing cards.

title: Squeeze Wrapper for Independent Entry/Exit Scale
text: Wrap all cards in a 'squeeze' div (inside the 3D group) that receives entry/exit scale animations separately from the main orbit group. Allows cards to pop in (0.72→1) while orbit continues, and whole carousel to scale down on outro without affecting card billboarding.
how: In compose_lab.py orbit renderer, create squeeze div as child of group; apply entry stagger to squeeze children, outro scale to squeeze itself.

title: BuildProgress Velocity Clamping via BoostCap
text: Arrive velocity vIn = min(max(cruise·arriveMul, arriveMin), cruise+boostCap). Exit velocity vOut = min(max(cruise·exitMul, exitMin), cruise+boostCap). Prevents extreme speed spikes when arriveMul/exitMul are high. Default boostCap=0.5 (50% above cruise).
how: Add boostCap parameter to pace.py progress builder; set per-block in style config. Guards against jarring motion in fast-paced tech shorts where cruise is high.

title: Distance-Eased Center-Symmetric Y-Tilt
text: Produce a ribbon-like curvature on horizontal carousels by tilting cards around their Y-axis based on distance from center: `rotY = cubicEase(abs(x - cx), 0, maxDist, 0, maxAngle) * (x < cx ? -1 : 1)`. Cards dynamically turn inward toward the focal viewer and flatten out dead center.
how: In `compose_lab.py`, apply dynamic `rotateY` transforms during horizontal card cascades to give flat cards natural focal convergence.

title: Composition embedding via data attributes
text: Blocks mount via <div data-composition-id="..." data-composition-src="..." data-start="0" data-duration="6" data-track-index="1" data-width="1920" data-height="1080" data-variable-values='{...}'>. Enables timeline composition without code changes.
how: Update publish.py/compose.py to generate master index.html with data-attribute composition mounting. Each scene becomes a composable block. doctor.py can validate data attributes. Enables A/B testing by swapping variable values.

title: Dual text layers with card-overlap clip-path masking
text: Two textline divs (above/below cards) with clip-path: above.cards-over-right gets inset(0 50% 0 0) (right half visible), above.cards-over-left gets inset(0 0 0 50%) (left half). Cards render between layers. Words split into spans with overflow:hidden for mask reveal.
how: Modify compose_lab.py text rendering: when cards_over_side set, generate two textline containers with clip-path. Place cards group between them in DOM. Word spans get xPercent animation for reveal. Works for any card-based scene.

title: Hard cut with scaled outro transition
text: At cutAt=3s: text scales 1→0.5 over 0.77s (power2.in), images scale 1→0.35 after 0.154s delay. Outro line scales 1.4→1.0 over 0.378s (power2.out) starting at cutAt. Matched to 'images exit velocity 2.11 scale/s' for continuity.
how: Add ending/outro config to scene spec. In compose_lab.py, create GSAP timeline with cutAt marker. Animate textLayers scale and squeeze group scale. Outro renders in separate clip div (data-start=cutAt). Preflight checks outro fits within duration.

title: Deterministic render at 2× with scaler transform
text: Composition authored at 3840×2160 (comp.width/height). Root scaler applies transform: scale(outWidth/comp.width) = 0.5. All positions, paths, card sizes authored in 2× space. Guarantees sub-pixel accuracy; final encode is single 1920×1080 pass. Camera zoom = 5669.29 (≈ 50mm equivalent at 2×).
how: Update compose_lab.py to author at 2× target resolution (configurable). Add scaler div wrapper. Adjust cameraZoom = comp.width * 1.48. Ensure ffmpeg uses -vf scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos for final encode. Improves text/card edge sharpness.

title: Variable system with 'portrays' for asset auto-selection
text: Each image variable declares portrays:['subject_image']. Registry passes imageVars[] + textVars{line1,line2} + speedVar. At runtime, variables override defaults; images are fetched, decoded, naturalWidth/Height measured, then fed to rig. Text variables split on whitespace to drive word arrays.
how: Extend ideas.py/research.py to output 'portrays' tags per asset. In compose_lab.py, read variable manifest, fetch/decode assets, measure dims, inject into DATA.cards before rig init. Enables 'swap subject images' without code changes.

title: 3D Carousel Block for Multi-Image Showcases
text: A reusable 6-second 1920×1080 block: 12 image cards on a closed Bezier path under a 3D camera (perspective ~5669px). Cards rotate toward center (yAngle3d −70/−120°), scale by depth (scaleDepth 57–130%, scaleMin −120% to −45%), and stagger entry (0.45s total, 0.55s each). Variables: 12 image slots + speed (0.25–3×) + background color. Renders at 2× (3840×2160) then scales down for sharpness.
how: Add compose_carousel_vision.py using this HTML/JS as template. Expose image1–12, speed, background via our variable system (portrays=["subject_image"]). Integrate into plan.py as a 'carousel' scene type for Kaise Tech product roundups or Puraan Ki Katha character galleries.

title: Card Inner/Outer 3D Structure with preserve-3d
text: Outer .card: position absolute, will-change: transform, backface-visibility: visible. Inner .card-inner: 100%×100%, border-radius, box-shadow, overflow hidden, background white. Image inside with object-fit: cover. Stage has transform-style: preserve-3d and perspective. Enables true 3D rotation (rotateY/rotateX) without flattening. z-index fallback for 2D mode (n−i).
how: Add card_3d() helper in visuals/cards.py generating this DOM structure. Use for any flip/reveal: tech spec cards, mythology story beats, before/after comparisons. Ensures clean 3D transforms in our HyperFrames renders; works with existing Ken Burns and lab looks.

title: Image fitting logic: fitBox or imageHeight
text: If look.imageHeight set: scale to that height preserving aspect. Else if look.fitBox (1500): scale = fitBox/max(w,h). Card centered via marginLeft=-w/2, marginTop=-h/2. No CSS object-fit needed; img uses object-fit:cover inside .card-inner.
how: Standardize in compose_lab.py image prop: add fitBox (default 1500) and imageHeight (optional). Use for all card/photo blocks. Ensures consistent sizing across aspect ratios.

title: Header morph: segmented control → actions pill
text: On send: segmented control fades/scales out (0.16s); right button widens 44→108px (0.26s power2.out); action icons (compose, dots) fade in (0.18s). Voice icon fades out. All triggered at same tGo beat.
how: Create reusable UI-transition component in compose_lab.py for mode switches (e.g., light/dark lab, map/detail). Parameterize widths, icons, durations.

title: Suggestion chips cascade entry (waterfall, weight-ordered)
text: Three suggestion chips enter with 0.09s stagger, 0.42s power3.out. Cleared on first keystroke with 0.04s stagger reverse. First keystroke also grows composer height 48→92px (0.24s).
how: Use for hook variations in ideas.py: generate 3 chip-style hooks; animate cascade-in on scene start; dismiss on first visual beat. Add to lab-look hook library.

title: Table assembly row-by-row with staggered word reveal
text: Table header + rule appear, then each row: height expands (0.22s), emoji/icon fades (0.14s), words cascade (0.09s each, 0.028s stagger), chip fades (0.2s), rule draws (0.12s), scroll to row anchor (0.72s). Row step 0.7s.
how: Add table-block to compose_lab.py for comparison videos (AI tools, myth weapons). Build rows from variable arrays; drive via GSAP timeline with rowStep parameter.

title: Font embedding via @font-face for cross-platform deterministic rendering
text: Inter embedded as 'ChatUI' family (400/500/600 woff2) with font-display:block. Apple Color Emoji local fallback. Ensures identical glyph rasterization regardless of OS fonts.
how: Add to HyperFrames base template: bundle Noto Sans Devanagari + Inter woff2; declare @font-face with fixed family names. Update style config to reference embedded families only.

title: Collapse reasoning steps into a summary chip
text: In simulated AI-app scenes, show the working steps (thinking line, search query, tool rows) as they run, then collapse them into one chip such as '2 steps' the moment the answer starts streaming. It proves the AI checked something, keeps the answer readable in a 9:16 frame, and gives the eye a beat before the payoff. Collapse one group at a time.
how: Add a collapse_to field to the scene plan in plan.py (e.g. '2 steps') and handle it in compose_lab.py: shrink the tool rows to a chip at the timestamp the answer's first line appears, reusing the existing typewriter/anchor code for the streamed answer.

title: Gap-on-child rule for collapsing blocks
text: When animating a block to height 0, box-sizing:border-box keeps the element's own padding, so the collapsed block still shows a gap and stacked rows drift apart. Put all vertical gaps on an inner child and animate only the wrapper's height; height 0 then truly collapses. Keep the gap in one CSS variable so the tween target and the bullet-marker offset always use the same number.
how: In compose_lab.py's chat-bubble and tool-row components, wrap each block in an .abox with overflow:hidden, move padding-top to the child, and animate the wrapper height. Verify in preflight.py that a collapsed row has zero rendered height and no residual gap.

title: Cinemagraph: one living region over a frozen still
text: A still photo stays frozen while exactly one region keeps moving: base = freeze-frame still, moving layer = looping video or procedural canvas revealed through a feathered mask (radial-gradient ellipse, 55% opaque to 78% transparent). Keep the loop seamless by giving every animated element an integer number of cycles that divides the clip duration, so the frame at t=DUR equals the frame at t=0. One living region per frame; two reads as a GIF.
how: Add a cinemagraph mode to compose_lab.py: freeze the Muse/FLUX still as base, overlay a looping clip (steam, rain, flame) inside the masked window, and drive it from the GSAP timeline (no requestAnimationFrame) so preflight stills match the render. Use for Puraan Ki Katha (lamp flame, mist) and Kaise Tech (server fan, screen glow).

title: Fonts-ready gate before any DOM measurement
text: Measured DOM animations break if you measure before webfonts load: fallback metrics give wrong line counts (a 7-line paragraph clipped to 6). Build the timeline once synchronously so it exists at parse time, then rebuild after document.fonts.ready, restoring natural layout (height:auto, opacity 1) before re-measuring. Never correct a natural-layout measurement arithmetically — re-measure in the state the tween will play in.
how: In compose_lab.py and preflight.py, await document.fonts.ready before any offsetTop/offsetHeight measurement or layout audit; if fonts are not ready, fail preflight with 'fonts not ready' instead of rendering. Add a regression test using a Devanagari fallback face.

title: FOV Aspect-Bounded 3D Camera Fit
text: To guarantee dynamic 3D cards or slabs fit vertically and horizontally inside any viewport (such as 9:16 Shorts) at a target fill ratio (e.g. 78%), calculate camera distance as max(slabH / 2 / tan(vfov / 2) / fill, slabW / 2 / (tan(vfov / 2) * aspect) / fill). This avoids manual camera placement when slab dimensions vary based on content lines.
how: Implement in our 3D template generator within compose_lab.py to auto-position the Three.js camera for vertical 1080x1920 mobile viewport framing.

title: Line-diff LCS for code state transitions
text: Split tokens into lines (by \n). Compute LCS dynamic programming (dp[i][j] = max match length). Walk dp to emit ops: same/del/add. Used in code-morph to render diff lines (red/green backgrounds) or to know which whole lines are new/removed for scene crossfade.
how: Implement lineDiff(a, b) in ideas.py/research.py when comparing code snippets for 'before/after' shorts. Also use in compose_lab.py to auto-generate diff overlays for refactor explanations.

title: Token-level code morph with FLIP
text: Bake Shiki-highlighted code states into keyed token arrays (unique key per token). Render both states invisibly, measure bounding rects per key, then animate transform (x/y) and opacity via GSAP: matching tokens glide, new tokens fade in at 45% progress, removed tokens fade out. Line-level LCS diff handles added/removed whole lines.
how: Add a Shiki build step in compose_lab.py to emit window.__TOKENS JSON for each code snippet. Create a new HyperFrames block (code-morph.html pattern) that reads baked tokens, builds scenes per state, and registers a paused GSAP timeline. Use in Kaise Tech refactor demos.

title: Seeded mulberry32 PRNG for deterministic particles
text: mulberry32(seed) returns a fast 32-bit PRNG: a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0; t = imul(a ^ a>>>15, 1|a); t = (t + imul(t ^ t>>>7, 61|t)) ^ t; return (t ^ t>>>14) >>> 0 / 2^32. Used for particle origin (x,y,z), delay, and any jitter. Seed = block.seed * 2654435761 >>> 0 ensures per-block uniqueness.
how: Replace any Math.random() in particle systems (compose_lab.py, particle-pool) with this mulberry32 factory. Store seed in block config (brain.jsonl). Guarantees identical particle layouts across renders — critical for preflight/review gates.

title: Offscreen canvas → Three.js texture pipeline
text: drawCodeToCanvas(state, {fontPx, lineH, padX, padY, weight, transparent, bg}) returns {canvas, W, H, lines, lineH, padY, fontPx}. Canvas drawn once after document.fonts.ready. getImageData() samples glyph pixels for particle targets or feeds CanvasTexture for lit 3D slab/dissolve effects. No runtime text layout.
how: Extract drawCodeToCanvas() into shared util (hyperframes/utils/code-canvas.js). In compose_lab.py, call during asset bake: render code to offscreen canvas, save PNG + metadata (token rects, line count). Blocks load PNG + metadata, skipping Shiki at render time. Cuts render CPU.

title: Shader particle color lerp: flight → true color
text: Fragment shader: vColor = token color from attribute. Flight color = vColor + vec3(0.32)*(1.0-vP) (brighter, whiter). Landed color = vColor. Final color = mix(flight, landed, vP). Alpha = smoothstep(0.25, 0.02, r2) * (0.7 + 0.3*vP). Particles pop bright mid-flight, settle to exact syntax highlight.
how: Add to our particle shaders (compose_lab.py particle system). Pass token color per particle via attribute. Drive vP = progress uniform (0→1). Gives code particles the 'lab' aesthetic: data resolving from noise.

title: Threshold Dissolve Progress Overshoot
text: In multi-octave noise dissolve shaders using smoothstep(noise - edge, noise + edge, progress), tweening progress strictly to 1.0 leaves residual unresolved noise specks at high-octave crests. Always overshoot the target progress value to 1.0 + edge (e.g. 1.15 when edge is 0.12) so all pixels fully resolve to crisp text before the hold.
how: Apply in GLSL dissolve shaders in `compose.py` / `compose_lab.py` by setting tween end values to 1.0 + uEdgeWidth.

title: Target Line Center-Lock and Dim
text: Center a target line within a long code or terminal block: compute delta dy = surfaceHeight * 0.5 - (lineTop + lineHeight * 0.5 - surfaceTop), tween both code surface and gutter container y to dy with power2.inOut ease. Concurrently fade non-target lines to 0.35 opacity and fade in an accent highlight box (border-left 3px, low-opacity fill) around the target line.
how: Add to `compose_lab.py` terminal and code widgets to spotlight specific config/code lines during Hinglish tech explainers instead of static truncated text.

title: Static Flat Plate Handoff for Tiled Meshes
text: Tiled and segmented 3D surfaces frequently produce subpixel hairline gaps during static holds. Render a single unsegmented flat background plate covering the viewport during rest phases (t <= firstMotion and t >= lastMotion), hiding the segmented mesh. Toggle visibility only during active wave motion to ensure perfectly seamless static frames.
how: Implement in `compose_lab.py` grid and tile reveal components, placing a flat full-resolution snapshot plate over the stage until animation starts.

title: Ink-Masked Cell Flip Partitioning
text: For grid tile text reveals, render typography to an offscreen canvas and count non-zero alpha pixels per cell bounding box. Cells containing ink pixels execute full 180° flips and damped bounce oscillation, while blank negative-space cells execute only subdued radial tilt without flipping, preserving layout readability and reducing layout thrash.
how: In `compose_lab.py` kinetic headline cards, sample canvas alpha per tile to partition active versus background cells before driving GSAP timelines.

title: VS Code Theme Token-to-CSS Variable Mapping
text: Map standard VS Code theme JSON definitions directly into CSS custom variables (--editor-bg, --gutter-fg, --token-keyword, --token-function, etc.). An applyTheme helper takes theme JSON objects and applies root CSS properties, allowing coding snippets to instantly adopt authentic VS Code colorways (Dark Modern, Dark 2026, Solarized) without bespoke CSS rewriting.
how: In compose_lab.py, add a theme loader helper that maps VS Code token dictionary colors to root CSS variables for code container blocks in Kaise Tech tech/AI explainers.

title: Orthogonal Property Separation for Typing Carets
text: Prevent typing animations from interfering with cursor blinking by decoupling animated CSS properties. Run a continuous step-eased yoyo tween on cursor opacity across the full scene duration, while moving the cursor coordinates via discrete tl.set() calls on x and y derived from the target character's getBoundingClientRect offset.
how: In compose_lab.py terminal and code typing animations, decouple cursor position updates from opacity blinking so position updates don't reset or cancel the blink tween.

title: Synchronized Active-Line and Terminal Reveal Rig
text: Stage realistic IDE showcases using a 3-act workbench sequence: 1) animate a high-contrast active-line highlight strip and active line number jumping vertically to each line before character reveal; 2) slide up an integrated bottom terminal panel (y: 140 -> 0) after code completes to display execution outputs; 3) apply a 3D perspective yaw (rotateY: -10deg) to present the result.
how: In compose_lab.py, wrap code snippets in a structured workbench container with an active-line backdrop and execution terminal slide-up timed to script resolution beats.

title: Beat pulse envelope from precomputed samples
text: Accept a comma-separated 0-1 envelope string (evenly spaced across clip duration). At time t, linearly interpolate between the two nearest samples. Empty envelope falls back to a flat pulse value. No audio analysis at render time — envelope is precomputed offline (e.g., from beat detection on the music bed).
how: Extend mix.py or a new audio_analysis.py to output pulseEnvelope JSON for each music bed. Pass it as a variable to shader blocks (cosmic-orb, future beat-synced visuals). In block JS, parse once, then sample via pulseAt(t) in the property-setter draw loop.

title: Pre-baked syntax tokens for deterministic highlighting
text: Run Shiki (or equivalent) at authoring time to produce a token array: each token has key, content, color, fontStyle bitmask. Store in window.__TOKENS. At render, reconstruct spans from this baked data — no runtime syntax highlighting, zero layout shift, deterministic across machines.
how: Add a CLI step (or extend ideas.py/research.py) that takes code snippets, runs Shiki via Node, outputs token JSON. Store in brain.jsonl or alongside the script. The code_typing block reads window.__TOKENS.feature.states[0].tokens directly.

title: CSS custom properties for block theming at runtime
text: Editorial Flash uses --hf-editorial-flash-wash/warm/cool; Data Chart uses --bg-color/--text-color on host. Allows per-instance recoloring without code changes. HyperFrames variables map to these via style.setProperty.
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, define CSS custom properties for all color tokens (brand, accent, bg, text). Pass HyperFrames variables to root.style.setProperty('--token', value). Update thumb.py to respect them.

title: Blender-baked motion import for deterministic 3D camera/object paths
text: Export camera/object keyframes from Blender as JSON (position, quaternion, FOV per frame) and replay in Three.js with basis conversion. Cuboid Carousel uses 200-frame Blender choreography (MOTION object) with camera settle, handheld, and hero breakaway phases. Enables complex, art-directed 3D moves that render identically every time.
how: Add a Blender export script (Python) that writes motion JSON. In compose_lab.py, load MOTION data and drive Three.js objects/camera via render(t) function. Use camera offset interpolation for custom start/end positions.

title: Staggered data chart animation with live counters
