how: Use for 'Inspiration' wall in dashboard: show latest 20 renders as drifting cards. Implement with CSS transform + requestAnimationFrame, IntersectionObserver to pause offscreen. Add global pause toggle persisted in localStorage. Ensure focus-visible centers card.

title: Single audible video coordination via capture-phase 'play' listener
text: Global document.addEventListener('play', handler, true) detects any video going unmuted. It pauses and mutes all other videos in the component. Used in day-list, remix-shelf, film-rows, replica-compare. Ensures only one sound source page-wide.
how: Add to dashboard layout: a single global listener that finds all video elements with data-audio='true' and mutes/pauses siblings when one plays unmuted. Tag our preview videos with data-audio. Prevents cacophony when user opens multiple approvals.

title: Workflow chooser: source-material-first routing with compact looping proof
text: 12 routes each show a 5-8s muted loop of the output type (product launch, explainer, PR video, etc.) with 'Bring a …' copy. Click goes to full guide. No preview = empty span (not black box). Reduced motion shows poster only.
how: Adapt for our 'New Video' wizard: show 6 workflow cards (Tech Explainer, Mythology Story, General Story, PR-to-Video, Music Video, Meme/Parody) with looping 720p previews. Copy: 'Bring a topic/article', 'Bring a script', etc. Link to plan.py templates.

title: Lazy initializer for reduced-motion state (avoids flash of autoplay)
text: useState(() => matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) reads preference on first render, so no autoplay attributes ever hit DOM for reduced-motion users. Not a post-mount effect.
how: Audit all our video components (preview, approval, dashboard). Replace any useEffect that sets reduced state with lazy initializer. Ensure autoPlay prop is conditional on that state from render 1.

title: Catalog gallery with URL-synced filters, search, and eager above-fold loading
text: Filters (query, group, section, kind, sort) read/write URL search params for shareable links. Search is in-memory on title/description/tags/section. First 6 items in pinned group load posters eagerly (fetchPriority:high), rest lazy. 'Show more' paginates by 24.
how: Apply to dashboard 'Runs' and 'Brain' pages: add ?q=&group=&sort= params. Make search debounced client-side. For approval queue, eager-load first 6 thumbnails. Add 'Show more' button. Store filter state in URL so Telegram deep-links preserve view.

title: Eager poster loading for above-fold cards (fetchPriority:high, loading:eager)
text: Pinned group cards (first 6) use loading='eager' fetchPriority='high' on poster images; rest use loading='lazy'. Poster is same first frame as video. On error, fallback to text label. Reduces LCP for key items.
how: In thumb.py: when generating approval grid, mark first 6 items as 'pinned'. In template, render their with loading='eager' fetchPriority='high'. Add onError to hide image and show text fallback. Measure LCP improvement in stats.py.

title: Remix shelf: hover preview, click for sound, 'Remix in Studio' CTA with copy link
text: Each card: hover plays muted loop, click plays with sound (becomes sole audio), 'Remix in Studio' button opens help text with 'Copy link' to original post. Reduced motion respected. Original videos never hosted locally.
how: Build for our 'Community Remixes' page: fetch top community videos via API, generate 720p loops. Card shows title, credit link to original X/IG post, 'Remix' button copies original URL to clipboard. Use same hover/sound coordination.

title: Template gallery hover-to-play with MutationObserver re-binding for SPA
text: Vanilla JS: on DOMContentLoaded, bind mouseenter/mouseleave to play/pause+reset to 2s. MutationObserver watches body for new .tpl-card video elements and binds them (data-hover-bound flag). Works across Mintlify SPA navigation.
how: Add to our static preview pages (GitHub Pages/Cloudflare Pages): same 10-line script. Binds hover play on any .tpl-card video. On leave, pause and seek to 2s (shows second frame). Re-binds after client-side nav. Zero dependencies.

title: Isolation and verified cleanup for ephemeral render jobs
text: Generate unique run IDs (timestamp+sha256), tag all cloud resources (stack, bucket, function, log groups) with ownership tag. Pre-flight: prove exact names absent via describe calls. Post-run: verify deletion of every resource (S3 versions, log groups, state machines) before exit. Fail closed on any verification error.
how: Apply to any future cloud rendering or even local temp dirs: doctor.py should generate run IDs, tag temp dirs, verify cleanup on exit. Add hf_assert_deploy_isolation style checks before creating resources.

title: Cost-aware concurrency cap for parallel renders
text: Lambda memory 10 GB × maxParallelChunks (default 8) = peak 80 GB. Cost ~$0.04 per 60s 1080p30 at 8 chunks. Set ReservedConcurrency (Map MaxConcurrency) to bound spend: 16 for speed, 2-4 for budget. Local equivalent: limit worker processes by (RAM_GB / 10) and CPU cores.
how: Add maxParallelChunks to compose.py config with default based on local RAM (e.g., 4 for 16 GB). In doctor.py, warn if configured chunks exceed safe memory. Log estimated cost per render using $0.0000167/GB-s formula.

title: Content-addressed render plan with artifact manifest (Plan v2)
text: Plan phase emits manifest.json listing every asset by sha256 + separate artifact files at artifacts/sha256/<hash>. Chunk workers fetch only needed hashes; retries are byte-identical. Enables caching, deduplication, and safe distributed rendering.
how: Modify plan.py to write manifest.json + content-addressed artifact store (e.g., renders/<planHash>/artifacts/sha256/). Update compose.py to read manifest and verify hashes before render. Add planHash to brain for change detection.

title: SDK pattern: validate config client-side before render
text: renderToLambda/renderToCloudRun call validateDistributedRenderConfig() locally, throwing typed InvalidConfigError before Step Functions/Workflows start. Shape errors surface synchronously, not as opaque ExecutionFailed. Config includes fps, width, height, format, chunkSize, maxParallelChunks, runtimeCap.
how: In plan.py, add validate_render_config(config) that checks: fps in [24,30,60], width×height ≤ 1920×1080, format in ['mp4','webm'], chunkSize 60-600, maxParallelChunks 1-32. Raise InvalidConfigError with field-specific messages. Call before any cloud/local render dispatch.

title: Parallel audio mix during chunk render
text: State machine runs Audio branch in parallel with RenderChunks Map. Plan returns SeparateAudio flag. If true, audio task mixes track while chunks render. Assemble stitches audio + chunks. Avoids sequential bottleneck; audio ready when chunks done.
how: In producer.py, split render_pipeline(): start audio_mix() in ThreadPoolExecutor alongside chunk renders. audio_mix() reads plan's audio spec, runs ffmpeg filter_complex, writes audio.mp3. Assemble waits for both futures. Reduces total wall-time by ~audio_duration.

title: Terraform/CloudFormation for reproducible infra
text: AWS: SAM template with parameters (memory, timeout, concurrency, Chrome source). GCP: Terraform module provisions bucket, Cloud Run, Workflows, service accounts, alert. Both output bucket name, function ARN/URL, state machine/workflow ARN. Version-pinned image tags.
how: Create infra/ folder with docker-compose.yml for local stack (MinIO, localstack, temporal). Define services: render-worker, planner, assembler. Use same env vars as Lambda/Cloud Run. Version-lock base images. Run `docker compose up` for local distributed render. Mirrors cloud parity.

title: Runaway invocation alarm via CloudWatch metric
text: Alarm on Lambda Invocations Sum over 1 hour > threshold (default 1000). Catches runaway Map state fan-out or sequential render loops. Separate alarms for Lambda Errors (>0 in 5 min) and Step Functions ExecutionsFailed (>0 in 5 min). TreatMissingData: notBreaching.
how: In doctor.py, add invocation counter per render job. If hourly invocations > 1000 (configurable), alert via Telegram and pause new renders. Track Lambda-style errors: any non-zero exit code in chunk worker. Track SFN-style failures: plan.py/assemble.py exceptions. Reset counters hourly.

title: Three-Tier Variable Precedence
text: Standardize variable overrides: 1. Declared defaults (data-composition-variables), 2. Per-instance host overrides (data-variable-values), 3. CLI/Runtime overrides. This allows the same 'lab' template to be reused with different data without modifying the source HTML.
how: Adopt this hierarchy in plan.py and the Gemini script-to-JSON mapper to ensure consistent behavior across local previews and final renders.

title: Agent-Safe CLI Protocol
text: Enforce 'Stdout is data, Stderr is messages' for all automation scripts. Use --json envelopes for all tool outputs and ensure isUnattended() checks prevent scripts from hanging on interactive prompts during automated runs.
how: Audit all .py and .js tools in the pipeline to ensure they never prompt for input and always emit structured JSON for the next stage.

title: Shader Transition Pre-Capture
text: Pre-capture animated scene samples for transitions and store them in IndexedDB. During playback, composite these cached samples with WebGL shaders. This prevents the DOM capture lag that usually occurs during complex scene transitions in the browser.
how: Integrate into the preview/approval flow in Telegram. Use IndexedDB to cache scene textures so re-watching a video doesn't trigger re-renders of transitions.

title: Audio-Locked Preview Mode
text: Implement an 'audio-locked' attribute that force-mutes playback and hides volume controls. This is essential for embedding previews in environments like chat apps or dashboards where unexpected audio is disruptive.
how: Add an 'audio-locked' flag to the Studio360 Telegram approval bot to ensure videos play silently by default in the chat thread.

title: Playback Range Constraints
text: Use range-start and range-end attributes to play only a specific segment of a composition. The player parks at range-start and loops back from range-end, which is ideal for testing specific hooks or transitions without replaying the whole video.
how: Add range controls to the Studio dashboard so editors can loop a specific 5-second 'hook' while refining the script.

title: Chroma subsampling 444 for text/UI-heavy masters
text: Use `--chroma-subsampling 444` when rendering MP4s that contain thin coloured text, terminal output, stat counters, or UI panels (our lab look). Default 420 blurs colour edges; 444 keeps full-resolution colour (yuv444p) at the cost of larger files and slower encode. Many players can't decode 4:4:4, so only use for masters, not direct publish.
how: Add `--chroma-subsampling 444` to render.py for lab-look compositions; keep 420 for classic/photo-heavy shorts. Document in render presets.

title: Caption discoverability contract for deterministic preflight
text: Caption compositions should expose `data-timeline-role="captions"` (required) and `data-caption-root="true"` (recommended) on their root node. Downstream UIs (timeline, mini-player, editor overlays) use these selectors to isolate caption previews deterministically. Our preflight.py vision review can target this selector for caption-specific checks (readability, timing, Devanagari rendering).
how: Ensure caption-layer composition template includes both attributes. Extend preflight.py to query `[data-timeline-role=captions]` and run Gemini vision prompts focused on caption legibility, word-highlight sync, and safe-area compliance.

title: Extend timeline to match media duration with zero-duration tween
text: Common mistake: composition ends when last GSAP tween ends, cutting off long narration/video. Fix: `tl.set({}, {}, TOTAL_DURATION)` adds a zero-duration tween at the exact end time, extending `tl.duration()` without visual side-effects. Duration comes from timeline, not `data-duration` on compositions.
how: In compose.py / compose_lab.py, after building all tweens, append `tl.set({}, {}, voice_duration + 0.5)` where `voice_duration` is from TTS metadata. Ensures composition lasts through full narration plus tail padding. Add assertion in preflight.py: `composition_duration >= max_media_end - 0.1`.

title: Pinned CLI version for reproducible re-renders
text: HyperFrames project templates pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` in `package.json` so the project re-renders identically weeks later. To upgrade: `npx hyperframes --cli-version latest upgrade --project . --check` shows delta; run without `--check` to rewrite pins. Prevents silent breakage from framework updates.
how: Add `hyperframes` to our `package.json` with exact version (e.g., `"hyperframes": "1.2.3"`). Document upgrade workflow in ops/runbook.md: run check, review diff, commit pin bump. Ensure doctor.py validates lockfile matches package.json.

title: Docker render mode for deterministic CI output
text: `hyperframes render --docker` uses a fixed Chrome version and font set inside a container, eliminating local-machine drift (font fallback, Chrome version, GPU differences). Local mode auto-detects GPU on first launch but can differ across runs. Docker is recommended for production renders. Requires Docker installed and running.
how: Add `--docker` flag to render.py for final delivery renders (after Telegram approval). Keep local `--no-browser-gpu` for fast previews. Update doctor.py to verify Docker daemon health before production render jobs. Pin base image digest in render Dockerfile.

title: Integrity-verified materialization before render
text: Plan V2 verifies every artifact's SHA256 and size before execution. Materialization writes a marker file with manifest + target, then re-validates on start. Fail-closed on any mismatch.
how: In preflight.py, after downloading render artifacts, compute SHA256 of each file, compare to manifest.json. Abort if any mismatch. Write .hyperframes-materialized marker with manifest hash.

title: Chunk-based video frame dependency mapping
text: Plan V2 maps each video source to the chunk indexes that actually need its frames (via FrameLookupTable). Chunks only materialize required frames; assembler gets all. Deferred sources referenced by URL.
how: When splitting long videos into chunks (future), compute per-chunk frame ranges using our timeline data. Store mapping in manifest for partial downloads.

title: Kill ghost watermark elements
text: Large low-opacity background text (e.g., 600px '2026' at 3% opacity) reads as rendering error, not branding. Either commit with 5-8% opacity and bold weight or remove entirely. Flagged in style-2 and style-3 reviews.
how: Update lab look design rules in compose_lab.py: reject background text elements with opacity < 0.05; if used, enforce min 5% opacity and weight 700+.

title: Frame scaled A-roll with intentional container
text: Scaling A-roll to 60-70% and leaving it floating on gray background looks amateur. Add subtle border, pronounced shadow, or lock to grid quadrant. Critiqued in style-2, style-4, style-6, style-8.
how: Modify compose_lab.py A-roll component: when scale < 0.8, auto-apply 2px accent border + 20px blur shadow + grid-snap positioning; add as default lab-look preset.

title: Sophisticate color palettes: avoid neon green/black, mustard gold, default CSS primaries
text: Pure #33FF66 on #0A0A0A causes eye strain; #D4A017 looks like expired mustard; #E74C3C/#F1C40F are default CSS colors. Use nuanced mint/emerald, metallic gold, or high-contrast neons with varied opacity. Critiqued in style-3, style-5, style-8.
how: Define brand color tokens in brain.jsonl: lab-accent='#00FF9F', lab-gold='#D4AF37', lab-crimson='#E2001A'; update compose_lab.py stat counters, UI panels, and kinetic titles to reference tokens not raw hex.

title: Subtle letter-spacing (0.05-0.2em) not 0.6em; dramatic weight contrast 300 vs 900
text: 0.6em letter-spacing on 42px text makes words fall apart. Vignelli-style Swiss design uses tight kerning (0.05em) with heavy/light weight pairing. Flagged in style-3 and style-7.
how: Add typography rules to brain.jsonl: caption letter-spacing max 0.15em; title letter-spacing 0.05em; enforce weight pairs 300/900 in compose_lab.py kinetic titles and caption components.

title: Background grids at 0.05 opacity or hidden — never visible
text: Visible grid lines (style-3) create visual vibration and scream 'template'. Grid should guide layout, not be seen. Reduce to 0.05 opacity or remove; use for alignment only.
how: Update compose_lab.py grid-bg component: default opacity 0.03; add 'invisible' mode (opacity 0) that still provides CSS grid lines for child positioning via grid-column/row.

title: Preserve VFR timestamps with ffmpeg -fps_mode passthrough for screen recordings
text: macOS ScreenCaptureKit recordings are VFR (avg 36fps, r_frame_rate 120/1). Re-encode with ffmpeg -fps_mode passthrough -c:v libx264 to preserve timestamps and avoid duplicate-frame bugs. From NOTICE.md.
how: Update scout.py and compose.py media ingest: when source is screen recording (detected via ffprobe isVFR), apply passthrough mode; store original timestamps in brain.jsonl for sync reference.

title: Enforce data-composition-id on root container
text: Top-level HTML container MUST have data-composition-id attribute (not just id) or the framework won't initialize the master timeline. Found as critical issue in style-2 review.
how: Add preflight check in preflight.py to verify root element has data-composition-id; auto-fix id→data-composition-id in compose.py when generating index.html.

title: Add Studio debug channels for edit tracing
text: Studio's decision failures (wrong selection, unexpected reload) leave no errors. Enable via localStorage: hf-drag-debug, hf-reload-debug, hf-select-debug. Documented in AGENTS.md.
how: Add debug panel to dashboard (stats.py) with toggles for each channel; log to console with [hf-drag] prefix; integrate with doctor.py to capture decision traces on failed renders.

title: Use window.__studioTest.selectByDomId() for reliable automated QA
text: Pixel-perfect clicks in iframe are flaky; Studio exposes dev-only hook window.__studioTest.selectByDomId('id') that selects element and opens inspector. Works in embedded mode. From AGENTS.md.
how: Extend review.py to launch headless Studio via CLI, call selectByDomId for each scene's key elements, verify computed styles match plan.py specs; add to preflight pipeline.

title: Deterministic runtime lockfiles synced to bun.lock
text: Maintain separate package-lock.json files for each Chrome source (sparticuz vs chrome-headless-shell) that pin only direct deps (puppeteer-core, @sparticuz/chromium) to the exact versions in bun.lock. Regenerate via `npm install --package-lock-only` after any bump; Renovate weekly maintenance keeps transitive tree fresh.
how: Create a lock-runtime script that reads bun.lock, writes per-source package.json, runs npm ci --package-lock-only, and commits the lockfiles. Run it in CI on dependency changes.

title: WebGPU adapter detection for shader fallback
text: On the render host, open a secure-context page (http://127.0.0.1) with a data-requires-webgpu element and call navigator.gpu.requestAdapter(). If it resolves, hardware WebGPU is available; if it throws WebGpuUnavailableError, force software SwiftShader (--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader).
how: In compose_lab.py, before rendering shader transitions, run a quick WebGPU probe. Set a global flag to choose GPU vs software compositing flags for Chrome launch.

title: ELF header validation for render binaries
text: Before any render, verify ffmpeg, ffprobe, and Chrome binaries are Linux x86_64 ELF (magic 0x7F454C46, class=2, machine=0x3E). Reject macOS arm64 or corrupted binaries with a clear error pointing to docker/linux build or npm_config_platform=linux npm_config_arch=x64.
how: Add a preflight check in doctor.py or compose.py that reads the first 20 bytes of each binary and asserts the ELF header. Fail fast with actionable message.

title: BeginFrame probe for Chrome render health
text: Launch Chrome with BeginFrame flags (--enable-begin-frame-control, --run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw, --disable-threaded-animation, --disable-gpu-compositing, --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader) and drive HeadlessExperimental.beginFrame via CDP until a valid PNG screenshotData returns. Retry up to 10 frames with 33 ms intervals.
how: Add a probe script (probe-beginframe.ts) that runs in doctor.py before batch renders. If it fails, alert and skip renders until Chrome is fixed. Use the same flags as the engine's browserManager.

title: ARM64 binary swap for Apple Silicon runners
text: If CI runs on arm64 macOS, stage an arm64 ffmpeg/ffprobe tarball (verified via ELF machine=0xB7), replace the x86 binaries in the render package, drop the x86 Chrome (sparticuz or chrome-headless-shell), but keep sparticuz fonts (fonts.conf + fonts/) for text fallback.
how: Add a stage-arm64-image step in the build pipeline that unzips the handler ZIP, swaps bin/ffmpeg and bin/ffprobe, extracts fonts.tar.br to fonts/, removes node_modules/@sparticuz/chromium/bin, and re-zips.

title: Artifact pinning with SHA256 sidecars
text: After building the render package (ZIP, Docker image, etc.), compute SHA256, write a `.sha256` file (`<hash>  <filename>`), and emit a JSON manifest with version, URL, sha256, and bytes. Use this for cache invalidation and reproducible deploys.
how: Extend publish.py or a new pin-artifacts script to hash the output, write sidecars, and update a manifest.json consumed by the dashboard for version tracking.

title: Chrome headless shell digest verification
text: When staging Chrome, compute a digest (e.g., SHA256 of the shell folder) and compare against a pinned value for the exact version. Refuse to stage if the cached folder digest mismatches or if the version differs from the pinned one. Error message includes the exact `@puppeteer/browsers install` command.
how: In compose.py's Chrome setup, add a digest check before launching. Store pinned digests in a JSON file keyed by version. Fail with actionable install command.

title: Typed non-retryable error classification
text: Define explicit error names (e.g., PLAN_HASH_MISMATCH, CHROME_BINARY_UNAVAILABLE, CHUNK_EXCEEDS_WORKER_TIMEOUT) and mark them as non-retryable (maxAttempts: 0) in retry policies. Only retry transient errors (throttles, network) with exponential backoff and jitter.
how: In doctor.py and review.py, classify failure reasons into retryable vs terminal buckets. Add error_name field to failure logs. Update retry logic in render pipeline to respect classification.

title: Chrome binary wedge detection and typed recovery
text: @sparticuz/chromium can wedge after sandbox timeouts, returning empty executablePath on warm invocations. Detect via ChromeBinaryUnavailableError (source, resolvedPath). Recovery: bump environment variable to force new execution environment (Lambda) or restart browser process (local).
how: In compose.py/compose_lab.py, wrap browser launch in try/catch for 'executablePath empty' or 'file not found'. On catch, log ChromeBinaryUnavailableError, restart browser subprocess, and retry once. Add env var HF_BROWSER_EPOCH to force fresh context.

title: Warm-up pattern for browser render workers
text: Before heavy render jobs, send a no-op 'warm' invocation to the renderer (Lambda or local browser pool) to initialize Chrome, load fonts, and populate /tmp. Failures caught and logged but don't block the main render. Reduces cold-start variance from ~8s to ~1s.
how: In plan.py or compose.py, add a preflight step that spawns a headless browser, loads a minimal page, and exits. Run in background while script finalizes. Reuse the same browser instance for the actual render if possible.

title: Structured pipeline event logging
text: Emit single JSON line per pipeline stage (plan, render, assemble) with event type, action, timings, and key IDs. Enables log querying without debugger.
how: In each Python script (plan.py, compose.py, publish.py), add log_event(event, action, stage, ms, ids) writing JSON to stdout. Parse with jq or send to Loki.

title: Stream large clips via HTTP range requests
text: For video clips >50MB, generate pre-signed URL (or direct URL with range support) and pass to ffmpeg via `-i <url>` with `-ss`/`-t` instead of full download. Chunk renderer uses this for deferred videos.
how: In compose.py, when a clip URL is from cloud storage, detect size via HEAD; if large, write a `.remote` manifest with URL and byte ranges. FFmpeg input reads directly.

title: Cloud storage bucket allowlist
text: Define allowed bucket/prefix in env (e.g., `ALLOWED_STORAGE_BUCKET`). Before any download/upload, parse URI and reject if bucket not in allowlist. Prevents SSRF and data exfiltration.
how: In `s3Transport.py` equivalent, add `validate_uri(uri)` called at start of download/upload. Load allowlist from env at startup.

title: Idempotent artifact publishing
text: Track published content hashes in a local DB. On publish, skip already-published digests. Support abort (mark publisher aborted) and retry (new publisher instance reuses existing blobs). Handler's publisher does this.
how: In publish.py, maintain `published_hashes.json`. Before upload, check if hash exists in remote (HEAD). On interrupt, write `aborted` flag; next run resumes from manifest.

title: Vendor ffmpeg and Chromium
text: Bundle static ffmpeg and Chromium binaries in `bin/` directory. Set `PATH` and `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH`/`PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` at runtime. Ensures identical renders across machines and CI.
how: Add `vendor_binaries.sh` to download ffmpeg static and Chromium headless shell. In `doctor.py`, verify binaries exist and set env vars before any render.

title: Fake Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare for tests
text: Implement in-memory fakes for external APIs (Gemini TTS, Muse image gen, FLUX) that record calls and return canned responses. Tests run without network, assert call sequences and payloads.
how: Create `fakes/` module with `FakeGemini`, `FakeMuse`, `FakeCloudflare`. In test suite, inject fakes into pipeline. Use `bun:test` or `pytest` with fixtures.

title: Object Storage Lifecycle Refresh via Self-Copy
text: Cloud storage lifecycle deletion policies trigger based on object creation or `LastModified` timestamps, not last read time. Hot cached artifacts (e.g. downloaded B-roll, shared font packs) can expire unexpectedly. To refresh an asset's retention TTL without re-uploading, issue a copy request with source equal to destination and metadata directive set to `REPLACE` once the object exceeds an age threshold.
how: In `doctor.py`, add a cache renewal check that scans asset storage and issues a metadata replacement copy on files approaching lifecycle expiration to reset their retention clock.

title: Probe Facts JSON Sidecar for Media Assets
text: Before processing or rendering video clips, extract stream metadata, packet counts, duration, and final frame/packet timestamps into a `<hash>.probe.json` sidecar. Storing these facts alongside content-addressed assets allows preflight, layout, and pacing scripts to query exact durations and stream specs instantly without repeatedly invoking `ffprobe` subprocesses during generation runs.
how: In `preflight.py` and `compose.py`, write an `asset_facts(path)` helper that checks for or generates a `.probe.json` sidecar using `ffprobe -show_entries` before inspecting video or audio files.

title: Fresh-Stream Retry for Media Uploads
text: Node/Python streaming uploads to remote endpoints (Meta Graph API, cloud storage) fail irreversibly on network drops because consumed streams cannot seek backwards. Streaming upload handlers must never retry the existing stream; wrap uploads in a loop that opens a fresh read stream per attempt and unconditionally destroys the previous stream in a `finally` block before sleeping.
how: In `publish.py`, refactor video file uploads to instantiate a new file stream inside the retry block so socket resets or HTTP 408/5xx errors start reading cleanly from byte 0.

title: Hard-Link Decoupling on Tarball Extraction
text: Extracting archived project bundles or template assets into shared worker directories can preserve hard links (`nlink > 1`), creating shared inode references that lead to silent race conditions or cross-contamination across concurrent jobs. Scan extracted files for `nlink > 1`, copy each to `.unlink-<uuid>`, and atomically replace the original to guarantee unique physical files.
how: In `compose.py` or template unpack utilities, implement post-extraction inode checking that unlinks and replaces multi-link files before launching worker browser instances.

title: Weighted render progress phases (10% plan, 80% chunks, 10% assemble)
text: Report progress as: 0 before plan; 0.1 after plan (totalFrames known); 0.1 + 0.8 × framesEncoded/totalFrames during chunk render; 1.0 after assemble. Matches HyperFrames' Plan → RenderChunk → Assemble pipeline.
how: Update doctor.py and dashboard to compute progress using this formula. In compose.py, emit framesEncoded per scene; aggregate in render loop. Show in Telegram approvals and 09:00 report.

title: Deterministic render IDs for predictable output paths
text: Use executionName = `hf-render-<uuid>` (or `studio-<page>-<date>-<seq>`). Output key becomes `renders/<executionName>/output.mp4`. Enables pre-computed URLs for approvals, CDN, and analytics before render finishes.
how: Standardize renderId generation in plan.py or new render.py. Ensure thumb.py, publish.py, stats.py all derive paths from renderId. Pass renderId through Telegram approval payload.

title: Exponential backoff for external API throttling (Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare)
text: Wrap all external API calls with retry on 429/ThrottlingException: max 8 attempts, exponential backoff. HyperFrames uses SFN client with maxAttempts=8. Prevents render failures during API rate limits.
how: Create api_retry.py with retry_async(func, max_attempts=8, base_delay=1). Apply to Gemini calls in ideas.py, research.py, plan.py, preflight.py; Muse in compose.py; Cloudflare in image fetch. Log retries.

title: Render input size budget enforcement
text: Enforce a hard cap (e.g., 256 KiB) on serialized render config + variables. Reject configs exceeding limit with byte count and pointer to 'URL your assets' docs. Forces asset references over inlining, keeps Step Functions/Lambda invocations fast.
how: Add validateStepFunctionsInputSize equivalent in preflight.py: JSON.stringify(config), measure UTF-8 bytes, throw if > 256 KiB. Log budget usage in dashboard (Today, Runs).

title: Variables payload sanitization
text: Deep-validate composition variables for JSON-serializability: reject functions, undefined, BigInt, NaN/Infinity, Symbols, Date instances, circular refs (objects/arrays). Walk nested structures and report precise path (e.g., config.variables.items[1].broken).
how: Integrate validateVariablesPayload into plan.py before passing variables to HyperFrames; run on brain.jsonl entries and Telegram feedback payloads to catch serialization bugs early.

title: Audio sidecar generation for transcription
text: When rendering final MP4, simultaneously output an audio-only .m4a (AAC, 128k) sidecar via ffmpeg -map 0:a. Store alongside video with same SHA-256 stem (e.g., abc123.audio.m4a). Enables accurate post-render transcription/captioning even if TTS drifts from script.
how: Extend mix.py to write sidecar after loudness mastering; register sidecar path in brain.jsonl and upload to R2 with video. Use for future caption correction pipeline.

title: Atomic file replacement for all pipeline outputs
text: Write every generated file (scripts, audio, video chunks, captions, manifests) to a temporary path then atomically rename (replaceFileAtomically). Prevents partial reads by concurrent processes (doctor.py, publish.py, Telegram approvals).
how: Wrap all file writes in utils/atomicWrite.ts (using @hyperframes/core/atomic-file); apply to ideas.py, research.py, plan.py, pace.py, mix.py, thumb.py, publish.py.

title: Cancellation token propagation across async steps
text: Pass AbortSignal through all long-running operations: media download, TTS, render chunks, upload, transcription. Each step checks signal.aborted and throws TranscribeError('cancelled')/RenderError('cancelled'). Tool lookups (ffmpeg, whisper) capped at 10s before abort.
how: Create a CancellationScope in doctor.py and pass signal to ideas.py, scout.py, plan.py, compose.py, publish.py. Use in voice gate to kill stuck TTS. Replace timer-based kills with cooperative cancellation.

title: Sound classification for content-aware pacing
text: The 'describe' capability returns tags like 'speech', 'music', 'applause' with confidence scores. Use tag mix to decide pacing: speech → slower cuts, music → beat-synced, mixed → hybrid.
how: In ideas.py scoring, add a 'audioKind' feature from describe tags; adjust freshness/fit weights based on dominant tag (e.g., music gets higher beat-sync potential).

title: Adaptive envelope hop size for efficient waveform viz
text: envelopeHopMs(seconds) returns 5 ms for short clips, coarsening to ~2000 values for long ones (max 90 ms hop). Guarantees consistent visual density regardless of duration.
how: In compose_lab.py's HUD/meter components, use this formula to set envelope sample rate; feed to GSAP tween for smooth level meters without oversampling.

title: Onset detection for visual event syncing
text: Spectral-flux onsets give precise attack times (strength 0‑1). Use them to trigger flash, particle burst, or text reveal exactly at sound onsets.
how: In plan.py, request 'onsets' capability for the voice/music track; pass onset events to compose.py as cue points for kinetic titles or card flips.

title: Provider ladder with quality gates for external APIs
text: Capabilities try providers in order (local → cloud) with 'local' quality keeping data on‑machine; 'best' uploads to HeyGen. Pin critical capabilities (beats/bpm) to same provider to avoid drift.
how: Wrap Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare calls in a similar ladder: local cache → free tier → paid fallback; add quality flag to doctor.py to control cloud usage; enforce same provider for linked steps (e.g., script+voice).

title: Content-addressed audio analysis caching
text: Cache key includes file identity (size, mtime, inode), clip window, sample rate, quality, and provider. Entries stored as atomic JSON in .hyperframes/audio-kind; symlinks are never followed for security.
how: Extend brain.jsonl with audio-analysis cache: key = hash(fileIdentity + clip + params); store kind, beats, loudness; invalidate on file change. Use in preflight.py to skip re-analysis.

title: 0.1 s edge context for accurate onsets
text: When analyzing a window, decode ±0.1 s extra at edges. Onset at window start/end gets context to distinguish true hit from cut artifact. Retained signal excludes context margins.
how: In mix.py SFX analysis, when cutting SFX clips, pad decode by 0.1 s each side; trim after onset detection.

title: Pulse validation: ≥2 beats, ≥50% heard
text: A beat grid is trusted only if at least two beats fall in the window and at least half of all beats in the window are heard (not masked). Prevents false grids in short or noisy segments.
how: In beat-synced cut logic, require pulse validation on music bed before snapping cuts to beats; else fall back to fixed cadence.

title: Drum group detection via beat alignment
text: Group sounds by spectral similarity; if a group has ≥8 events and ≥70% land within 50 ms of a beat, classify as drum group and exclude from effect list. Prevents music beats from triggering SFX visuals.
how: In effect detection, after grouping, compute beat alignment; mark drum groups; only non-drum groups trigger visual effects.

title: Reject ambience-only tracks as music beds
text: readMusic classifies noise (rumble, hiss) as ambience: no segments, no pieces, ambience array with db -40 to -10. Tonal music gets segments with bpm, pieces with instruments. Run on candidate bed; if music.segments empty → discard.
how: In ideas.py or scout.py, when fetching background music candidates, run readMusic first. Filter out tracks where music.segments.length === 0. Cache result keyed by file SHA.

title: Piece-level music metadata for series branding
text: music.pieces have id, instruments (loudest stems playing through ≥50% of first segment), bpm, firstAt. Same piece reappears with entry='returns'. Store piece signatures in brain.jsonl; reuse instrument/bpm profile for recurring series theme.
how: In scout.py, when a music bed is selected, extract pieces. Save {piece_id, instruments, bpm, firstAt} to brain.jsonl under series key. In ideas.py, suggest 'reuse piece 3 from episode 12' for consistency.

title: Fade-out detection for outro extension
text: segment.fadeFrom returns timestamp where level drops >10 dB below segment median in last 3s. If present, music fades rather than hard stop. Extend last visual scene to fadeFrom→end; don't cut to end card early.
how: In plan.py, if last segment has fadeFrom, set final scene end = segment.end. In compose_lab.py, schedule end card at segment.end, not voice end. Add slow vignette breathe during fade.

title: Centralized timeout constants
text: Replace magic numbers with named constants: ACCOUNT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=15000, OAUTH_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS=3600000, MIN_HELPER_TOKEN_LIFETIME_MS=600000. Makes timeouts discoverable and adjustable in one place.
how: Add timeouts.py with constants for render chunk timeout (e.g. 300000), API request timeout (30000), doctor interval (600000). Import in doctor.py, render workers, publish.py.

title: Token refresh with rotation handling
text: When refreshing OAuth tokens (future YouTube upload), always persist new refresh_token if returned. IdPs rotate refresh tokens; reusing the old one causes permanent lockout.
how: In future youtube_oauth.py, store both access_token and refresh_token. On refresh, update both from response. Never assume refresh_token stays constant.

title: Credential scrubbing in error logs
text: Scrub API keys (hg_*, Bearer tokens) and JWTs from all error messages before logging. The library redacts secrets in 401 responses using a scrubCredentials helper that replaces key patterns with <redacted>.
how: Add a scrub_secrets() utility in doctor.py/review.py that regex-replaces Gemini/Muse/Cloudflare keys in exception logs. Call it in all except hooks before writing to results.md or Telegram.

title: Structured error codes for pipeline branching
text: Define typed error classes with stable codes (RENDER_FAILED, API_QUOTA_EXCEEDED, VOICE_GATE_REJECTED, ASSET_MISSING) so doctor.py/preflight.py can branch on err.code instead of string matching.
how: Create errors.py with AuthError-like subclasses. Replace generic Exception raises in compose.py, mix.py, publish.py with specific codes. Update doctor.py to handle each code distinctly.

title: Credential isolation for render subprocesses
text: When spawning Chrome/ffmpeg workers, create a temp dir (0o700), write minimal credentials file (0o600), set HEYGEN_CONFIG_DIR env, and delete dir on exit. Prevents credential leakage between concurrent renders.
how: Wrap render worker launch in a context manager in compose.py/compose_lab.py that creates temp config, injects only needed API keys, and guarantees cleanup via try/finally.

title: Forward-compatible config storage
text: Preserve unknown fields in brain.jsonl and project configs by storing a hidden '_extra' dict during load, merging it back on save. Allows schema evolution without data loss when adding new fields.
how: Modify brain.jsonl load/save in ideas.py/research.py to pop '_extra' on load, merge on dump. Use a '_extra' key in project JSON configs for series templates.

title: Constant-time secret comparison
text: Use hmac.compare_digest (Python) or crypto.timingSafeEqual (Node) for webhook signature verification (Telegram, Meta, YouTube). Prevents timing attacks on secret validation.
how: Add verify_signature(payload, signature, secret) in publish.py/webhook handler using hmac.compare_digest. Apply to Telegram approval callbacks and Meta webhook endpoints.

title: External API response validation
text: Validate Gemini/Muse/Cloudflare responses with schemas before processing. Reject malformed payloads (non-JSON, missing fields, wrong types) with structured API_ERROR instead of crashing downstream.
how: Add response schemas in research.py (Gemini), compose.py (Muse/FLUX). Wrap API calls in validate_response(resp, schema) that raises typed API_ERROR on mismatch.

title: Unit tests for critical pipeline functions
text: Add pytest tests for ideas.py scoring (yt-dlp view parsing), research.py hook extraction, plan.py scene validation, voice_gate.py thresholds. Mock external APIs; run in CI on every push.
how: Create tests/ folder with test_ideas.py, test_research.py, test_plan.py. Use fixtures for sample yt-dlp JSON, Gemini responses. Enforce 80% coverage on core modules.

title: Credential resolution priority chain
text: Define a fixed priority for API key sources: 1) host-injected env (HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN), 2) stored OAuth (fresh or refreshable), 3) shell env (HEYGEN_API_KEY, HYPERFRAMES_API_KEY), 4) saved config file, 5) project .env (only if no saved config). Reject expired non-refreshable logins.
how: Document in `ops/config_resolver.py`; implement `resolve_credentials()` returning source; use in `publish.py` for Meta API, `research.py` for Gemini.

title: Header safety validation
text: Before inserting any string into an HTTP header (Authorization, x-api-key), verify it contains no control characters (charCode < 0x20 or 0x7F). Reject or sanitize to prevent header injection attacks.
how: Add `is_header_safe(s)` in `utils/http.py`; call in all API clients (Gemini, Muse, Cloudflare, Meta) before setting headers.

title: Consistent UUID derivation for cross-system IDs
text: Derive stable UUID v5 from video title/series name using SHA-256: `uuid = sha256(name).bytes; set version/variant bits`. Use for analytics, file naming, database keys across YouTube, Instagram, internal tracking.
how: Add `derive_uuid(name)` in `utils/ids.py`; use in `publish.py` for video IDs, `stats.py` for joining metrics, `brain.py` for series keys.

title: Deduplication of concurrent API calls
text: Maintain a map of in-flight requests keyed by (endpoint, params); subsequent identical calls await the same promise. Prevents duplicate Gemini/Muse/Cloudflare calls during parallel research or render steps.
how: Add `deduped_fetch(key, fn)` in `utils/api.py`; wrap `gemini_call()`, `muse_generate()`, `cloudflare_flux()`; key by normalized params.

title: Project-local config detection with notice
text: Detect a `.env` or `config.json` in the project directory; if used, log a one-time notice: `[studio] Using GEMINI_API_KEY from ./project/.env: renders go to that account.` Prevents accidental cross-project credential leakage.
how: In `config_resolver.py`, check `projectEnvDir()`; emit notice via `logger.warn()` once per process; integrate with `doctor.py` startup.

title: Atomic credential storage with cross-tool compatibility
text: Store credentials in a JSON file with atomic writes; preserve unknown top-level keys and unknown sub-keys inside `oauth`/`user` objects. Allows sharing credential file with other tools (e.g., future CLI) without data loss.
how: Implement `credential_store.py` with `read_store()`, `write_store()`, `clear_oauth()` using `UNKNOWN` bag; use for Meta API tokens, Gemini keys, Cloudflare tokens.

title: Efficient Raw Video Frame Streaming
text: Uses an async generator to read raw video frames from a pipe, allocating buffers only as needed and ensuring each frame has its own dedicated memory to prevent data corruption during processing.
how: Adopt the 'readFrames' generator pattern in our media processing scripts to handle large video inputs without loading entire files into memory.

title: Local ONNX Background Removal with Fallback
text: Implements local background removal using ONNX Runtime with CoreML provider for Apple Silicon, including automatic fallback to CPU if inference fails. Uses specific ImageNet normalization (MEAN/STD) to ensure parity with u2net_human_seg training distributions.
how: Integrate the inference logic into our pipeline to perform background removal locally on clips, reducing dependency on external APIs and improving latency.

title: Display Matrix Orientation Correction
text: Detects 'Display Matrix' rotation metadata via ffprobe. If rotation is 90 or 270 degrees, it transposes frame dimensions (width/height) to ensure correct frame sizing and processing.
how: Update our preflight or composition logic to probe input video metadata and adjust layout dimensions dynamically before rendering.

title: Chrome Process Tree Reaper
text: Tracks process descendants and ensures orphaned browser/Chrome instances are killed on CLI exit or crash, preventing resource leaks.
how: Add a cleanup utility to our doctor.py that scans for and reaps orphaned browser processes after render jobs or unexpected crashes.

title: Dual-Output Mask Invariants
text: Ensures foreground and background plates are byte-identical in RGB, with alpha channels summing to 255 per pixel. This ensures seamless compositing.
how: Implement the 'applyMask' function in our composition logic to generate consistent foreground/background pairs for professional-grade masking.

title: Chrome install facts logging for diagnostics
text: Extract build version from managed-cache path (e.g., `win64-152.0.7928.2`), path ASCII-ness, length bucket (<120, 120-199, 200-259, 260+), and drive type (posix, windows_c, windows_other, unc). Log these on every render start for correlation with failures.
how: Add `describeBrowserInstall(chromePath)` in utils/browserFacts.ts. Call in compose.py's render entry and doctor.py's health check. Append to events NDJSON and results.md. No code change to Chrome launch, just logging.

title: macOS old Chrome crash detection and remediation
text: Detect launch failure with dyld `Symbol not found: _kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ReferenceBufferCount` from VideoToolbox framework. This signals macOS <13 incompatible with pinned Chrome 152+. Remediation: install `chrome-headless-shell@150` via puppeteer/browsers and set `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` or `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH`.
how: Add `isMacosOldChromeCrashError(errMsg)` check in doctor.py's Chrome launch error handler. If on macOS and matches, print the exact install command and env var example. Only relevant if any Mac runners exist in CI; otherwise document for contributors.

title: Download retry with configurable stall timeout
text: Chrome download accepts `downloadStallMs` (default 200ms) and `downloadAttempts` (default 1 on non-TTY, 3 on TTY). On stall, abort child process (OS closes sockets), retry up to attempts. Non-TTY fails fast with hint to set `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` or run `doctor`.
how: Apply same parameters to Muse/FLUX asset downloads in compose_lab.py: `stallMs: 200`, `attempts: 3` for interactive, `1` for CI. Use the stall watchdog from item 1. Surface `HYPERFRAMES_ASSET_PATH` override hint on repeated failure.

title: Linux shared-library preflight via ldd probe
text: Before any Chrome render, run `ldd <chrome-binary>` and parse lines ending with `=> not found`. If missing libs (libnss3, libatk, etc.), surface the exact distro-specific install command (apt/dnf/pacman/apk) and block the render. Probe runs only on Linux; returns inconclusive otherwise.
how: Extend preflight.py with a `probeChromeSharedLibs(chromePath)` function that shells out to ldd, parses output, and raises a structured error with remediation. Call it in doctor.py's pre-render checks and in the render pipeline before launch.

title: Structured progress protocol for long operations
text: Define a line-based protocol: `PREFIX:JSON\n` for progress (downloaded, total) and log lines. The child writes to stdout; parent reads line-by-line, parses, and updates UI/metrics. Torn lines are dropped; next progress line carries current state.
how: Adopt the `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_INSTALL_PROGRESS` pattern in utils/progressProtocol.ts. Wrap Muse image/video downloads, FLUX asset fetches, and FFmpeg renders. Feed parsed events into stats.py's dashboard and Telegram approvals.

title: Sandbox fallback with diagnosis capture
text: On Chrome launch failure, if error indicates sandbox denial (namespace, seccomp, macOS seatbelt), retry once with `--no-sandbox` (and `--single-process` on Linux). Capture stderr from both attempts; if diagnosis enabled, run a headless probe with default args to surface missing libs or GPU issues.
how: Wrap the Chrome launch in compose.py with a `launchWithSandboxFallback` helper that mirrors `launchWithChromeSandboxFallback`. Pass `diagnose: true` for production renders, `false` for GPU probe. Feed captured stderr into review.py's vision review.

title: One-shot warning for system-Chrome fallback
text: warnSystemFallbackOnce() fires only once per process on Linux when falling back to system Chrome (non-headless-shell). Avoids log spam in long-running studio process. Resettable for tests.
how: In preflight.py, when GPU capture unavailable, warn once per session. Use module-level _warned flag. Add _reset_warnings_for_tests() for pytest.

title: Corrupt-archive auto-recovery with single retry
text: Detects zip corruption via error strings (end of central directory, corrupt zip, etc.). On corruption, clears staging dir and retries download exactly once. Second corruption propagates. Logs recovery attempt. Prevents permanent cache poisoning from partial downloads.
how: Wrap Muse/FLUX/Pollinations download calls in installWithCorruptArchiveRecovery(run, clearCache, onRecover). Add is_corrupt_archive_error() matching their strings. Log to events.ndjson.

title: Windows file-lock retry with exponential backoff
text: On Windows, EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES on rename/unlink retries up to 5 times: 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 4s. Calls onRetry callback between attempts. Non-lock errors or non-Windows fail immediately. Fixes AV scanner transient locks.
how: Add retry_while_locked() to utils/fs.py. Use in thumb.py, compose.py, publish.py when moving/overwriting files on Windows runners.

title: Guaranteed temp-profile cleanup on SIGINT/SIGTERM
text: pageNetwork registers cleanup via registerBrowserSessionCleanup(release). release() closes proxy, deletes userDataDir (hf-cli-profile-*). On Ctrl-C, cleanup runs before exit; test verifies profile gone. Proxy server also closes on browser disconnect.
how: In doctor.py and render entrypoints, register atexit/signal handlers that call cleanup_temp_profiles(). Track active profile dirs in a global set. Ensure ffmpeg/Chrome child processes are reaped.

title: Disk-space preflight before large downloads
text: assertRoomToDownload() checks free space at cache root (getFreeDiskMb) against ARCHIVE_PLUS_UNPACKED_SHELL_MB (512MB). Fails fast with actionable message. Also sweeps stale staging/replaced dirs before check.
how: Add check_disk_space(min_mb) to preflight.py. Call before render (estimate 2GB for 4K), before model downloads, before browser ensure. Use shutil.disk_usage.

title: Staged install with atomic rename and leftover sweep
text: Downloads to .chrome-staging-<uuid>, verifies executable, renames over target version dir (atomic on same FS). Old dir moved to .chrome-replaced-<uuid> (kept for live readers), deleted after swap. SweepKilledInstalls() removes orphaned staging/replaced dirs on next run.
how: Implement stage_and_swap(src, dest) in utils/fs.py. Use for model checkpoints, font bundles, browser binaries. Add sweep_killed_installs() to doctor.py startup.

title: Proxy lifecycle tied to browser session
text: launchWithPageNetwork starts capture proxy, creates temp profile, passes proxy args to Chrome. On browser disconnect or launch error, release() closes proxy and deletes profile. Proxy URL verified open during session, closed after.
how: If studio ever needs network isolation for renders, replicate pattern: start proxy → launch browser with args → register cleanup on disconnect/error. Use httpx to verify proxy health.

title: Windows Chrome STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN detection and workaround
text: Exit code 3221225595 (0xC0000409) indicates a pinned chrome-headless-shell crash on some Win10/11 hosts. Remediation: set HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH to system Chrome (any build works for screenshot capture path). Detection matches Puppeteer launch-failure wrapper + decimal/hex/symbol crash code.
how: In doctor.py or render error handler, match this error pattern and auto-suggest the env var; document in runbook for Windows-based render workers.

title: Agent prompt generation (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) with data inventory for captured sites
text: generateAgentPrompt() writes a markdown inventory listing all captured files (contact sheets, tokens.json, design-styles.json, asset-descriptions.md, visible-text.txt, lottie/shader manifests) with descriptions. Points AI agents to hyperframes skill references/film.md and references/types/launch.md. Sanitizes page content (strips instructions, code, markdown) — treats capture as data only.
how: When scout.py captures a reference site, generate this prompt and feed to Gemini in plan.py for script/visual planning; ensures the LLM sees only structured data, not executable instructions.

title: Page-network fence: static analysis ensures all Chrome launches use network isolation
text: AST test (pageNetwork.wiring.test.ts) scans all .ts files for launchManagedBrowser, puppeteer.launch, acquireBrowser calls. Passes only if each is inside a launchWithPageNetwork callback that forwards network.args and network.userDataDir. Allows known exceptions (GPU probe, capture, measure hands). Renamed imports also flagged.
how: Add a similar lint step in our CI (doctor.py) to verify our Chrome launches (in compose.py, render workers) go through our network proxy/fence; prevents accidental direct launches that bypass traffic shaping or monitoring.

title: Deterministic version parsing for FFmpeg/Chrome banners
text: parseToolVersion() extracts 'ffmpeg 7.1.1-essentials_build' or 'ffmpeg n8.0.1-66-g...' from banner. extractMajorVersion() reads first X.Y number (supports 'n' prefix for release branches). Works for FFmpeg, FFprobe, Chrome, HeadlessShell.
how: Use in preflight.py to parse version strings from our bundled ffmpeg/chrome; enforce minimum versions (e.g., FFmpeg ≥7, Chrome ≥119) for feature compatibility (10-bit HEVC, BeginFrame).

title: Animation cataloging for GSAP recreation (Web Animations, CSS, scroll triggers)
text: collectAnimationCatalog() captures: 1) document.getAnimations() with keyframes/timing, 2) CSS animation/transition declarations via getComputedStyle (up to 5000 elements), 3) IntersectionObserver targets (scroll-triggered elements), 4) CDP Animation.domain events. Returns structured catalog with summary counts. Includes budgeted scroll and evaluate with timeout degradation flag.
how: Add a capture step in scout.py or research.py when analyzing reference sites; feed catalog into plan.py to recreate animations in lab-look GSAP components (stat counters, line charts, flows).

title: Asset cataloging with rich DOM context (alt, heading, banner, home-link signals)
text: catalogAssets() extracts every referenced asset (img, video, font, icon, background, meta og:image, CSS url()) and records: contexts (img[src], css url(), etc.), alt/aria-label/figcaption, nearest heading (h1-h4), section classes, above-fold boolean, inBanner (header/nav/[role=banner]), inHomeLink (anchor to '/' or origin), matchesTitleBrand (brand segment in alt). Deduplicates Next.js image variants keeping highest w=.
how: Integrate into research.py when scraping reference pages; use banner/home-link/brand-match signals to auto-select hero images/logo for thumbnails and lab-look hero shots.

title: Robust unzip with disk-full detection, cancellation, and no-unzip fallback
text: unzipArchive() runs unzip -q -o with input closed (prevents hang on 'Continue? (y/n)' when disk full). Detects exit code 50 → throws actionable error. Runs in caller's process group so SIGINT/SIGTERM cancels it. Returns false if unzip binary missing (caller uses JS fallback). Creates parent dirs, leaves no empty folder on failure.
how: Replace any archive extraction in our asset download pipeline (Muse, FLUX outputs) with this logic; ensures failed downloads don't leave corrupt caches and respect doctor.py cancellation tokens.

title: Deterministic SVG Standalone Conversion
text: toStandaloneSvg adds xmlns and xmlns:xlink (only when xlink:href used) to inline SVG outerHTML. Idempotent, preserves all root attributes (class, width, height, fill). Hash-based filenames (sha1 8-char) prevent content drift. Logos get logo- prefix.
how: Use toStandaloneSvg for any inline SVG we capture (logos, icons); name files by content hash; store in assets/svgs/ for reuse in lab-look compositions.

title: SSRF-Safe Fetch with Redirect Re-validation
text: safeFetch() manually follows redirects (max 5 hops) and re-runs isPrivateUrl() on every Location header before fetching. Blocks metadata hosts (169.254.169.254), private IPv4/IPv6, localhost aliases, and non-http(s) schemes. Cancels redirect response bodies before validating next hop.
how: Replace our current fetch in assetDownloader with safeFetch pattern; add isPrivateUrl denylist covering cloud metadata, RFC1918, link-local, ULA, and internal DNS suffixes (.internal, .local).

title: Asset Drop Reason Telemetry
text: Every dropped asset increments one of five counters: size-floor (<10KB raster, <50B SVG), size-ceiling (>2MB SVG), budget-exhausted (time/byte budget), cap-reached (30 fonts, 6/family, 30 inline SVGs, 8 icons), unavailable (network/write failure). Counts are exact per drop site — no double-counting.
how: Add AssetDropCounts to our downloadAssets/downloadAndRewriteFonts returns; surface in doctor.py and dashboard so we know if captures are thin due to limits vs failures.

title: Icon Classification & Bare-Mark Promotion
text: Downloads all declared icons (up to 8), classifies each as bare-mark / badge / unknown via SVG shape analysis (knocked-out mark vs full-bleed). Headline favicon chosen by shape preference (bare-mark > unknown=badge) then declared rank. Manifest records reason (e.g., 'bare mark preferred over 2 badges').
how: In thumb.py/asset download, fetch all <link rel=icon/apple-touch-icon>, classify with iconClassifier, promote best to assets/favicon.<ext> for brand strip; keep all icons in manifest for debugging.

title: Shared Byte/Time Budget Across Asset Types
text: createCaptureDownloadBudget() creates a byteBudget with remainingBytes. Passed to font, icon, image, and OG downloads. Each fetch decrements budget; fetchBuffer returns null when exhausted. Time budget via remainingMs() callback shared across phases.
how: Create single DownloadByteBudget in captureAttempt; pass to downloadAssets, downloadAndRewriteFonts, downloadDeclaredIcons; add remainingMs() from postNavigationDeadline.

title: Symlink Planting Protection
text: ensureCaptureDirSync refuses to create/write through symlinks pointing outside capture directory. Tests cover planted assets/, assets/svgs/, and dangling symlinks. Throws CaptureDirRefusedError before any browser launch.
how: Add symlink check in ensureCaptureDirSync (used by compose.py, thumb.py, capture): resolve target, ensure it's under outputDir; refuse with clear error.

title: WebGL Shader Capture for Effect Recreation
text: Injects evaluateOnNewDocument hook on HTMLCanvasElement.getContext to intercept shaderSource calls. Captures vertex/fragment GLSL source (truncated to 5000 chars) into window.__capturedShaders. Enables Claude Code to recreate visual effects from captured shaders.
how: Add shader capture hook in launchCaptureBrowser; save shaders.json to extracted/; include in project scaffold for reference when building lab-look scenes.

title: Late Resource Waiting Beyond Settle Cap
text: openSettledCompositionPage waits for images/fetches that arrive after DOMContentLoaded and default 1.5s settle cap. Uses lateSubresourceTimeoutMs (default 60s) to wait for all network idle. Test shows 3s late image and 500ms late fetch both awaited before render.
how: In captureCompositionFrame, add lateSubresourceTimeoutMs option; wait for page network idle (no pending fetches/images) before marking renderReady; use in our HyperFrames render for reliable frames.

title: Tiered seek-settle profiles
text: Three settle profiles per capture pass: AUDIT = double rAF + 500 ms font wait; SCREENSHOT = AUDIT + 3 s image-decode wait; DENSE_GEOMETRY = no rAF/font/sleep, no video-frame hold, WebGL draws skipped. Measured: 600 dense seeks x ~185 ms of video-frame waiting pushed a 79 s 1080p project past its deadline. Geometry is valid synchronously after setTime.
how: In preflight.py, split the audit into a fast geometry sweep (no waits) and a per-scene still pass (double rAF + 500 ms font + 3 s image decode). Cap the dense pass near 600 samples and log per-pass wall time so doctor.py can flag a slow audit.

title: Runtime-ready gate before sampling
text: Before any layout, motion or validate sample, wait for the runtime's __renderReady flag (or __hfStartupError) with a timeout. If __hfStartupError is a string, fail loudly with that message instead of reporting 'ready'. A timeout is a warning, not a pass: the capture may be mid-animation, so flag the frame as unverified rather than clean.
how: In preflight.py, poll window.__renderReady after page load; on timeout mark the scene 'unverified' in the report, on startup error abort the run with the error text. Use the same gate before review.py samples frames.

title: Selector-to-crop resolution for zoomed diagnostics
text: Resolve a CSS selector to its live bounding box, pad 24 px on every side, then clamp to the canvas; explicit 'x,y,w,h' regions are used exactly (clamped only, never padded). A selector matching nothing is a loud error, not a silent full-frame fallback. If the clamped region is under 8 px on either axis (element animated off-canvas), return null and skip the frame. Capture at deviceScaleFactor 3 for density without CSS zoom.
how: When Gemini flags a scene in preflight.py, capture a 3x DSF crop of the offending element (selector or region) and attach it to the Telegram approval card, so the editor sees the exact defect instead of the full frame.

title: Visible-layer image decode enumeration
text: Before a screenshot, enumerate every visible image layer: currentSrc, SVG href, and CSS background-image url(), skipping display:none / visibility:hidden elements. Then await image.decode() with a 3 s cap and return the pending and failed source lists, so a blank frame is attributed to a specific asset instead of guessed.
how: In preflight.py's still pass, run this enumeration after each seek; if any source is pending or failed, log the URL with the scene id and re-fetch through our provider ladder before Gemini judges the frame.

title: Byte-based asset validation
text: Determine image type from bytes, never the URL suffix: check magic signatures, then decode with a 40 M decoded-pixel cap and a 10 MB / 40 M aggregate cap for embedded rasters. Reject SVGs containing script, foreignObject, on* handlers, external href/@import/url() references, or DOCTYPE/ENTITY. Truncated or mislabelled files fail before reaching a composition.
how: Add a validation step to our asset ingestion (Muse / FLUX / Pollinations downloads) before files enter the render cache: decode-check each image, cap dimensions, drop failures, so preflight never renders a broken or blank frame.

title: Stage budget with typed timeout errors
text: Cap every seek settle at protocolTimeout - 10 s (180 s default, so 170 s) so a stuck seek can never consume the whole protocol budget. Wrap each stage in a remaining-budget race that rejects with a typed StageBudgetTimeoutError naming the stage. Classify navigation timeouts separately from Runtime.evaluate timeouts, because they need different retry and fallback decisions.
how: In doctor.py/preflight.py, give each stage (load, seek, sample, judge) its own remaining budget; on StageBudgetTimeoutError mark that scene failed and continue, on navigation timeout retry once with a longer navigation timeout.

title: Disable thinking on vision calls
text: Thinking tokens are drawn from maxOutputTokens, so a thinking-capable model can consume the whole budget and return empty text while the request 'succeeds'. Set thinkingBudget 0 (Vertex) / thinking off for Gemini image judging and research summarisation, and treat an empty caption as a failure: retry once with thinking off, then mark the scene for manual review.
how: Add thinkingBudget: 0 to the Gemini generateContent config in preflight.py and research.py; after each response, if text is empty or whitespace, count it as a failed judgement so the existing bad-scene rewrite path handles that scene instead of silently passing it.

title: Read assets through an open fd with a 4 MB inline cap
text: Vision APIs reject large inline payloads. Open the asset, fstat the descriptor, read the bytes from that same descriptor (closing the stat-then-read race so a replaced file cannot be sent), and only send when size <= 4,000,000 bytes; larger assets are skipped with a warning, not a batch failure. Test both 4,000,000 and 4,000,001 bytes.
how: In preflight.py's still-judging loop, read each still via an open fd, check the byte count against 4,000,000, and downscale oversized stills (e.g. 1080 px JPEG q80) before sending; skip anything still too large and log the skip count.

title: Assert rendered title pixels, not just file format
text: A PNG/JPEG can be the right format and still contain no text: a misconfigured font stack makes SVG label overlays draw nothing while the file writes fine. Verify the text actually rasterised by counting non-background pixels inside the label/title band (anything other than #1a1a1a in the 26 px band) and fail if the count is zero.
how: In thumb.py and preflight.py, after writing the cover, count non-background pixels in the hook-title region and fail the render if zero; this catches a missing font before the thumbnail reaches Telegram approval.

title: Browser-ready capture deadline watchdog
text: A capture watchdog whose clock starts only when the browser is registered, so a first-run Chrome download is not counted against the deadline. On expiry it closes the browser and resolves a typed 'deadline' outcome; the losing attempt's promise always gets a rejection handler so a late browser-close error never becomes an unhandled rejection. Default budget 240,000 ms; zero, decimal or malformed env values are ignored.
how: In our render wrapper (doctor.py / HyperFrames launch), arm a 4-minute deadline only after Chrome is up; on expiry close the browser and mark the run 'deadline' rather than a generic failure, and always attach a .catch to the abandoned render promise so the worker survives late rejections.

title: Labeled contact sheet for whole-video stills review
text: Instead of sending N scene stills to a vision model, stitch them into a labeled grid: 3 columns, 9 cells per page, 600 px cell width, 26 px label band, labels like '3. 4.2s', EXIF auto-orient per image, contain-fit on #1a1a1a, and a remaining-time budget checked before each page so a long sheet stops cleanly. One sheet per page cuts image tokens roughly 50-65%.
how: In preflight.py, build contact sheets of the per-scene stills (label = scene index + timecode) and send each page to Gemini for a whole-video consistency pass; keep individual stills for scenes Gemini flags. Write sheets atomically and skip a page if the preflight time budget is exhausted.

title: Hard timeout race around vision calls
text: An AbortSignal alone is not enough: some SDKs ignore it. Race every vision request against a timer (20 ms in tests, 30-60 s in production) so a hung provider can never stall the pipeline. Isolate each asset in its own try/catch so one failure keeps the successful siblings, and emit warnings containing neither the API key nor the local file path.
how: Wrap every Gemini call in research.py and preflight.py with Promise.race([request, timer]) plus an AbortController; on timeout return a typed 'request-timeout' outcome, keep other scenes' results, and log only counts (timed out / failed / budget exhausted) to the run log.

title: Grade-group propagation check by pixel sampling
text: A grade applied to a group must repaint every member clip, not just the first. Test it cheaply: render N members (50 in the source), sample the centre pixel of each member's canvas before and after editing the group's grading attribute, and require every member to cross the threshold (e.g. red >150 before, <70 after) with zero page errors.
how: Add a preflight check in compose_lab.py's audit: after applying a colour group, sample one pixel per member frame and fail the scene if any member is unchanged; log which member failed so the grade group is corrected before render.

title: Baked-grade vs runtime parity test
text: If grades are baked (LUT/.cube) and also applied live, the two paths must agree. Render a 16-step RGB lattice (8x8 tiles, 64 per row) through the live runtime and compare each tile centre with the baked cube: require max channel difference <= 2 codes, mean difference < 0.1, and that the grade moved codes by > 20 so an ungraded draw cannot pass.
how: Add a test in our repo that renders our lab-look grade through the browser runtime and compares it with the baked LUT we ship; run it in CI so a grading change cannot silently shift the look between preview and final render.

title: Asset description priority: video > captioned images > uncaptioned > SVGs > fonts
text: Generate asset-descriptions.md with video clips first (tagged [video] with dims), then Gemini-captioned images, then uncaptioned images with catalog metadata (heading, section, above-fold), then SVGs (caption or label), then fonts. Video manifest carries DOM heading/caption + dimensions.
how: In preflight.py asset audit, sort available assets by this priority. Feed top-N to Gemini for visual planning. Ensures motion clips and captioned hero images drive composition decisions.

title: SVG rasterization before vision captioning
text: Vision models hallucinate wordmarks from raw SVG paths. Rasterize SVGs to 256px PNG with contrasting background (dark slate for light glyphs, white for dark) before sending to vision API. Process SVGs serially (sharp.concurrency=1) to avoid libvips heap corruption, then caption in parallel batches.
how: In compose_lab.py asset prep, add SVG→PNG rasterization step before any vision call. Use sharp with background fill based on fill-color analysis. Set sharp.concurrency(1) during rasterization batch, restore after.

title: Library detection via globals, DOM, scripts, and shaders
text: Detect animation/3D libraries (GSAP, Three.js, Framer Motion, etc.) from four signals: window globals, DOM fingerprints (canvas data-engine, component tags), script src patterns, and WebGL shader uniforms (modelViewMatrix→Three.js, vTextureCoord→PixiJS, viewProjection→Babylon). Deduplicate results.
how: Add to scout.py when analyzing reference sites. Run page.evaluate in headless Chrome to collect all four signal types. Store detected libs in brain.jsonl for style reference.

title: Clean visible text extraction with TreeWalker
text: Extract all visible text in DOM order using TreeWalker (NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT). Filter: skip <script>/<style>/<noscript>, hidden elements (display:none, visibility:hidden, opacity:0), cookie/consent banners via regex, nav/footer text <8 chars. Truncate to 30k chars.
how: Add extractVisibleText() to research.py for competitor page analysis. Use same filtering rules. Feed clean text to Gemini for hook/structure analysis instead of raw HTML.

title: Comprehensive design token extraction
text: Extract computed styles for 9 categories: typography (8 roles, dedup by fontSize+weight+family), buttons (filled CTAs in nav kept, dedup by visual appearance), cards, nav, chips, stat cells (numeral ≥28px), tabs, spacing scale (GCD base unit 4/8), radius, shadows (semantic+utility, area-filtered), gradients (chroma-weighted area), glass panels (backdrop-filter blur, raw fill with alpha).
how: Create designTokenExtractor.ts for reference site capture. Run in headless Chrome during scout. Output JSON matching DesignTokens type. Use in compose_lab.py for auto-styling panels/charts to match reference brand.

title: Preserve stylesheet cascade order when inlining
text: When inlining external stylesheets, fetch each in DOM order, replace its <link> with <style> at the same position, preserving media attribute. Later inline styles override earlier sheets; repeated links are fetched each time. Relative url() in CSS are rewritten absolute against the sheet's href. Failed fetches leave the link intact.
how: In preflight.py layout audit, capture reference sites with this cascade-preserving extraction. Store extracted headHtml in brain.jsonl for design-token mining.

title: Capture retry with WebGL disable on navigation stall
text: If navigation times out AND WebGL was observed (context loss), retry once with --disable-gpu (no --enable-webgl, no --use-angle). If stall without WebGL or second attempt fails, abort. Carries degradation warning into result. Watchdog enforces 4-min total deadline, then writes partial capture bundle (extracted HTML, screenshots, tokens, assets).
how: In doctor.py self-repair: when render worker hangs on WebGL-heavy scene (Three.js, shaders), retry once with --disable-gpu flag. Log degradation in brain.jsonl for future scene simplification.

title: Asset download with relative URL rewriting and entity decoding
text: After inlining stylesheets, rewrite all url() in
how: In assetDownloader.ts, apply same rewriting to downloaded CSS before saving. Fixes broken relative paths in Muse/FLUX generated assets. Use in thumb.py for cover images.

title: Icon font detection via glyph coverage not name
text: Detect icon fonts by glyph set: must lack basic Latin alphabet (<26 of A-Za-z) AND have >50% glyphs in Unicode Private Use Area (U+E000–U+F8FF or U+F0000–U+10FFFD). Prevents misclassifying SF Pro (81% PUA but full alphabet) or Booton (50% PUA, full alphabet) as icon fonts. Measured: Font Awesome 95% PUA/0 letters, custom 'hushly' 63% PUA/7 letters.
how: In fontMetadataExtractor.ts, use isIconCharacterSet(font.characterSet) to set isIcon flag. In compose_lab.py, exclude isIcon fonts from kinetic title/caption font selection.

title: Font metadata extraction with family canonicalization
text: Use fontkit to read OpenType name tables from downloaded .woff2/.ttf files; canonicalize family names by stripping trailing weight tokens (e.g., 'Inter Medium' → 'Inter' + weight 500) and detect icon fonts via glyph coverage (<26 Latin letters AND >50% PUA glyphs). Outputs fonts-manifest.json with per-file metadata and per-family aggregation.
how: Add to assetDownloader.ts after font download: run fontkit on each file, write manifest to extracted/fonts-manifest.json. Feed canonical families into DESIGN.md font allowlist and preflight.py font-gate.

title: Lazy scroll with budget and image-wait for long pages
text: Scroll in 70% viewport steps (400ms delay), stop at bottom or budget (default 20s). After reaching bottom, wait up to 5s for pending images (poll every 250ms), then scroll to top. On evaluate timeout, degrade gracefully: warn, attempt scroll-to-top recovery, return degraded=true. No unbounded waits.
how: Add to captureAttempt.ts for reference-site capture of long articles. Also use in review.py to auto-scroll rendered HyperFrames compositions for full-frame vision review.

title: Local page server with security isolation for capture
text: Serve local files for capture via loopback server: blocks private files (.env, .git, .aws, .hyperframes), refuses service-worker script requests (403), validates Host header (only allows server's own port), resolves symlinks only within root, sets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Asset downloader reads directly from this origin bypassing system proxy.
how: Adopt for local composition preview in doctor.py and Telegram approvals: startLocalPageServer(compositionDir) with same security, use in publish.py for Instagram/Facebook preview renders.

title: Preview rendering size gate
text: Skip preview/thumbnail generation for source assets >2 MB to avoid CDP message limits and OOM. Source enforces this for Lottie previews (fileSize <= 2_000_000).
how: In thumb.py and preflight.py, add size check before headless render: if asset > 2 MB, log warning, skip preview, use placeholder. Adjust threshold for video/image previews.

title: Private URL blocking in headless preview pages
text: Intercept all requests in headless preview/thumbnail pages and block private IPs (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, ::1, file://, local networks). Source's guardLottiePreviewRequests allows only pinned runtime, images, fonts, stylesheets.
how: In thumb.py/preview render, add CDP request interception: abort any request to private URL per isPrivateUrl list. Reuse existing SSRF-safe fetch denylist.

title: Content-addressed asset deduplication
text: Before saving any generated asset (image, video, audio), compute SHA-256; if hash exists in asset store, reuse existing file. Source deduplicates Lottie animations by content hash (savedHashes Set).
how: Extend content-addressed project uploads to individual assets: in mix.py/thumb.py/publish.py, hash output bytes, check asset store (e.g., assets/.hashes/), symlink or copy existing. Saves disk and upload bandwidth.

title: Byte budget for external asset downloads
text: Shared byte budget across all external downloads (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations) with hard cap enforced while streaming; abort if exceeded. Source's DownloadByteBudget and readBoundedResponse cap at 75 MB/video, 10 MB/Lottie, 5 MB/discovery.
how: Create global DownloadByteBudget in doctor.py or config; pass to asset downloaders (Muse, FLUX, Pollinations). In download helpers, stream with chunk accumulation, abort if total > budget. Reset per render job.

title: Blocked page detection heuristics
text: Flag protection pages using: minimal DOM (≤5 body children, <500 text chars) AND (challenge element present OR HTTP 401/403/429 OR title matches blocked patterns: 403/forbidden/access denied/attention required/just a moment + optional Cloudflare/Sucuri suffix). Allows image-led pages and real content discussing blocks.
how: In scout.py after fetching a URL, run detectBlockedPage() on response (status, title, textLength, bodyChildCount, hasChallengeElement). If blocked, skip extraction and log actionable warning: retry from allowed network or provide assets directly.

title: CSS fixed/sticky neutralization for full-page screenshots
text: Before full-page screenshot, temporarily override position:fixed/sticky (including !important) to static via inline style with data-hf-plate attribute, capture, then restore original computed style and priority. Handles stylesheet and inline declarations.
how: In preflight.py or review.py when capturing full-page stills, inject evaluate() script that finds fixed/sticky elements, stores original style, sets position:static!important, screenshots, then restores. Wrap in try/finally.

title: Navigation fallback with proxy error explanation
